Sports.title: The clubs who could seek compensation as Premier League sides consider legal action after Man City found guilty of vast majority of rule breaches - and what happens next: Key questions answered
Sports.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their rule-break charges concerning the Premier League’s financial regulations.

The competition accused the club of widespread financial cheating over an era of sustained success – with an independent panel hearing concluding in 2024.

The long-awaited verdict has now been reached with the belief it is a victory for the Premier League, despite Man City having strenuously denied the charges.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation.

Daily Mail Sport's Mike Keegan provides answers to the key questions, including the next steps, Man City's expected appeal and how serious the punishment could be.

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 Premier League rule-break charges

WHAT DOES IT MEAN?

This cannot be viewed as anything other than an overwhelming victory for the Premier League.

To see Manchester City found guilty of the ‘vast majority’ of the 115 charges is an outcome that Richard Masters will no doubt see as vindication for what has been a costly, long-running legal battle in which the stakes were incredibly high.

It is safe to assume that had the tables turned the other way, the chief executive would have been in P45 territory.

More important than that, those who City feel were the key protagonists, the so-called ‘Red Cartel’, will also feel vindication.

To put it simply, Manchester City have been found guilty of cheating their way to success between 2009 and 2018, a period when they dominated English football.

The verdict cannot be viewed as anything other than an overwhelming victory for the Premier League and its chief executive Richard Masters

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

There has been no statement from the Premier League, while City’s only says that the process remains ongoing and is subject to strict confidentiality.

What is clear is that City will appeal. What is not clear is whether the sanction will drop before any appeal.

WHAT ARE THE PUNISHMENTS?

Take your pick. Hefty points deductions, potential relegation and transfer bans are all on the table. Rule W51 in the Premier League handbook states ambiguously that ‘such other penalty as it shall think fit’ is an option.

There is, however, a scepticism among some, based on a lack of noise from many of the other clubs and the lenient punishment recently handed to Chelsea that whatever penalty lands will not see City stripped of titles or relegated. ‘They’ll get a slap on the wrist and ordered to pay legal costs and not much else,’ one exec predicted.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation

HOW DOES AN APPEAL WORK?

In all likelihood City will appeal and recent cases tell us that they tend to be dealt with expeditiously.

An appeal board would be set up, appointed by the chair of the panel and, again, featuring three people. Some feel that this would be an exercise in the Premier League marking its own homework.

At this early stage, it is worth an assumption that City could argue the panel was not impartial. The bad news for them, however, is that this is a high bar to clear.

Unlike City’s case with UEFA, it cannot go to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (who overturned UEFA’s findings).

WHAT ABOUT COMPENSATION?

Last year, in a move believed to have been instigated by former Arsenal chief executive Tim Lewis, the Gunners, Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Manchester United served legal notices reserving their right to take action.

Should the verdict stand, they will then seek damages for a wide variety of issues. The most costly claims are likely to come from those who say they missed out on Champions League qualification during the period in question thanks to City’s law breaking. But the scope would not end there.

Clubs could also, for example, argue that as a result of the breaches they were unable to sign a calibre of player that would have allowed them to be more successful on the field. Some believe £200m would not be out of the question, but that remains to be seen.

Ex-Arsenal chief executive is understood to have instigated a move last year that saw the Gunners, Tottenham, Liverpool and Man United served legal notices reserving their right to take action

WHAT ABOUT THE INDEPENDENT FOOTBALL REGULATOR?

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the Regulator declined to comment when contacted by Daily Mail Sport. However, David Kogan will be well aware of the situation.

The IFR was brought in for a variety of reasons, not least to ensure that those owning the nation’s football clubs were fit and proper to do so. The IFR would have the power to force City’s owners to sell, but such a scenario is viewed as unlikely.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

The Premier League and City are not commenting.

Given the verdict is in, the two parties will enter into a period of negotiation with regards to when the detail will be released. That will also include suggested redactions, as both sides go through what is likely to be a finding that may well run into the hundreds of pages.

DIDN’T CITY TRIUMPH OVER THE PREMIER LEAGUE RECENTLY ON SPONSORSHIP RULES?

They did, with three senior judges deeming the rules unlawful. As a result, a series of amendments were made. City again launched a legal challenge, but surprisingly came to an agreement with the Premier League in September. Those cases, however, were always separate to the 115, as it became known.

Sports.title: Inside Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa struggles: The doubt over who really signed him from Chelsea, ominous signs behind the scenes that won't please Unai Emery - and how Argentine can still win him over
Sports.content:
Inside Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa struggles: The doubt over who really signed him from Chelsea, ominous signs behind the scenes that won't please Unai Emery - and how Argentine can still win him over

Surely it cannot be happening again. Aston Villa have already spent one season paying a substantial salary to a loan player they did not want. Would they really repeat that mistake?

‘Harvey Elliott’ is the name people remember when they look at Alejandro Garnacho’s situation at Villa Park. The same terms – loan with a conditional obligation to buy – and the same lack of playing time.

By last autumn, Unai Emery had decided he did not wish to sign Elliott permanently and therefore, under the terms of his loan agreement, he was able to make just nine appearances across that campaign before going back to Liverpool.

At that stage of his Villa career, Elliott had played 118 minutes, even though he joined the club only at the end of the summer 2025 transfer window. Garnacho arrived at Villa Park and has featured for only 31 so far.

The £43million transfer next summer, as detailed in the loan arrangement with Chelsea and which will happen if certain targets are hit, is already looking unlikely.

There is still plenty of time for Garnacho to alter the course of this story. Villa play two friendlies during the break, one of which is against Sevilla in Spain on October 2. Garnacho owes it to himself to attack this training camp with all his heart. The rest of his time at Villa may depend on it.

Alejandro Garnacho has had a miserable start to life at Aston Villa, featuring for just 31 minutes so far this season

‘We are delighted with Alejandro,’ said Unai Emery at Garnacho's unveiling. ‘He is so talented.' But that positivity already feels like ancient history

Why Garnacho?

Not long after the final whistle in Aston Villa's 3-1 win at Coventry on September 16, Garnacho was heading out of the CBS Arena and en route to the Villa team bus. With Emery making changes for the Carabao Cup clash, many had expected Garnacho to start. He did not even make it on to the pitch.

Any player would be disappointed in that situation, especially one with nearly 200 senior appearances and eight caps for Argentina before the age of 23. It is also understood there were no compulsory post-match exercises as the players were due to train the following morning.

Generally, though, constant application is the route to Emery’s heart as the Spaniard demands ‘serious, mature, responsible’ players.

Emery may not be pitchside after matches but nothing escapes him.

His backroom team will tell him exactly what happened during the post-match running drills: which exercises were performed, which players gave their all, which – if any – were slacking off.

Garnacho was left on the bench at Tottenham three days later, too, and may not even have made the squad had Brazilian winger Alysson been fit.

The attraction of Garnacho is obvious. Even though he struggled at Chelsea last season, between 2023-25 he scored 21 goals and had 17 assists for Manchester United. Emery has wanted an incisive wide attacker ever since he came to Villa and on the face of it, Garnacho ticked the boxes.

Yet the nagging doubt remains: was Emery truly desperate to sign him, the way he was desperate to bring in Morgan Rogers in January 2024, or Marco Asensio on loan a year later, or Nicolas Jackson this summer?

If Emery were, it seems surprising that he would then promote academy prospect George Hemmings above Garnacho and sign off on the £50m deal for Ibrahim Mbaye, who can play on either flank. Not to mention his early-season backing for Alysson.

Not long after the final whistle in Aston Villa's 3-1 win at Coventry on September 16, Garnacho (pictured the week before) was heading out of the CBS Arena and en route to the Villa team bus

Garnacho stayed in his tracksuit at Tottenham three days later, too, and may not even have made the squad had Brazilian winger Alysson been fit

Villa co-owner Nassef Sawiris and Chelsea counterpart Behdad Eghbali are also thought to enjoy good relations though Emery laughed off suggestions last month that the two clubs, both on the naughty step with UEFA for breaching financial rules, would ever help each other.

‘They want to kill us, and we want to kill them,’ he said. ‘They signed Morgan and Emiliano Martinez to kill us.’

The facts are these: Garnacho joined Villa from Chelsea on July 23, two days after Rogers had moved in the opposite direction for a record £117m. Chelsea and Villa traded four players this summer alone, with Martinez moving to Stamford Bridge along with Rogers, and Jackson joining Garnacho in the West Midlands. Set-piece coach Austin MacPhee swapped Villa for Chelsea, too.

Clubs can deal with one another as they see fit but unless Garnacho starts to play regularly, we will always wonder about the exact circumstances that led him to Villa.

Can Garnacho turn it around?

After Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho, Garnacho is the third player to lose his way at United and turn up at Villa on loan not long afterwards.

The spell at Villa Park in the second half of 2024-25 revived Rashford’s career. Though he could not help Villa qualify for the Champions League, he did enough under Emery to earn a year’s loan at Barcelona and make the England squad for the World Cup. Rashford is now playing for United again, which seemed impossible only a year ago.

On the flipside, Sancho started only nine Premier League games for Villa and is now without a club after leaving Old Trafford last summer. Reports in Russia this week said the 26-year-old was in discussions with top-flight club Krasnodar. Emery had really wanted Rashford; Sancho not so much.

Whose path will Garnacho follow? Playing for Emery can be exhausting but there are still relatively painless ways to impress him.

Emery has already ticked off Garnacho for dawdling on the touchline when preparing to come on

The Villa boss reignited Marcus Rashford's career after he fell out of favour at Man United. Can he do the same for Garnacho?

Lucas Digne, for example, won his boss over partly by turning up for extra sessions on his days off. ‘Continue working,’ said Emery when asked how Garnacho can force his way into the team. ‘Work, work, train, work.’

There is another simple rule with Emery: a player can catch the eye as much he likes on the ball but if he does not follow instructions when Villa do not have possession, he will not play very often.

Emery has already ticked off Garnacho for dawdling on the touchline when preparing to come on and has admitted Garnacho could have done better in his early appearances. These are not good signs.

Listening actively in meetings, both individual and collective, is also key. Emery will explain in painstaking detail what he wants from a player. If he does not deliver it, woe betide him.

Emery will not tailor his approach to young people with short attention spans. It’s his immersive way – repetitive training sessions, 90-minute video briefings, detailed tactical breakdowns – or nothing. With 12 major trophies to his name, why should he change?

After significant turnover this summer, Emery is relying even more on a cohort of senior players who have been at Villa throughout his time – John McGinn, Matty Cash, Tyrone Mings, Emi Buendia. They emphasise to new signings exactly what is needed to succeed at the club.

The smart ones listen and learn. There is no suggestion that Garnacho, a shy, quiet individual, is disruptive but clearly he is not doing enough to convince Emery and right now few at Bodymoor Heath can see a path to regular first-team football.

There is mitigation: Garnacho suffered a nasty facial injury during a pre-season fixture against Thai club BG Pathum United, which slowed his progress and meant he did not feature in the UEFA Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain. Playing on the wing for Emery is also the most tactically demanding role on the pitch and very few master it immediately.

Daily Mail Sport understands Garnacho scored the only goal in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Southampton yesterday. That won't do his cause any harm.

Garnacho’s career is still in his own hands – though Sancho’s tale should be fresh in his mind.

There is no suggestion that Garnacho is disruptive but clearly he is not doing enough and right now few at Bodymoor Heath can see a path to regular first-team football

How does the story end?

Watch Garnacho’s first interview at Villa and you will see a player who has lost his way and is fighting to regain it.

‘We are delighted with Alejandro,’ said Emery at the time. ‘He is so talented, young and he showed us his wish to help our project. We are really happy.’

Emery has seen what Garnacho can do. Cash was one of Villa’s best players last season yet when Chelsea hammered them 4-1 at Villa Park, Garnacho gave the right back a chasing. It was a reminder of what he offered during his best spells at United.

‘I was looking for a club to get confidence and to try to be the player I was in my first years at United,’ said Garnacho on the day he joined Villa. ‘I spoke with the manager and I think he will give me the confidence to be here and to help the team.’ Emery and Garnacho were filmed embracing during the video.

Since he crossed swords with former United boss Ruben Amorim, there has been far more focus on Garnacho’s mistakes than his talent – and this is partly his fault. He still has immense raw ability and Emery is exactly the type of coach who can unlock it, as long as they can find a common understanding.

Time is already running out. Daily Mail Sport revealed on September 21 that La Liga clubs are already following the situation, should the loan be cancelled in January. If that happens, it would feel like a huge missed opportunity, for Villa, Emery and most of all Garnacho himself. The ball is in his court.

Sports.title: RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: 'Not bothered' Cole Palmer may be too cool for school but here's why he should follow Harry Kane's example - and how he may have blown it with detail-obsessed Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Here's a niche question for British readers: have you heard of Chase McLaughlin or Evan McPherson? What about Harrison Butker, Trey Smack or Jason Myers? One version of the answer is that they’re who Harry Kane wishes to be when he grows up.

A little more detail is probably necessary here, because with the exception of Myers, they’re in the top four for field goals in the early weeks of the NFL season.

I’ve thrown Myers in there for a simple reason – his team is the Seattle Seahawks and that means he is the most recent kicker to win a Super Bowl. Of Seattle’s 29 points against the New England Patriots in that match, Myers kicked 17, including five field goals – a record.

But he wasn’t named MVP. That isn’t the kicker’s place in the American Football food chain – only three specialist kickers exist among the 387 players in the NFL hall of fame. They’re dedicated and well-paid as game-changers, but their life is one for the shadows.

Across his 12 years in the NFL, it is estimated Myers has spent around three hours on the pitch and 170 hours waiting for his six-second cameos on the sidelines, not counting the ad breaks.

So who dreams of being a Myers? Kane does. And as he said this week, he has spent time mapping out how that pathway to kicking could work, comprising a strategically placed spell in Major League Soccer and up to a year of graft to understand a different ball. Only then might he put himself forward for consideration.

The kicker’s union might see arrogance in that; I see humility, because we know what kind of person Kane is. We also know that voting closes on the Ballon d’Or next week and if there’s any sense left in football, Kane will win it, the main character of the main game, but a man who will always see himself as a cog. As one of the guys. Never above anything; not too big to kick his heels between kicking balls.

All of which is a very long way of asking: why can’t Cole Palmer be more like Harry Kane?

Cole Palmer has started the season impressively - but will he regret turning his back on England for this international break

Why can’t Palmer be more like Harry Kane? A man who, despite his talent and records, will always see himself as a cog

I love Palmer as a player, because who doesn’t? I like him as a person, too, or as much any of us can without knowing him up close.

His irreverence is part of his charm and brand – he trademarked the Cold Palmer schtick. Too cold to buckle under pressure, too cool for school, and no one’s idea of a malign influence.

But you have to wonder if he committed a significant cock-up by withdrawing from the current England camp.

We should take Palmer at his word that he’s legitimately injured, with that being a muscular issue, but there’s no one I’ve spoken to in or around Chelsea who see it as anything serious.

It’s said to be minor and most would expect him to start against Bournemouth on Chelsea’s resumption of Premier League fixtures on October 10, just as he started against Fulham, Brighton, Arsenal, Hull and Brentford in the last game before the break. Luton in the Carabao Cup? He started that one as well and scored a couple off the bench against Leeds.

Palmer’s early-season form has been excellent and so has his availability – he played all but 52 minutes of Chelsea’s fixtures to date. Had he shown the same last season, Thomas Tuchel surely would have taken him to the World Cup.

One instinct is to say it’s unfortunate that a niggle nudged Palmer off the wave just as he was recalled for England. Another is to query if he lacks a little sense. A little humility. Because why wouldn’t he go with the squad anyway? Why not show face as a non-playing member of the group, even if it was only for a few days?

That might seem trivial but it isn’t. This fortnight counts for half of the time Tuchel has across the entirety of the season and the first gathering since the World Cup. It’s the get-together that spelled out how they will move on from that semi-final, how this next chapter must be committed to finding leaders who don’t retreat under pressure.

For Thomas Tuchel, this camp was always going to be about knowing who is with him, who is invested, who can be relied upon and who, crucially, buys into his demand for ‘brotherhood’

For Tuchel, this one was always going to be about knowing who is with him, who is invested, who can be relied upon and who, crucially, buys into his demand for ‘brotherhood’.

In short, it’s a room you desperately want to be in if you have a point to prove to Tuchel, because he watches everything. And not just the football.

I remember writing in this space two years ago about the kind of details he studies – he looks to see who leaves a dirty plate for the dinner crew to clear away after lunch. He watches to see who skims the corner on a recovery run and who is too big to have a respectful chat with lower-ranking members of staff. It irritates and consumes him.

This was all spelled out in a surreal video he filmed alongside an Indian health guru, shortly after his sacking from Chelsea, when he was explaining how exhausting it is to be Thomas Tuchel.

If any player saw the clip, let alone those who have worked with the man, they would know these little details never escape his glare and he applies meaning to it all, disproportionate or otherwise. That’s his way.

When Jude Bellingham was thrown into exile, we know it wasn’t about his touch or vision. And we can reasonably guess, also, that when Palmer gave an interview in pre-season, reflecting on his snub from the World Cup the contents may have raised an eyebrow from the manager who left him out.

‘I’m just looking forward to the season with Chelsea, and to be honest, I’m not too bothered about that,’ said Palmer. ‘My summer was great. I had like seven weeks off or something, which I’ve never really had. It was good. I went on holiday with my family and that.’

Asked about the games he watched on television, he admitted falling asleep at half-time of the Mexico win. He’s a cool guy, that Palmer. Every bit as cool as Tuchel is intense.

Harry Kane at England training this week. The captain knows the value of being present even when you may not be playing

Palmer said he fell asleep and so missed England's glorious victory against Mexico at the World Cup

But there’s a difference between cool and wise. And there’s a difference between being a greater player in a team and the kind who knows the value of being there, even when you’re not playing. Kane, for one.

There was never any chance of him being fit to play Brazil or Belgium under Gareth Southgate in March 2024 but he turned up anyway. He was in the room. Same went for Bellingham a year earlier – he was ruled out of qualifiers against Malta and Macedonia but demonstrated his commitment by reporting for duty.

Point is, it’s one thing to kick your heels and another to kick yourself. Palmer ought to spend some time studying the distinction.

Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE REPORT CARD - PART TWO: Man City's formidable start under Enzo Maresca, how Hull have shocked the league and Spurs and Man United struggle - last 10 sides GRADED
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE REPORT CARD - PART TWO: Man City's formidable start under Enzo Maresca, how Hull have shocked the league and Spurs and Man United struggle - last 10 sides GRADED

The beginning of the new Premier League season has been scintillating to say the least with fans going through every possible emotion during the opening five gameweeks.

While Manchester City and Arsenal being in the top two at this early stage is no great surprise, the league has had its fair share of unpredictability, with Spurs being bottom and Manchester United failing to take advantage of their kind start on paper.

The newly promoted sides all look to pose a decent threat to the weaker sides – especially Hull, who have lost just once so far.

The extended international break gives us time to take stock and review how clubs have got on.

Daily Mail Sport has already graded the first ten teams – now it is the time for a verdict on the rest.

Hull City

Position: 8th. Points: 8

The first team to receive their grade in part two are the roaring Tigers, who have been electric upon their return to the Premier League.

Many wrote this Hull team off before a ball was even kicked, deeming the squad too weak and the manager too inexperienced to have any chance of staying up. But after a ten-year hiatus from the Premier League, Jakirovic's men have looked more like European hopefuls rather than relegation fodder so far.

They made a perfect start to the campaign by beating Manchester United and have kept up steady form since, seeing off fellow newcomers Coventry away and earning creditable draws against Chelsea and Aston Villa.

Hull have found success through solidity and ruthless finishing – they were also the last side this season to concede a goal – and have outperformed their xG in every one of their wins this season.

Defeat at Newcastle remains their only blip so far and, while it will be tough for Hull to maintain their early form and retain their top-flight status, they are already proving their doubters wrong.

Grade: A

Hull continue to surprise with the newly-promoted side losing only one of their opening five

Ipswich Town

Position: 11th. Points: 6

Another newly promoted team are up next. Ipswich Town have made a swift return to the Premier League at the first time of asking after relegation in 2024/25 - and look better equipped this time around.

Under Gary O'Neil – sacked by Wolves after losing to his current club in late 2024 – they have made a promising start to their campaign as they bid to avoid dropping back into the Championship.

Ipswich sit comfortably in 11th place at the first break of the season after two impressive victories over two sides that may also be battling for survival, Sunderland and Crystal Palace.

Defeats at Old Trafford and at home to Liverpool were to be expected and are not the games O'Neil and his progressive, attacking side will be judged on come what May.

If they maintain this level they have every chance of staying up.

Grade: B+

Rolling over the competition: The Tractor boys are loving life back in the big leagues

Leeds United

Position: 5th. Points: 9

Yet another surprise package this season are Leeds, who have looked a huge threat so far this season.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin's three goals in the first five matches have helped propel Daniel Farke's unbeaten side into the early European places. This has been no fluke either – Leeds have been playing some of the best football in the division with a five-man midfield that has the capacity to dominate proceedings.

An impressive demonstration of their style came in a 4-1 rout of Newcastle, with three goals coming without reply in the first half.

The season is still at a very, very early stage but Farke's start, coupled with the smart business done in the transfer window, will have fans dreaming of more than a relegation battle and perhaps an outside push for a European place.

Leeds will return from the international break to the toughest of tests, a lunchtime kick-off at Arsenal. Most will assume the Gunners will end their unbeaten run but don't bet against an upset at the Emirates.

Grade: A

Daniel Farke has experienced some tough seasons in the Premier League before but now could have something special brewing at Elland Road

Liverpool

Position: 6th. Points: 9

Mixed results early on may have left supporters wondering where to stand on Andoni Iraola's start to life at Anfield.

Following a dismal defence of their Premier League crown last season, leading to the sacking of Arne Slot, Iraola has arrived with fresh ideas and a new plan – which even he has admitted is tricky for his expensive band of stars.

After the departure of Mo Salah in the summer, there are now only three players from Jurgen Klopp's legendary Premier League and Champions league winning side and finding replacements have been an expensive and largely unsuccessful process for Liverpool so far.

But, after the issues of the 2025-26 campaign, Iraola has managed to get a tune out of some Liverpool's big money recruits. Alexander Isak is finally firing after returning from a nasty injury, Alexis Mac Allister is back to his best despite his contract dispute and Cody Gakpo has transformed his game.

These improvements have helped Liverpool to remain unbeaten in the first five but draws with Forest, Newcastle and Fulham will be a worry. They have also been left defensively exposed in midfield at times and are yet to see a return of investment from £116million Florian Wirtz.

Iraola will only grow into the role but, as the schedule gets tighter and tougher tests await, Liverpool will be hoping that doesn't take too long.

Grade: B

Alexander Isak is back in the goals and unbeaten Liverpool will hope Iraola can get this team of superstars finally ticking

Manchester City

Position: 1st. Points: 15

The only 100 per cent side so far are of course the perennial title challengers, Manchester City.

City have adapted marvellously to life under Enzo Maresca. Worryingly for the rest, the former Chelsea boss appears to have picked up from where Pep Guardiola left off in the club's first season in a decade without the Spaniard at the helm.

Erling Haaland has begun another campaign in splendid form, sitting at the top of the goalscoring charts with five in five games, and will hope his goals can bring the title back to the Etihad after two years, the longest it has been away from City since Guardiola's arrival in 2016.

As always the owners splashed the cash in the summer, spending £321million to build a new midfield in the wake of legends Bernardo Silva, Ilkay Gundogan and Rodri all leaving. The investment already seems to be paying off.

Elliot Anderson has started to look very accomplished at the base of Maresca's double pivot in midfield, the young Ayyoub Bouaddi has been impressively comfortable in a new league and Enzo Fernandez has been magnificent following his move from Chelsea.

Arsenal will have a tough job on their hands stopping this City juggernaut from rolling towards what would be a ninth Premier League title but considering the start both teams have had we can be excited for another close and chaotic title race.

Grade: A

Manchester City are already firing under Maresca with five wins from five leaving them top

Manchester United

Position: 12th. Points: 5

From the blue half of Manchester to the red – and completely differing fortunes for United, who have endured a woeful start to the campaign.

A kind start to the season, featuring games against two newly-promoted sides, has not yielded the results Michael Carrick, the club and the fans would have wanted or expected.

The Red Devils got off to the worst possible start with defeat at Hull and haven't fully recovered since. They managed to respond the following week with an emphatic 5-2 win over Ipswich but that remains their only league victory so far this season.

Carrick was trusted with the permanent role in the summer after an excellent end to last season but teams already seem to have worked his style out.

Opponents appear to have got wise to his counter-attacking style and his players have struggled to break down opponents, while failing to keep clean sheets.

Many feel the club's recruitment team left Carrick short in the summer window and the Red Devils are feeling the effects now.

Unless these underlying issues with tactics and personnel are sorted, United are in danger of slipping back down the table and starting the process of a 'rebuild' all over again.

Grade: D

Manchester United have made a poor start to a season that had promised so much

Newcastle United:

Position: 9th. Points: 8

After a summer of being gutted Matthias Jaissle has done remarkably well to steady the ship at St James' Park.

The Magpies had a testing transfer window losing not only Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes but also their long-term manager Eddie Howe and have incredibly rolled with the punches perhaps looking even better as a result.

Young German coach Matthias Jaissle has come in and instilled the same style of play that Jurgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel found so much success with in England and is taking Newcastle into a new era.

Of course they have not been perfect on Tyneside but considering what some Geordies feared I think they will be pleased with the steady progress they have made in the first month. The Magpies did take a real wing clipping against Leeds losing 4-1 away at Elland road but that aside results have been steady.

They have had drawn two all twice at home and managed wins against Spurs and Hull, being the first side this season to pick up three points against the Tigers and appear to score in bunches with their goals coming within less than ten minutes of each other in both their wins.

Grade: B

Geordies will be extremely pleased with their start to season after a rough summer and look forward to the Premier League returning more than most

Nottingham Forest

Position: 13th. Points: 5

Oliver Glasner was tasked with being the man to provide stability to Nottingham Forest after the club churned through four managers last season, which began with Nuno Espirito Santo's acrimonious departure.

Glasner's side are yet to truly get going so far this campaign, something that might concern their ambitious owner Evangelos Marinakis.

Concerningly, Forest have failed to score in their three home matches against Leeds, Tottenham and Coventry, losing two of them.

The 1-0 defeat to newly promoted Coventry – who had lost their opening four matches without scoring – will have worried fans heading into the extended international break.

Forest's sole league win came away against midlands rivals Aston Villa, with Igor Jesus's late goal giving them their highlight of the campaign to date.

Grade: C

Forest will need to pick up regular points quickly to avoid slipping further down the table after the international break

Sunderland

Position: 14th. Points: 4

The Black Cats have the tricky task of backing up their stunning campaign last season after their promotion back to the top flight, which ended in Europa League qualification.

Few are expecting them to kick on this campaign, with a drop off considered more likely due to having to balance European football with their domestic endeavours.

Sunderland have only managed one win so far against a struggling Fulham side, but have also had to face both Manchester City and Arsenal in the first month. They performed well in both but ultimately suffered defeats, despite Brian Brobbey's hat-trick at the Etihad.

Regis Le Bris's men will be frustrated to have slipped up in their season opener away at Ipswich where they lost late on to the hands of their former player, Jack Clarke.

Four points may be seen as a disappointing return to date, with the fixture list only going to become more congested and the squad stretched after the international break.

Grade: C+

Sunderland have been unlucky thus far but must begin winning again soon if they are to avoid the common second season relegation

Tottenham Hotspur

Position: 20th. Points: 2

After back-to-back 17th placed finishes, Tottenham's heavy summer spending prompted hope they could lift themselves out of the crisis state the club has been in.

Yet Tottenham find themselves propping up the table after five games with Roberto De Zerbi's side still without a win in the league.

Spurs have only managed two goals all season and are sat rudderless at the bottom of the table

Most pundits believe Tottenham have too much quality to get involved in another relegation scrap, but their start to the season has been extremely worrying.

Tottenham have proved unable so far to resolve their disastrous home record that has plagued them over the past two seasons. De Zerbi's side have been beaten by Newcastle and Aston Villa – who both underwent drastic summer changes as well – and also drew with Everton in front of their home fans.

The club's ownership has so far yet to see the return on the more than £300million spent on new arrivals this summer, after they reacted to the scare of just surviving on the final day of last season.

A major improvement in results after the international break is needed to lift the mood and ensure Tottenham are not facing a third consecutive season of struggle at the wrong end of the table.

Grade: F

Sports.title: Why Tottenham may regret selling red-hot Will Lankshear, the warning signs Lee Carsley cannot ignore and a fresh Chelsea injury concern as England's Under 21s beat Kazakhstan 4-2
Sports.content:
Why Tottenham may regret selling red-hot Will Lankshear, the warning signs Lee Carsley cannot ignore and a fresh Chelsea injury concern as England's Under 21s beat Kazakhstan 4-2

England men's Under 21s squeezed past Kazakhstan to move Lee Carsley's side within one match of sealing their place at next summer's tournament.

The back-to-back reigning champions made life difficult for themselves, going behind early on and then conceding an equaliser on the stroke of half-time.

But goals from Manchester City loanee Max Alleyne and former Tottenham striker Will Lankshear ensured England picked up all three points in a dominant qualifying campaign in which the Young Lions have won eight and drawn one of their nine matches.

England now need just a point against Slovakia next Friday to seal their spot as one of the 16 sides heading to Albania and Serbia next year.

Daily Mail Sport's TARA ANSON-WALSH was at Molineux Stadium to give you the things we learned from England's 4-2 win over Kazakhstan...

Lee Carsley's side now need just one point against Slovakia next Friday to book their spot among the 16 sides heading to Albania and Serbia next year

The striker Tottenham let get away

The name on everyone's lips at the moment is former Tottenham striker Will Lankshear after the 21-year-old's impressive start to the season at Middlesbrough.

Lankshear joined Boro for £20million this summer after making six appearances for Spurs during the 2024-25 season, scoring once. He has hit the ground running on Teesside, scoring six times in his first eight Championship matches.

His purple patch showed no signs of slowing on Friday, with the forward sliding in to score an impressive flick from close range just 22 minutes after coming off the bench.

England have produced plenty of No10s in recent years, winning the 2025 Euros without a recognised centre forward, but the lack of an out-and-out striker has long been a bugbear for Carsley.

Michael Owen even suggested Lankshear should have been considered by Thomas Tuchel amid a 'dearth' of strikers in the game and no obvious successor to Harry Kane.

Carsley, mindful of not overhyping a youngster who has already begun to draw comparisons with England's record goalscorer, was measured in his praise at full-time.

'He's had a strong week. The way he's played at Middlesbrough, he's definitely brought that confidence into the camp.

'You always wonder whether that's transferrable, when you're doing so well at a club, but he's showed that tonight. His finish was outstanding.

'He's shown a bit of character because I left him out of the squad for the first game against Kazakhstan (last September) and sometimes that goes one way or the other and he's definitely found his game.'

As for Tottenham, given their own struggles in front of goal this season, Roberto De Zerbi and Co may yet come to regret cashing in on a young striker who cannot stop finding the back of the net.

Lankshear's purple patch showed no signs of slowing on Friday, with the forward sliding in to score from close range just 22 minutes after coming off the bench

Man City's academy shines amid the chaos

On the day news broke that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 of 115 charges, three City academy graduates lined up for Carsley's side, more than from any other club.

Those were Rico Lewis, Under 21 debutant Stephen Mfuni (on loan at Coventry City) and goalscorer Max Alleyne (on loan at Birmingham City). Divin Mubama, who is currently on loan at Southampton, completed the City contingent, although he is not an academy graduate, having come through the ranks at West Ham.

For everything that has clearly been wrong with how the club has been managed over the past couple of decades, that cannot detract from the plaudits it deserves for its investment in local talent.

Appearing unfazed by the latest developments, the trio impressed in equal measure against Kazakhstan. Lewis looked particularly strong going forward and consistently looks at ease in this expansive set-up. Mubama provided a serious goal threat and was unlucky not to score in the first half. And centre back Alleyne capped off his night with his first Under 21s goal on the hour mark, guiding home the winner from a free kick.

City's Lewis looked particularly strong going forward and consistently looks at ease in this expansive set-up

Carsley gets a timely warning

For all England's dominance, this match against the group's underdogs was not without its concerns for Carsley.

Kazakhstan had not scored more than once in any of their previous nine qualifying matches and ended that two-year run at Molineux on Friday night.

The manner of the goals conceded will be Carsley's chief concern given they both came from moments when England appeared to be sleeping at set pieces.

Kazakhstan's first arrived after just three minutes from a corner, and it quickly became apparent that Carsley's side had not realised the game had started when Artyom Litosh breezed into the six-yard box and coolly volleyed home to send the 20 or so away fans, four of whom stood proudly behind a Kazakhstan flag for most of the match, into raptures.

The visitors' equaliser before the break came from a long throw, with Kazakhstan's Saif Popov given two attempts at goal before his third effort finally found a way past Birmingham City's James Beadle.

Not only that, but England also looked vulnerable immediately after scoring two of their goals and would have been punished had Kazakhstan possessed a little more quality.

At full time, Carsley said: 'This team haven't played together for six months, so I'm not going to be too critical, but they know that they have to play better than that if we're going to be a serious team.

'We were too open at times. Against a better team, no disrespect to Kazakhstan... we were under pressure.'

Kazakhstan had not scored more than once in any of their previous nine qualifying matches and ended that two-year run at Molineux on Friday night

Fresh frustration for Gittens

What had already appeared to be a difficult start to the season for Jamie Gittens now looks as though it may have become even tougher.

After making 16 appearances for Chelsea last term, Gittens has yet to feature for Xabi Alonso's side in the Premier League, with his only two outings this season coming in the Carabao Cup.

Any hopes of breaking into the first-team picture may now be delayed further after the 22-year-old limped off in the 39th minute following a kick to the ankle and headed straight down the tunnel.

He later left the stadium on crutches and wearing a protective boot, with Carsley confirming he will return to the London club for a full assessment.

Gittens left the stadium on crutches and wearing a protective boot, with Carsley confirming he will return to his club for a full assessment

A homecoming for Coady

Sometimes football's storylines are simply too neat, and Conor Coady's return to Molineux for his first taste of coaching with the Under 21s was one of them.

The 33-year-old agreed to terminate his contract with Wrexham in the summer before being swiftly appointed as Carsley's assistant. Coady has not formally retired, either, with Carsley joking that his ability to still join in training is 'a bonus'.

'He's an excellent example,' Carsley said. 'It's always important that we have someone on the staff who knows what it's like to play at Wembley for England and to be around squads. We had that in Ash (Ashley Cole) and Joleon (Lescott) and now we've got it in Conor.'

Coady received a warm welcome on his return to Molineux, where he spent seven seasons marshalling Wolves' defence. The Liverpudlian's 314 appearances for the club still place him among the club's top 20 appearance-makers of all time.

Sports.title: Former Liverpool star Andy Robertson admits 'shock' over Man City's guilty verdict in case against Premier League - but insists players who beat him to TWO titles are not to blame
Sports.content:
Former Liverpool star Andy Robertson admits 'shock' over Man City's guilty verdict in case against Premier League - but insists players who beat him to TWO titles are not to blame

Scotland captain Andy Robertson insists it would be wrong for Manchester City’s players to be tarnished by the bombshell verdict on the club’s breach of financial regulations.

City have finally been found guilty on almost all of the 115 charges which had been hanging over them for these past few years.

During his nine years as a Liverpool player, Robertson jousted regularly with City as the two clubs forged one of the great rivalries in the Premier League era.

Robertson was twice part of a Liverpool side that finished second to City in the Premier League in 2019 and 2022. But, in terms of the players he faced on the pitch, Robertson insists he holds no grudges after some epic battles with City over the years.

‘I think you can hear the shock in my voice,’ said Robertson, who will lead Scotland out and win his 98th cap in the Nations League clash against Slovenia.

‘The case has obviously been going on. For me, the [Man City] players showed they were good enough on the pitch.

Andy Robertson was involved in many fierce battles with Manchester City while at Liverpool

‘I don’t know too much about the charges. But they had an incredible team, one that I loved battling against.

‘I don’t think when it comes to these things that players are ever to blame. That’s all I can focus on.’

This will be the start of a new era for Scotland with Sebastien Pocognoli taking charge of the team for the first time.

Robertson revealed that the 39-year-old Belgian travelled to London to personally meet him and have dinner after being appointed.

The skipper is excited about the prospect of what the future could hold under the new head coach but also believes it’s important not to forget the achievements of Steve Clarke.

Clarke resigned after the World Cup in the summer following Scotland’s group stage exit, a fate they also suffered at Euro 2020 and Euro 2024.

‘Time will tell if it will look different,’ said Robertson. ‘We haven’t had a lot of time on the pitch. He’s given us good information without overloading us.

‘It’s been a really good training week. We’ve enjoyed it and hopefully that we can take that into this game against Slovenia.

Andy Robertson and Jack Hendry will hope to get Sebastien Pocognoli off to a positive start

‘I don’t think there’s an in-between. You can be excited for the future but respect the past. Some people have been caught in two minds on that.

‘In my opinion, the time under Steve Clarke was a hugely successful one. He came in and his remit was to qualify for tournaments. For him to do three out of four, that’s nothing but success.

‘We can talk about how we performed at the tournaments but as a team and as a country we managed to get back on the biggest stage.

‘That has to be a positive. Now, we can be excited for the future under this manager. It will maybe be a different way of playing, a different style, younger players coming in.

‘So you can do both. That would be my message to everyone. You can still appreciate what we had in the past and what we achieved. But we can also be excited for the future.

‘That’s been my message to the players and I think they can feel that. Hopefully we can push to reach new heights.’

Sports.title: Man City face RELEGATION 'nuclear option' and appeal 'highly unlikely to succeed', says their former financial advisor, as they are found guilty of 114 Premier League charges
Sports.content:
Former Manchester City financial advisor Stefan Borson has claimed 'anything is possible,' including the nuclear option of relegation, after the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

The Premier League accused the club of widespread financial cheating over an era of sustained success – with an independent panel hearing concluding in 2024.

There has since been a frustrating wait for a verdict but Daily Mail Sport sources have disclosed that clubs have been informed that the panel has now reached a decision – and there is a belief it's a win for the top flight.

City are understood to have been found guilty on all but one of their 115 rule-break charges concerning the Premier League’s financial regulations.

Borson, who advised Man City between 2002 and 2007, was asked by talkSPORT whether the nuclear option of relegation from the Premier League was on the table as a possible punishment following the decision.

'Anything is possible and all hell is now going to break loose, as this is going to go on for weeks and weeks and weeks,' Borson said.

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 Premier League rule-break charges

Former Man City financial advisor Stefan Borson believes 'anything is possible' regarding the club's potentinal punishments and that an appeal is 'hihgly unlikely to succeed'

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation

'It is going to be very hard for City to say anything or to contain the fallout from this scenario and that is without being able to see what is in this decision.

'We will almost certainly soon see the decision of the independent commission laid out in great detail, it will give people huge ammunition to attack those individuals and the club.

'Then we will go into the process, which will be behind closed doors, around the sanction.

'Man City have denied everything all the way through, they have gone through a process that may have cost more than £100m between the two parties and they have been found to have breached everything.

'They are in very, very serious trouble.'

An appeal from Man City is considered inevitable with the club having always strongly denied wrongdoing, since they were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League.

A Manchester City spokesperson said: 'The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023.

'The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

Borson claimed an appeal from Man City is 'highly unlikely to succeed' and suggested their statement indicated their likely arguments in an attempt to overturn the verdict.

'An appeal on the facts is highly unlikely to succeed,' he said.

The club have maintained that they are innocent throughout the process and are expected to appeal

'Where we are now with City being found guilty of more or less everything, the decision itself will be scathing in terms of the club’s conduct, the conduct of individuals, the behaviour of individuals and the hearing itself in terms of their credibility. There won’t be any hiding place when that decision is published.

'To then have to present that to an appeal that does not have the benefit of listening to the whole case all over again, in terms of witness evidence, seeing all the documentation again, it is going to be extremely difficult for City to overturn those factual findings.

‘City have hinted in the last paragraph of their statement, I think their suggestion is that the process and panel itself was in some way partial and biased and that they will in some way challenge the length of time it has taken for the decision to come out.

'All of those sorts of arguments, be it bias or something procedural, all of them are very unlikely to succeed. Overturning factual findings I would say is very, very unlikely.

'Ultimately now I think City will have to take their punishment and it will be severe.'

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

A three-man panel was tasked with considering the evidence, with the initial expectation a verdict would have been reached on the case within months. It has since taken three-and-a-half years.

The original 115 charges were extended to a total of 130 after an administration issue in what is the most expensive and wide-ranging case in English football history.

Eight Premier League titles, three FA Cups, six League Cups and one Champions League have all been won by the club in the modern era

City remained steadfast in maintaining their innocence over more than 115 alleged breaches across eight years, some including the start of the Pep Guardiola era.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups, and seven EFL Cups.

City vehemently denied any breaches of financial rules but the investigation started in December 2018 after German website Der Spiegel published documents from a Football Leaks cache which had originated from Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto.

It alleged that City had overstated sponsorship income with money paid from the club's owners instead of sponsors linked to Abu Dhabi.

Roberto Mancini's wages were said to have doubled via a secret contract with an Abu Dhabi club when he was at Man City, while they were also alleged to have broken rules over approaching young players.

The Mail on Sunday has led the way on reporting the story. In July 2021, they reported on emails that appeared to suggest that Man City had millions funnelled into the club by Abu Dhabi to help inflate their income.

Back in February 2020, the club were banned from the Champions League and fined £25million after they were found to have seriously misled European footballing governing body UEFA and broken financial fair play rules.

This was then lifted by the Court of Arbitration for Sport which also reduced the club's fine to £9million.

Sports.title: MAN CITY FAN VIEW: My club's relationship with financial skullduggery has left me yearning for the comedy club days, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
For those of us who supported Manchester City long before they were accused of financial skulduggery, it has been a strange few years. City were completely inoffensive back then – the comedy club who once kept the ball near the corner flag because they had been (wrongly) told a draw would spare them relegation. For years, the fans survived on scraps. The near miss in the 1981 FA Cup final, when they were robbed by a freakish Tommy Hutchison own goal. The Full Members’ Cup final of 1986, when they lost 5-4 to Chelsea. The mad play-off comeback against Gillingham. But when the money poured in from Abu Dhabi, there arose a strange conundrum. Did I prefer the old days, when City were popular but useless? Or was it all about winning, no matter the cost? The answer was not always straightforward. Now that they’ve been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges, at least we finally have a bit of clarity, grim though it looks. My greatest fear has always been that they would be retrospectively stripped of titles, like Russian athletes at the Olympics. Man City's 115 charges saga has left LAWRENCE BOOTH yearning for the comedy club days The idea Sergio Aguero's last-gasp title winning goal against QPR in 2012 might now be null and void is hard to stomatch Financial penalties, points deductions, even relegation – I could live with all that. But the idea that the last-ditch winner against QPR in 2011-12 might now be null and void is hard to stomach: Aguerooooo…oh! Other fans, who have continually protested their indifference to a ‘small club’ like City, will still say their achievements deserve an asterisk. That’s how fandom operates. No matter the lawyers eventually conclude – needless to say, City will appeal – the court of public opinion made up its mind long ago. I get the sentiment. I didn’t like the fact that City were attracting censure, not affection. I hated the thought that their trophies were regarded as ill-gotten gains. But try as I might, I couldn’t cut the umbilical cord. It’s not terribly logical, but that’s how fandom operates too. I was also suspicious of the notion that money automatically means success. Manchester United are proof that life isn’t always so simple. Money helps, sure. But it has to be spent wisely: Sergio Aguero, Kevin de Bruyne, Bernardo Silva, Ederson, even Manuel Akanji – was anyone else trying to buy these guys? Oddly, I found last season quite relaxing, what with Arsenal finally getting over the line. Sorry if it sounds arrogant, but winning the league was no longer the thrill it was when Aguero did his thing. Life felt a bit more normal again: a draw was not a disaster, and City’s defending was occasionally comical, just like the old times. Who knows: perhaps, one day, people will even learn to love us again, though I accept that is more likely if we’re banished to the Enterprise Rent-A-Car National League first.

Sports.title: 'I turned down England call up – it was a rash decision that cost my career'
Sports.content:
'I turned down England call up – it was a rash decision that cost my career'

Getting asked to represent your country is the pinnacle of most footballers' careers, but one former England star snubbed a call-up in a decision he ultimately regretted

View 2 Images Chris Sutton feels his England snub in 1998 derailed his international career (Image: Ben Radford /Allsport)

Chris Sutton admits he acted rashly in snubbing a call up to the England B team in 1998, which he claims ultimately cost him his international career. The Three Lions return to action on Saturday night with a visit from World Cup winners Spain in the Nations League.

‌



Thomas Tuchel has seen five players withdraw from the squad since his announcement. Cole Palmer, Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Declan Rice all stepped down from their latest request for international duty.

‌



Tuchel has opted to call upon Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner as replacements. One former England star who regrets not sticking with his initial call-up over 25 years ago is popular pundit Sutton.

‌



The former striker had only managed one senior cap before he was requested to play in a B team game against Chile in the build-up to the 1998 World Cup. Then-manager Glenn Hoddle wanted to see Sutton in action before selecting his official tournament squad.

Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest READ MORE :

Inside the rise of Ezri Konsa and why World Cup star can inspire England's next generation READ MORE :

However, Sutton snubbed the chance to be involved as he firmly believed he deserved to be in the main team. Previously speaking to the Daily Mail, the now-53-year-old accepted that saying no to England at that time derailed his international career.

Sutton explained: "Yes, I made a rash decision with England. Well, a little bit of a rash decision. I don't know if it was held against me when Sven Goran Eriksson was manager.

‌



View 2 Images The formidable forward went on to find major success with Celtic (Image: Getty)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"I went to Celtic and had five good years there, playing some good football and never got a look-in. Let's be realistic, I wouldn't have played that often because there were players ahead of me in the pecking order. But that decision back then? Yes, it was a bit impetuous."

‌



At the time, Sutton was playing a starring role for Blackburn Rovers after helping them win the Premier League title in the 1994/95 season. A year at Chelsea followed before he saw his major success come with Scottish side Celtic.

The ex-striker won eight major trophies in Scotland, including four league titles, three Scottish Cups and the League Cup. He was also part of Martin O'Neill's side that reached the UEFA Cup final in 2004, losing 3-2 to Porto.

Sutton retired in 2007 after stints at Aston Villa and Birmingham City, having earned only one cap for his country. As for England now, their Nations League campaign is set to begin, and you can still get VIP tickets for the upcoming fixtures.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Barcelona make position clear on JJ Gabriel and academy star signs pro contract
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Barcelona make position clear on JJ Gabriel and academy star signs pro contract

Manchester United won't be in action for another two weeks with the international break in full flow but there's still plenty going on behind the scenes

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has two weeks before Manchester United play again (Image: Getty)

Manchester United will be back in exactly two weeks as the extended international break continues. Michael Carrick's side have endured a difficult start to the season.

‌



Club football has been put on hold as players have jetted off to represent their respective national teams. But that hasn't paused the discourse surrounding United. In five top-flight matches so far, they've won just once against Ipswich Town.

‌



United began the season with a 2-0 loss to Hull City and have also lost 1-0 to Manchester City. They drew with both Everton and Fulham, their last game before the break. Carrick's team have also been knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton but did win their Champions League opener against Sabah FK.

‌



Not to mention, behind the scenes, there have also been complications with one of the club's most promising youngsters, JJ Gabriel, who has requested that his registration be cancelled. An update has now been issued regarding Barcelona's interest in the 15-year-old. Mirror Football brings you all the latest from Old Trafford.

Barcelona chief speaks out about JJ Gabriel

Last week, 15-year-old Gabriel requested that his United registration be terminated. As he is not old enough to sign a scholarship agreement or a pro contract, this would have been the only way for him to become a free agent and therefore leave for another club.

View 3 Images Gabriel has made it clear he wants to leave United (Image: Getty)

‌



United denied this request to leave, but would be powerless to prevent Gabriel from leaving when he turns 16 on October 6. Because he qualifies for an EU passport via his Irish and Cypriot heritage, he could, in theory, move to another side in continental Europe after this date.

Barcelona were one club rumoured to be interested and reports even suggested that Gabriel and his representatives flew in to hold talks with La Blaugrana. However, their sporting director, Deco, has now shut down these suggestions.

"There's nothing to say about this boy," Deco said at the Portugal Football Summit. "It's normal that players are linked with us. It always happens. There's a huge market for that with a lot of interests involved, even when [players] are young.

‌



"But we are not interested in any player in his situation. I'm not sure what's happening, and if he's still a Manchester United player. We are not involved in that. First of all, we need to understand how the situation is before we try to do something. To speak about young, teenage players, it is not our business."

Academy winger signs new long-term deal

Elsewhere, one of Gabriel's team-mates, Noah Ajayi, has signed his first professional contract at the club. The 17-year-old prospect has impressed this season and last.

View 3 Images Ajayi has signed his first deal (Image: Getty)

‌



Ajayi is a regular for United's Under-18s, with whom he has played alongside Gabriel, and represents Germany at youth level, having been born in Hamburg.

United released a statement announcing Ajayi's contract, reading: "Exciting youngster Noah Ajayi has committed his future to Manchester United. The 17-year-old winger has signed a long-term professional contract.

"Ajayi was a stand-out for Darren Fletcher's Under-18s side last season, making important contributions to help the young Reds reach the FA Youth Cup final.

Article continues below

"Everyone at Manchester United is delighted that Noah has signed a new deal and looks forward to seeing him progress."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta's assistant names huge transfer target as Kai Havertz latest emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta's assistant names huge transfer target as Kai Havertz latest emerges

Arsenal's interest in a world class player has been confirmed by Mikel Arteta's assistant

View 3 Images Arsenal assistant coach Miguel Molina has shed light on the Gunners' summer transfer activity (Image: Getty )

A whopping 17 Arsenal players were called up by their national teams for the current international break. Several of them have already lit up the Nations League, with captain Martin Odegaard most notably notching two assists for Norway and Christos Tzolis getting on the scoresheet for Greece.

‌



A large Gunners contingent will also face off tonight as World Cup winners Spain take on third-placed finishers England. But Mikel Arteta’s priority will be for all of his players still on international duty to arrive fit and healthy for Arsenal’s Premier League clash with Leeds United on October 10.

‌



The Premier League champions kicked off the 2026/27 campaign with seven straight wins across the Community Shield, league, Champions League and Carabao Cup. That run ended with a shock 3-0 demolition at Brighton in their last fixture - something Arteta and his staff will be eager to put right.

‌



Now, Mirror Football brings you the latest Arsenal news from the international break.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal receive fresh Kai Havertz injury update as Germany star to leave camp READ MORE :

Martin Odegaard admits injuries diminished his enjoyment of Arsenal's Premier League title READ MORE :

Huge transfer target named

View 3 Images Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr was a target for Arsenal during the summer window (Image: Getty )

‌



Arteta’s assistant coach, Miguel Molina, has confirmed Arsenal’s summer pursuit of Vinicius Junior. In late July, the north Londoners emerged as a serious potential destination for Vinicius.

The 26-year-old winger had only a year left on his contract and was widely claimed to have hit a wall in negotiations over a new deal with Real Madrid. Arsenal sought to capitalise on his uncertainty by reportedly agreeing personal terms in a deal which would have made Vinicius their highest-paid player by some distance.

However, the Gunners were left surprised when Real Madrid bosses performed a sudden U-turn and offered the Brazilian an improved contract extension until 2032, ending Arsenal’s hopes of sealing his signature.

‌



Molina, who joined his compatriot’s backroom staff back in August 2020, recently appeared as a guest on Radio Marca’s La Tribu, where he was asked about Arsenal’s interest in Vinicius.

He said: "Yes, of course. Obviously, I can’t stray from the facts, but he [Vinícius] was a name that was on the table, yes." The Brazilian’s decision to remain at the Bernabeu doesn’t seem to have worked out in his favour yet, however, as he has gone nearly a month without finding the net.

Kai Havertz injury latest

View 3 Images Havertz picked up an issue just 30 minutes into the Germany game (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Kai Havertz will return to Arsenal and undergo an assessment after suffering an injury during Germany’s first Nations League fixture against the Netherlands. The 27-year-old striker was forced to come off in the first half of the 1-1 draw on Thursday evening.

His international break is over due to the suspected hamstring injury, which came as a result of a reckless challenge by Arsenal team-mate Jurrien Timber’s twin brother, Quinten. However, The Athletic reports that there is optimism regarding Arteta’s star striker, with the early belief being that his injury is not serious. Havertz is set to return to N5 for assessment and recovery.

The German has started off the season as Arteta’s first-choice striker over Viktor Gyokeres. And the manager’s heart would have been in his mouth after Havertz went to ground clutching his hamstring, having missed much of last season.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: JJ Gabriel transfer update, Glazers stake decision, INEOS boycott plan latest
Sports.content:
Manchester United still have more than two weeks to go until they are next back in action against Tottenham with the extended international break in full swing

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football 's Manchester United news live blog for Friday, September 25.

JJ Gabriel is still the main topic of conversation at Old Trafford, more than a week on since he expressed his desire to cancel his registration and leave United with immediate effect. The Reds have been left stunned by Gabriel's decision but are still hoping to convince him to stay, despite significant interest elsewhere.

Barcelona and Real Madrid are among the leading contenders to land Gabriel's signature and it's thought he would prefer a move to Spain, rather than joining Bayern Munich or Paris Saint-Germain. If he does chose to remain in England, however, Chelsea is his top option.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland U-turn confirmed immediately after Man City found guilty of 114 charges
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland U-turn confirmed immediately after Man City found guilty of 114 charges

Erling Haaland was due to speak to the media for Norway this weekend but Manchester City's charges update has reportedly led to a change

View 2 Images Erling Haaland's Norway press conference was cancelled after Man City's guilty verdict (Image: Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images)

Norway have reportedly taken the decision to remove Erling Haaland from press conference duty following news of Manchester City being found guilty of alleged financial breaches. The City striker was originally scheduled to face the media this weekend ahead of Norway’s clash against Portugal on Sunday in the Nations League.

‌



News emerged on Friday claiming that City had been found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges that were brought against them by the Premier League back in 2023.

‌



City are now facing a wait to discover what punishment they could receive, with the club having the right to appeal the outcome, which has been widely reported in the media. As a result, City face the prospect of being given a punishment which could range from a points deduction all the way up to expulsion from the Premier League.

‌



Haaland is currently with the Norway squad for the extended international break, and was recently in action on Thursday night as he helped his country claim a 3-2 win over Denmark, where he was on the score sheet twice.

Rodri speaks out on Man City guilty verdict as press conference stopped after 'justice' claim READ MORE :

Premier League clubs consider legal action as Man Utd react to Man City guilty verdict READ MORE :

The striker was expected to speak to the media this weekend ahead of Norway’s next game against Portugal, but that will no longer be the case.

As reported by TV2, Haaland has been replaced for Norway’s pre-match press conference duties by Benfica duo Andreas Schjelderup and Fredrik Aursnes.

‌



Norway’s media manager Morten Skjonsberg is reported to have given a message to the media that Haaland will no longer be speaking to reporters this weekend.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Haaland will no longer address the media (Image: Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images)

‌



“We are making changes to tomorrow’s press conference,” the message is reported to have read. “(Stale) Solbakken, (Fredrik) Aursnes and (Andreas) Schjelderup will be on the ground floor.”

Haaland has already previously spoken about the charges that were brought against City, where the striker says he was reassured that the situation would be resolved.

"I spoke with the bosses, and in the end, I believe them," Haaland said in an interview with TIME Magazine in July last year. "It’s such a tricky situation for me to even sit there and speak about, because I wasn’t really involved in it.

"So I think the club knows what they’re doing. They will sort it out."

Sports.title: Man City get new punishment verdict as three factors for guilty ruling appeal made clear
Sports.content:
Man City get new punishment verdict as three factors for guilty ruling appeal made clear

Manchester City have been handed new verdicts on what will follow them being found guilty of a significant number of financial charges

View 2 Images Manchester City's next steps regarding an appeal have been revealed (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Two legal experts have shared their thoughts on the next steps for Manchester City regarding their expected appeal and potential punishments. Earlier today, it emerged that the club had been found in breach of 114 Premier League financial regulations.

‌



City were initially charged in February 2023 with this outcome from their hearing against the Premier League just under two years ago. And there is expected to be further delays to any final solution with it understood that City will be appealing against the guilty verdict.

‌



Sports barrister at Church Court Chambers Yasin Patel has now offered his thoughts on the appeal while also making it clear that some clubs could take action.

‌



He said: "City's lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors - importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

Every new Premier League champion if Man City are stripped of titles for 114 guilty charges READ MORE :

Man City verdict LIVE: Premier League giants found guilty of 114 of 115 charges READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

"Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City's wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon."

‌



Ian Hargreaves, a partner at specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, has also discussed City's next moves following the latest development.

Hargreaves said: "The rumoured verdict is not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase in what has become one of the most closely watched legal battles in global sport.

"The key questions this news raises are what sanction the panel considers proportionate and what guidance can be drawn from previous cases. There is a wide range of options, with a transfer ban at the more moderate end of the spectrum and expulsion from the league the most severe repercussion.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City released a statement of their own

"There is also the question of whether the panel's decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel's findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides."

"The outcome will also have wider implications for the balance of power in European football, although Premier League clubs will point out that these findings relate to historic conduct and not the league's current financial framework."

‌



A City statement read: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool are the sides to have been denied Premier League titles during the period in which City are judged to have secured an unfair advantage.

Article continues below

City are not back in action for another two weeks, with the extended international break stretching into October, and their first opponents upon return are Liverpool — arguably the club who have been denied the most silverware by City over the past decade.
