He also challenged whether Gbeisay had genuine ties to Nimba County or any standing to weigh in on its land affairs.

Adding another layer to the controversy, former Superintendent Cooper testified during proceedings before Gbeisay that he and others had already returned a separate parcel of land in Ganta to Suah in an earlier attempt to settle overlapping claims — though it remains unclear whether that parcel has any bearing on the property at the center of the recent evictions.

With the fresh summons, Suah’s public comments about the Chief Justice may now themselves become the subject of judicial proceedings, adding a new legal front to a dispute that has already spanned the courts, the community, and the media.

Gbeisay continues to frame the matter as simple enforcement of a lawful court order, distancing the Supreme Court from direct blame. Suah and affected residents, meanwhile, argue the real issue is how long-term occupants were treated and whether the eviction process was fair. Neither man has been found to have committed wrongdoing by any judicial body, and both sets of allegations remain unproven.

A motion challenging the underlying judgment is reportedly set for a December hearing, leaving the core ownership dispute — and the increasingly personal battle between a sitting Chief Justice and a former mayor — unresolved for now.

World.title: LAA Seeks Aviation Partnerships, Investment at Major African Airports Conference in Nigeria
World.content:
Hughes-led delegation explores technical cooperation, infrastructure support and funding opportunities to modernize Liberia’s airport system

HARBel, Margibi County — The Liberia Airport Authority (LAA) says it is seeking technical partnerships, investment and logistical support to strengthen Liberia’s aviation infrastructure as it participates in a major regional airport conference in Abuja, Nigeria.

The LAA delegation, led by Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Ernest R. Hughes, with Chief Financial Officer Victor Debah, is attending the Airports Council International (ACI) Africa 35th Annual General Assembly, 75th Board and Committee Meetings, Regional Conference and Exhibition, running from September 19 to 25, 2026.

According to a press release issued by the Authority, the weeklong gathering is bringing together airport executives, policymakers, regulators, development partners and aviation industry stakeholders to discuss the future of African aviation under the theme, “Next-Gen Airports: Driving Performance and Resilience.”

The LAA said its participation is intended to strengthen Liberia’s engagement with regional and international aviation institutions while exploring opportunities to improve airport operations, infrastructure and service delivery.

During the conference, the delegation is expected to hold bilateral and multilateral discussions with airport authorities, aviation agencies, development partners, financial institutions and industry stakeholders.

The proposed engagements will focus on technical assistance, operational support, logistics cooperation, capacity development, infrastructure advancement and institutional strengthening.

The Authority said it also plans to explore opportunities for investment, innovation, knowledge transfer and resource mobilization to support the development of Liberia’s airports.

Hughes Pursues Regional Aviation Cooperation

Beyond the ACI Africa conference, Hughes is undertaking separate engagements with key Nigerian aviation institutions, including the Nigeria Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN).

The discussions are intended to strengthen technical cooperation and secure logistical and capital support that could improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of Liberia’s aviation infrastructure.

The LAA said the engagements align with its broader objectives of strengthening aviation safety, advancing airport infrastructure development and building technical partnerships to support the long-term growth of the sector.

The Authority also views the conference as an opportunity to deepen regional integration, exchange best practices with other airport operators and explore emerging technologies that could support Liberia’s aviation modernization efforts.

LAA Links Participation to National Development

The Authority said its participation reflects its commitment to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s national development agenda, particularly in improving infrastructure, strengthening regional cooperation and expanding transportation connectivity.

ACI Africa, the regional arm of Airports Council International, represents African airports and promotes advocacy, capacity-building, innovation, connectivity and sustainable growth across the continent’s aviation industry.

The LAA said it remains committed to developing a modern, safe, secure, efficient and resilient airport system capable of supporting economic growth, trade, tourism and regional connectivity while improving services for the traveling public.

The press release did not specify the amount of funding or capital support being sought, identify any agreements finalized during the engagements, or provide a timeline for the anticipated infrastructure improvements.

World.title: Liberian Leader Demands Two Permanent African Seats On Security Council, Fairer Global Finance System
World.content:
UNITED NATIONS, New York – President Joseph Nyuma Boakai on Thursday night told world leaders that trust in the United Nations has been broken by the uneven application of its founding principles, and called for sweeping reforms of the Security Council and the global financial system to restore it.

By Rodney D Sieh, rodney,[email protected]

Addressing the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly, held under the theme “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All,” the Liberian leader said the world is facing “a lingering crisis of legitimacy and relevance that demands urgent attention.”

“Our answer to that fragmentation cannot be less multilateralism,” President Boakai declared. “It must be better multilateralism!”

‘Eighty years of patience is enough’

The President reserved his strongest words for the Security Council, noting that Africa, home to 1.5 billion people and nearly one-third of UN membership, still has no permanent seat, even though 80 percent of the Council’s mandates concern African peace and security.

“Eighty years of patience is enough. The time for structural reform is now,” he said, describing the imbalance as a “historical injustice” that “is no longer tenable.”

Reaffirming Liberia’s support for the Common African Position, President Boakai said Africa demands no fewer than two permanent seats with full rights, including the veto for as long as it exists, plus additional non-permanent seats. “Correcting this imbalance is not a favor to Africa,” he said. “It is necessary to restore the United Nations’ trust, credibility, and legitimacy.”

Security Council seat and the drug war

Speaking as a current member of the Security Council, the President highlighted threats facing West Africa, including transnational organized crime, cyber warfare and narcotics trafficking along maritime routes in the Gulf of Guinea.

He said Liberia’s Joint Security forces are “tightening the vise on transnational drug cartels,” but stressed that no nation can fight global criminal networks alone. He appealed to international partners for targeted support in coast guard surveillance, intelligence sharing and port security technology.

He also called for an immediate end to hostilities in conflict zones, unhindered humanitarian access and stronger investment in preventive diplomacy, arguing that “the cost of preventing a war pales in comparison to the cost of rebuilding a broken society.”

‘Governed by so few’

On the economy, President Boakai said developing nations are being “squeezed by unsustainable debt, shrinking fiscal space, and mounting external shocks” as the 2030 deadline for the Sustainable Development Goals approaches.

He called for structural reform of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, whose governance, he said, still reflects the world of 1945. “A financial system that decides the fate of billions cannot continue to be governed by so few,” he said.

At home, he pointed to progress under the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development – focused on Agriculture, Roads, Rule of Law, Education, Sanitation and Tourism – citing gains in revenue administration and rural farm-to-market roads. He also said his administration is strengthening accountability, financial management and the fight against corruption.

Climate justice, youth and AI

The President noted that Liberia contributes virtually nothing to global emissions yet suffers coastal erosion, flooding and disrupted farming seasons, while holding 42 percent of the remaining Upper Guinean Rainforest. He urged industrialized nations to honor their climate financing pledges and put loss-and-damage mechanisms into operation.

He called for investment in STEM education and digital skills for Africa’s youth, more than 60 percent of whom are under 25, reaffirmed Liberia’s commitment to equality for women and girls, and joined calls for binding rules on artificial intelligence, particularly in warfare. “Innovation must protect human development, not automate human destruction,” he said.

From San Francisco to today

Recalling that Liberia was one of only four African nations to sign the UN Charter in 1945, President Boakai presented the country’s journey from civil war to constitutional democracy as proof that “institutions can be rebuilt.”

He opened his address by congratulating Khalilur Rahman on his election as President of the 81st Session, thanking outgoing President Annalena Baerbock, and saluting Secretary-General António Guterres as he prepares to end his tenure.

“Let us leave this Assembly committed to a United Nations that not only deliberates on crises but also resolves them,” he concluded.

World.title: Liberia: Kwarbo vs. Coleman: The Drug Van Order that Nobody Owns
World.content:
A statement attributed to detained former Highway Patrol Chief Wadell Kwarbo says IG Gregory Coleman ordered him to escort the drug van. His family denies he made it, and the IG calls it part of a four-month disinformation campaign.

MONROVIA — A few days ago, Wadell Kwarbo’s father appeared on Spoon FM with an account of what his detained son had allegedly told him before he was taken into custody.

By Rodney D. Sieh

According to the father, a senior officer had called Kwarbo and instructed him to escort a shipment of drugs. At the time, he did not publicly identify the officer.

This week, however, a name emerged.

A statement attributed to Kwarbo, the former chief of the Liberia National Police Highway Patrol Division who remains detained at the Monrovia Central Prison, identified Police Inspector General Gregory O. W. Coleman as the officer who allegedly made the call.

“Police IG Gregory Coleman ordered me to escort the van. He instructed me to escort the drugs with my patrol vehicle (RL-141). And I acted on his order,” Kwarbo was quoted as saying on Spoon FM.

The statement reportedly went further, calling for his telephone records and written statement to be made available.

“Let them get my call log. My call log can be subpoenaed through the Court,” he was quoted as saying. “Let them release my written statement also. Why are they keeping it? They have it.”

But there is now a direct contradiction over whether Kwarbo actually made those statements.

Family: “He Never Made Such A Statement”

On Thursday, Kwarbo’s wife, Bendu Kwarbo, issued a statement on behalf of the family distancing her husband from the allegations against Coleman.

The family said it “categorically dissociates” Kwarbo from reports attributing the allegations to him and said neither the family nor his lawyers knew about or authorized any statement accusing the police chief.

“Mr. Kwarbo himself firmly rejects and denies this allegation in its entirety and maintains that he has made no such statement,” the family said.

The family said Kwarbo’s lawyers had advised him to remain silent and allow the court process to determine the case.

It described the statement circulating in his name as “malicious” and urged media organizations and the public to verify information before publishing or repeating allegations.

The family also maintains that Kwarbo should not have been arrested and that the case against him is based on what it described as false and misleading allegations.

Coleman: “Sustained Disinformation Campaign”

Coleman, meanwhile, has rejected the allegation and characterized it as part of what he says has been a prolonged campaign to undermine his credibility.

“For the past four months, I have been the target of a sustained disinformation campaign intended to damage my character and silence my fight against the culture of impunity, including the ongoing drug investigation,” Coleman said.

The police chief said freedom of expression must be respected but warned against spreading what he described as false information concerning an active criminal investigation.

“The facts must be established through evidence and lawful process. Anyone found to have broken the law must be held accountable under that same process,” Coleman said. “I will remain focused on my duty. I will not be intimidated.”

The US$ 317 Million Drug Case

The dispute comes against the backdrop of Liberia’s largest cocaine trafficking investigation, involving a shipment authorities have valued at approximately US$317 million.

Kwarbo, a former Highway Patrol chief, was stripped of his duties and later arrested and charged alongside Anthony T. Blaye, who served as Chief of the Liberia National Police Financial Crime Division.

The two have been accused of using marked police vehicles to escort a large cocaine shipment.

According to findings attributed to a joint Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency and Liberia National Police investigation, the cocaine was transported from a coastal landing site to a stash house using two police vehicles in an escort formation, with one vehicle reportedly positioned ahead of the shipment and another behind it.

Coleman said investigators uncovered evidence indicating that state security personnel played a role in moving the narcotics from the landing site to a holding location.

The foreign nationals, a Serbian and a Colombian, are being accused of bringing the cocaine into Liberia through aircraft and shoreline landing operations.

Liberian authorities publicly destroyed the seized cocaine on July 30 in what officials described as the country’s largest-ever drug destruction exercise.

Kwarbo’s Bail Fight

Kwarbo has denied wrongdoing and, in August, filed a motion seeking bail before Criminal Assizes “C” at the Temple of Justice.

His lawyers, including Cllr. Sayma Syrenius Cephus, maintain that he is being detained largely on allegations that he provided an escort to principal defendants after the alleged crimes had already been committed.

Kwarbo’s lawyers argue that the prosecution has not presented objective evidence placing him at the scene before or during the commission of the alleged offenses.

The defense has also challenged allegations attributed to co-defendant Christian Nyantee, arguing that Nyantee may have a motive to shift responsibility and that uncorroborated accomplice testimony should not be sufficient to establish the legal standard required for continued detention.

Kwarbo’s lawyers further contend that he had no prior knowledge of the alleged drug operation and that providing security escorts can form part of routine security duties during major national-security operations.

The Questions That Remain

The latest dispute leaves several questions unanswered.

It remains unclear who spoke to Spoon FM on Kwarbo’s behalf, whether the statement attributed to him was actually made by him, and how the statement emerged from the prison.

It is also unclear whether the written statement Kwarbo was quoted as referring to exists, what it contains, and whether investigators have sought or obtained his telephone records through the court.

Analysts say those questions may be resolved through evidence presented in court rather than competing accounts outside the courtroom.

For now, the public has two sharply different versions: one attributed to Kwarbo naming Coleman as the officer who allegedly ordered the escort, and another from Kwarbo’s family saying he never made the statement.

Kwarbo remains in detention and, under Liberia’s Constitution, is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

World.title: Liberia: Bail Denied, The Former Vice President’s Lawyers Weigh A Trip To The Supreme Court And a Long Legal Fight
World.content:
MONROVIA – For three weeks, the most important document at Jewel Howard-Taylor’s home has been a visitors’ log.

By Willie N. Tokpa

Every person who passes her gate is written down. Police officers stand watch around the clock. She may step outside only when the court has approved a trip to the hospital in advance. The former vice president, once second in line to lead the country, now needs a judge’s permission to see her doctor.

On Thursday, her lawyers went to court hoping to change that. They left with the same restrictions in place and a stinging rebuke from the bench.

By evening, the defense team had gathered in Monrovia to decide what comes next. For lawyers who have shifted strategy more than once in five weeks, the choices are narrowing. The road now leads up Capitol Hill, to the Supreme Court.

“We believe that she is eligible”

Atty. Gbawu Kowou, one of her lawyers, said the defense would take its case to the Justice in Chambers.

“The court argued that the crime extended up to 2026 based on the allegation that she received US$15,000. We disagree,” he told FrontPageAfrica. “The defense believes the court did not properly apply Liberia’s law on bail and pretrial detention, and that is the reason we are filing a petition for certiorari before the Justice in Chambers. We believe that she is eligible for bail.”

The papers are ready, he said. The team hopes to file on Friday, September 25, or by Monday, September 28 at the latest. Cllr. Kabina Ja’neh and former Associate Justice Lavalah Supuwood will lead the fight.

And the woman at the center of it? “The Vice President has been briefed on the latest decision from the court,” Kowou said.

A judge’s rebuke

The defense’s argument was simple. The 2023 Controlled Drugs and Substances Act makes the charges against her grave and non-bailable. But her lawyers said the conduct she is accused of happened in 2021 and 2022, before the law existed. A law, they argued, cannot reach back in time.

Judge Ousman F. Feika of Criminal Court “C” turned to the defense’s own paperwork to answer them.

Attached to their motion was the Writ of Arrest. It alleges that she received US$15,000 from the cartel through Sheikh Bashiru Kante as recently as August 2026. If true, the judge reasoned, the alleged conduct did not stop in 2022. It ran well past the new law.

Then he went further. He accused the defense of ignoring a major part of its own exhibit and warned that such conduct runs against the lawyers’ code of ethics. It is rare for a judge to scold counsel this way in a pretrial ruling.

Her lawyers noted their exception and told the court they would “take advantage of the statute controlling.” In Liberian courtrooms, everyone knows what that means: we’ll see you upstairs.

The road upstairs

The tool they will likely use is a writ of certiorari. Just last month, on August 28, the Supreme Court ruled in the Capitol arson case that certiorari is the proper way to challenge a trial judge’s interlocutory ruling. Chief Justice Yamie Quiqui Gbeisay explained that it lets the high court review a lower court that has jurisdiction but is alleged to have acted irregularly or contrary to law.

Recent history offers the defense both hope and caution.

In March 2025, Justice in Chambers Ceanneh Clinton Johnson overturned a Criminal Court “C” decision revoking the bail of Peach Bility, son of Representative Musa Hassan Bility, and sent him home.

Six years earlier, it went the other way. Justice Joseph Nagbe granted the State’s petition and overturned a trial judge who had found grounds to admit murder suspect Oliver Dillon to bail. Dillon stayed behind bars.

A filing could also buy time. In a 2024 case, the State’s certiorari petition automatically halted scheduled Criminal Court “C” proceedings until a conference with the Justice in Chambers. A similar pause here would freeze action before Judge Feika while the high court looks at his ruling.

Whatever the outcome, the question reaches beyond one defendant. The Justices may have to decide whether a no-bail law passed in 2023 can apply to conduct that allegedly began before it. Judge Feika’s order leaned on the continuing nature of the alleged offense and did not squarely answer that argument. The defense is likely to press the gap.

Waiting on the grand jury

Other fights remain unresolved. Judge Feika still has to rule on defense motions to quash the arrest writ, a habeas corpus petition and a motion to suppress evidence.

The defense has already shown it is willing to change course. On September 17, it withdrew the preliminary examination before Magistrate L. Ben Barco, giving up an early chance to test the State’s evidence. That evidence includes WhatsApp messages and audio recordings investigators say came from Kante’s phone. No one has yet heard them played in court.

And over all of it hangs the grand jury. Judge Feika can decide whether she goes home or stays confined. He cannot put her on trial without an indictment, and more than a month after her arrest, there is none.

Her allies have noticed. Lenn Eugene Nagbe, chief of staff to former President George Weah, said the government’s failure to indict her raises questions about the strength of its case.

The August Term of Court is in its 39th day of jury sitting. The clock is running.

The bigger picture

Her case sits at the heart of Liberia’s widest drug investigation. It began with a cocaine seizure valued at about US$317 million and has reached into the police, the intelligence services and the prison system.

Her party, the Coalition for Democratic Change, calls it political persecution. The government says she is presumed innocent and will have her day in court.

She was released from Monrovia Central Prison on medical grounds on September 4. The court has warned she could be sent back if her health improves significantly.

So she waits. Behind her gate, under guard, with each visitor’s name written in a book, while her lawyers climb the hill to argue that the case against her belongs to 2021, and the State insists it runs right up to this summer.

World.title: Chipolopolo fall in Algeria
World.content:
Captain Fashion Sakala was on target but Zambia launched the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign with a 3-1 loss to Algeria in Group I.

Algeria posted a well deserved win after dominating both halves at the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium.

The home side started on a promising note when Jaouen Hadjam opened the scoring just after two minutes.

Algeria went into the half time break leading 1-0 after wasting some decent chances.

Saudi Arabia based Sakala equalised 12 minutes after the break to make it 1-1.

But Algeria bounced back in front after 67 minutes when Ibrahim Maza beat Zambia keeper Willard Mwanza from inside the box.

Winger Anis Hadj Moussa sealed the win in the 72nd minute with Algeria’s third.

The result puts Algeria top of Group I on three points on goal difference after Match Day One, while Zambia are bottom.

In the other Group I match played today, Togo made a winning start with a 1-0 victory over Burundi at the Kégué Stadium in Lomé.

Karim Dermane scored the only goal in the 17th minute to give the Sparrow Hawks all three points.

Togo controlled the first half and held on in the second, with Burundi unable to find an equalizer.

Group I Table After Match Day 1:

1. Algeria – 3 pts (+2)

2. Togo – 3 pts (+1)

3. Burundi – 0 pts (-1)

4. Zambia – 0 pts (-2)

Togo now travel to face Zambia on 29th September, while Burundi host Algeria on the same day.

World.title: President Hichilema urges prudent use of public resources
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has sworn-in Patricia Malaila as Deputy Auditor General Audits, in the office of the Auditor General.

Speaking during the swearing-in-ceremony at State House, President Hichilema highlighted the significance of the utilisation of public resources and the timely delivery of audits.

“Accountability is crucial, all of us in public office must understand that we are accountable to the people of Zambia in what we do and superintending on resources that are available to us,” Mr Hichilema said.

President Hichilema further said the Office of Deputy Auditor General Audits, plays an important role to the citizens of Zambia.

The Head of State said accountability is crucial and everyone has a duty to comply with utilising resources in the most efficient and effective way.

“As Deputy Auditor General Audits, we expect you and your team to deliver audits on a timely basis,” Mr Hichilema said.

The President said audits should be delivered and concluded on time.

Mr Hichilema has since urged Ms Malaila to identify institutional weaknesses that require remedy, stating that this will help in the improvement of the use of public resources.

And newly sworn in Deputy Auditor General Audits, Patricia Malaila, said her office is committed to ensuring that real time audits are done.

“We will ensure that audits are done as an event is happening to prevent mistakes other than correcting after a mistake has been made,” Ms Malaila said.

Ms Malaila added that resources will be utilized accordingly, adding that every cent will be accounted for.

She said audits that will have an impact on the lives of people will be conducted so that the citizens can benefit.

World.title: Zambia records 16,500 new cancer cases annually
World.content:
University Teaching Hospital (UTH) Cancer Diseases Hospital (CDH) has disclosed that Zambia records approximately 16,500 new cancer cases and 9,700 cancer-related deaths annually, with cervical cancer accounting for the highest number of cases.

UTH-CDH Acting Senior Medical Superintendent, Paul Kamfwa, says the country records about 4,700 new cervical cancer cases every year, with more than half of the affected patients dying from the disease.

Dr Kamfwa made the remarks during a community cleaning exercise conducted by Zambia Correctional Service Officers to commemorate Africa Corrections Day at the Cancer Diseases Hospital in Lusaka.

He disclosed that about 3,000 of the 16,500 cancer patients recorded countrywide are currently receiving treatment at the hospital.

Meanwhile, Zambia Correctional Service Commissioner-General, Fredrick Chilukutu said the Service is committed to community engagement as part of efforts to promote safer and more resilient communities.

Mr Chilukutu, represented by ZCS Deputy Commissioner-General, Crispin Kaonga said correctional facilities should not only focus on custody but also equip inmates with skills, healthcare, education and opportunities for successful reintegration into society.

He also highlighted the need to strengthen healthcare services in correctional facilities through medical screening, disease prevention, health education and access to treatment.

Mr Chilukutu said the Service is placing greater emphasis on the mental health and overall well-being of inmates and correctional officers.

He has called for continued collaboration among government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations and regional correctional services to improve correctional management.

World.title: 14th National Assembly official opening slated for Friday
World.content:
The ceremonial official opening of the first session of the 14th National Assembly by President Hakainde Hichilema will take place on Friday, October ninth, 2026, at Parliament Buildings, in Lusaka.

In his address to the National Assembly, President Hichilema is expected to give policy direction for the country for the year 2026/2027.

Clerk of the National Assembly, Loveness Mayaka announced and confirmed the development in a statement Issued to the media in Lusaka today.

Ms Mayaka stated that Members of Parliament will, thereafter, proceed to debate policy pronouncements contained in President Hichilema’s speech.

The Clerk further called on all stakeholders and the general public to follow the live proceedings of the National Assembly on Parliament radio and Television as well as other National Assembly online platforms.

World.title: President Hichilema swears in Deputy Auditor General
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has sworn in Patricia Malaila, as Deputy Auditor General Audits, in the office of the Auditor General at State House today.

During the swearing in ceremony at State House, President Hichilema highlighted the significance of the utilisation of public resources and the timely delivery of audits.

“Accountability is crucial, all of us in public office must understand that we are accountable to the people of Zambia in what we do and superintending on resources that are availed to us,” President Hichilema said.

President Hichilema further said that the Office of Deputy Auditor General Audits plays an important role to the citizens of Zambia.

The Head of State added that the Government is open to bring in skills and expertise from across the country.

He noted that accountability is crucial and everyone has a duty to comply with utilising resources in the most efficient and effective way.

“As Deputy Auditor General Audits, we expect you and your team to deliver audits on a timely basis,’” President Hichilema said.

The President said that audits should be delivered and concluded on time.

Mr Hichilema has since urged Ms Malaila to identify institutional weaknesses that require remedy, adding that this will help in the improvement of the use of public resources.

And the newly sworn in Deputy Auditor General Audits, Patricia Malaila says that her office is committed to ensuring that real time audits are done.

“We will ensure that audits are done as an event is happening to prevent mistakes other than correcting after a mistake has been made,” Ms Malaila said.

Ms Malaila added that resources will be utilised accordingly, adding that every cent will be accounted for.

She said audits that will have an impact on the lives of people will be conducted so that the citizens can benefit.

The President is mandated by the Constitution of Zambia to appoint office bearers with the respective articles of the Constitution thereof.

World.title: Increased allocation to early Childhood Education elates ZANEC
World.content:
The Zambia National Education Coalition (ZANEC) has welcomed the increased allocation to early Childhood Education in the 2026 National budget from two point five percent in 2025 to three percent in 2026.

Speaking during the policy forum on advocating for appropriate Early Childhood Education (ECE) Legislation, policies and structures in Lusaka, ZANEC Board Chairperson, Henry Kabwe, noted that the increment signals growing Government attention to foundational learning and investment in the early years of a child.

Mr Kabwe noted that his institution recognises the construction of Early Childhood Education Centers under the Zambia Education Enhancement Project as a vital step towards expanding access to safe and appropriate learning spaces for young children.

He added that increased investment can only deliver tangible results only if it is matched by effective implementation, quality assurance and accountability.

Mr Kabwe however noted that there are some challenges that seem to limit the reach and quality of Early Child Education such as, inadequate and unsustainable public financing, limited Implementation of inclusive education, inequitable access to quality ECE services and weak Coordination among sectors.

The Board Chairperson stated that these challenges require more than policy commitments but legislation, adequate and sustainable financing and strong accountability mechanisms.

Mr Kabwe, further disclosed that at the end of the ZANEC discussion with its stakeholders, a shared understanding of the current state of early Childhood education in Zambia, identification of key policy and implementation gaps, strengthened attention to vulnerable children should be reached.

He revealed that he expects that greater accountability and coordination, clear and practical advocacy priorities and recommendations should be highlighted and addressed in the meeting.

And UNICEF Zambia’s Early Childhood Development Education Specialist, Zewelanji Serpell said the increase in the budget allocation from the current three percent of the education budget to at least 10 percent is critical to expanding access and improving the quality of early childhood education.

Ms Serpell noted that her organisaton is working with the Ministry of Education, particularly the Early Childhood Education Directorate, to support the construction of stand-alone ECE centers, production of teaching and learning materials, and teacher training and capacity building.

She added that through funding from the European Union, her organisation has since supported the construction of stand-alone ECE centers in North-Western and Luapula Provinces, while also partnering with the Ministry in the production of materials to support the implementation of quality ECE.

She further reiterated that her organisation will continue to work with the Government to strengthen ECE, including supporting the implementation of the new ECE curriculum and advocacy for increased investment, so that every Zambian child can access quality early childhood education.

World.title: Nkandu condemns Kalumba’s remarks against President Hichilema
World.content:
United Party for National Development (UPND) National Management Committee Member, Elvis Nkandu has condemned remarks attributed to former Minister of Finance, Katele Kalumba against President Hakainde Hichilema.

In a statement Issued to the media in Lusaka, Mr Nkandu indicated that such remarks are deeply regrettable and unbefitting to Zambia’s political discourse.

He noted that while citizens enjoy constitutional freedoms of expression, such rights must be exercised with responsibility and respect for state institutions, particularly the Presidency.

Mr Nkandu said it is unfortunate that Dr Kalumba, a former senior public servant, would resort to language intended to demean the Head of State despite having personally benefited from the President’s compassion.

He recalled that Dr Kalumba was pardoned on medical grounds in 2023 after serving a conviction linked to offences under the former MMD administration.

Mr Nkandu stressed that President Hichilema’s decision to extend clemency was an act of humanity and not weakness, which should have been met with gratitude rather than disrespect.

“The President extended mercy when mercy was sought. The least that can be expected in return is respect for the institution of the Presidency and for the people who entrusted President Hichilema with leadership,’’ he stated.

Mr Nkandu further warned against attempts to inject regionalism into political debate, saying Zambia’s unity must not be undermined by divisive rhetoric.

“Zambia belongs to all of us, and the Presidency belongs to all Zambians,” he emphasised.

He also urged political actors to demonstrate maturity following the 2026 elections, reminding them that disagreement does not equate to enmity.

Mr Nkandu stressed that criticism of government policies is legitimate, but reckless allegations and insults against the Presidency threaten national cohesion.

“As a member of the UPND National Management Committee, I will continue to defend democratic values, including respect for constitutional institutions, national unity, human dignity and the rule of law,’’ Mr Nkandu affirmed.

He called on Dr Kalumba to reflect on his public standing and contribute constructively to national dialogue, stressing that Zambia’s unity is greater than any individual politician or party.

World.title: Chongwe Mayor leads a Market clean-up exercise
World.content:
Chongwe Mayor, Frederick Sashi has led a clean-up exercise at Mwalubemba Market in Chinkuli Ward as part of the Council’s ongoing Keep Chongwe Green, Clean and Healthy campaign.

The exercise brought together Councilor for Chinkuli Ward Moses Banda, the Council’s Public Health Team and employees from various departments, who worked together to remove waste and improve sanitation at the market.

Mr Sashi said maintaining clean trading spaces was important in safeguarding public health and creating a conducive environment for both traders and customers.

The Mayor also toured the market to assess compliance with Council regulations and engaged shop owners and bicycle operators on the need to operate with valid licences and adhere to the required standards.

He urged traders and other business operators to take responsibility for keeping their surroundings clean and comply with Council regulations to promote order, safety and responsible trading.

Mr Sashi also encouraged residents, business persons, marketeers and other stakeholders to participate in maintaining clean, green and healthy communities as part of efforts to improve sanitation and public health across Chongwe District.

During the exercise, Council teams removed accumulated waste that had remained at the market for an extended period, restoring cleanliness in various parts of the trading area.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 25, 2026
World.content:
press review

Uganda Begins $121M South Sudan Power Interconnection Project

Uganda has commenced implementation of the South Sudan-Uganda Power Interconnection Project (SUPIP) after securing US$121 million from the African Development Fund (ADF) to finance the Ugandan component of the regional electricity initiative. Combined with counterpart funding from the Ugandan government, the financing will support the construction of high-voltage transmission infrastructure linking Uganda's electricity grid to South Sudan. The project is expected to facilitate cross-border electricity trade, strengthen Uganda's northern transmission network, and provide South Sudan with access to more reliable and affordable power.

Malawi's Electoral Body Under Fire Over Relocation to Blantyre



The Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) is facing pressure over plans to relocate to Blantyre - the country's commercial capital - alongside a string of staff union grievances that risk undermining public confidence in the body ahead of upcoming elections. An executive order directed MEC to move its headquarters back to Blantyre after it had relocated to Lilongwe in June 2023 to be closer to the seat of government. The commission's staff union has demanded an urgent meeting with leadership, citing unresolved issues surrounding the relocation and lease uncertainties.

Liberian Govt Says Cybercrime Law Doesn't Target Free Speech

Senator Francis Dopoh has reassured Liberians - particularly journalists, activists, and social media users - that the newly enacted cybercrime law is not intended to suppress criticism or peaceful dissent. This clarification follows the recent arrest of an individual over a social media post, which sparked public debate about the legislation. Dopoh said the law instead targets behaviors posing direct threats to individuals, institutions, and national security. He added that its protections for women, girls, and children will help combat online threats, blackmail, and the non-consensual sharing of private images.

Zimbabwe Parliament Wants State of Emergency Over Harare Sewage Crisis

Harare is facing a public health crisis as raw sewage continues flowing into rivers feeding Lake Chivero, the capital's main water source, according to a parliamentary committee report. The report paints a grim picture of Zimbabwe's deteriorating wastewater management system, stating that only 20 of the country's 63 sewage treatment plants are currently operational. Active plants discharge an estimated 570 megaliters of raw sewage daily, worsening pollution levels across major water sources.

World.title: Nigeria: 'Dangote Refinery IPO Opens Ownership to Nigerian Investors'
World.content:
Nigerians can invest in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals with a minimum subscription of N5,250 under an initial public offering launched recently. The company is offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 each. The offer, valued at about N2.15 trillion if fully subscribed, opened September 14 and is scheduled to close October 13.

FCMB Group Chief Executive, Ladi Balogun, said the offer gives Nigerians access to a world-scale business while demonstrating the growing reach of the country's capital market.

"It presents an opportunity for every Nigerian to experience the benefits of investing in world-class and world-scale businesses that would otherwise be inaccessible,"Balogun said at the opening gong ceremony and Facts Behind the Offer presentation at the Nigerian Exchange in Lagos.

Balogun said Nigeria's capital market was deepening as it attracted retail, high-net-worth, institutional and international investors through a widening range of channels.



"Retail investors are buying shares on their mobile phones through fintechs, banks and brokers," he said. "High-net-worth individuals and institutional investors such as pension funds are bringing depth to the market, while international investors are bringing scale." He said the breadth of participation demonstrated the market's capacity to help credible Nigerian companies raise capital at scale. Balogun also described the refinery as largely insulated from the macroeconomic and currency risks associated with the Nigerian economy.

"The number of such companies on our Exchange is growing," he said. "This indicates the potential and direction of the Nigerian economy."

World.title: Niger: Canadians, Australians and Americans Relaunch Niger's Uranium Industry
World.content:
Niamey — Niger's military junta is seeking to relaunch the country's uranium mining industry with the signing of an agreement with Australian company Atomic Eagle, through which the State of Niger has established the Madaouela Mining Company (MAMICO). The company, 60% owned by Atomic Eagle and 40% by the Nigerien State, plans to revive uranium mining operations in Agadez, in the central-northern part of the country.

The agreement provides for an initial royalty payment of 10 million US dollars, as well as investments in local development and in strengthening the capacity of the mining administration. According to the Ministry of Mines, the project should also create around 1,000 jobs for young Nigeriens.

Madaouela has a resource of 52,843 tonnes of uranium oxide, an estimate based on exploration carried out by the previous licence holder, GoviEx Uranium Inc., which obtained the licence in 2016.



The agreement settles the dispute that arose following the expropriation of the project from GoviEx in 2024. GoviEx and Tombador Iron merged in November 2025, creating Atomic Eagle. Under the agreement reached, the new company will withdraw its arbitration proceedings within seven days of the signing of the agreement.

The pact signed with the Australian company came just days after Canadian mining company Global Atomic obtained approval from the Board of Directors of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) for debt financing of up to 414.2 million US dollars for its Dasa uranium mine project, also in the Agadez region.

The Dasa deposit is operated by Société Minière de Dasa (SOMIDA), a Niger-based company 80% owned by Global Atomic and 20% by the Nigerien government. Discovered in 2010 and authorized in 2020, the deposit has been under mining activity since 2022, but its full development has been subject to several delays. The completion of the mine is now expected in the first half of 2028, with commissioning scheduled for the second half of the year.

Niger's mining sector was historically dominated by French industry, first Areva and subsequently Orano. Niamey nationalized the local subsidiary amid deteriorating relations with France and closer ties with Russia. Orano, 90% owned by the French State, has launched several legal actions against Niger, accusing the authorities of confiscating its assets in the country.

Despite the Russian presence in the country and the insecurity caused by jihadist groups, Anglo-Saxon mining companies do not appear to be facing particular obstacles in investing in Niger's uranium sector.

World.title: Nigeria: Nigeria, U.S. Sign Framework to Attract Investment Into $700bn Mineral Resources
World.content:
Nigeria's Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US Deputy Secretary of State, Christopher Landau.

The framework is expected to use the relationship between the Nigerian and US governments as a foundation for business-to-business transactions and investment across Nigeria's mineral value chain.

Nigeria and the United States have signed a framework aimed at attracting American investment into Nigeria's estimated $700 billion mineral resources.

The agreement was signed on behalf of the governments of the two countries by Nigeria's Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US Deputy Secretary of State, Christopher Landau, on Wednesday at Nigeria's Mission House in New York.

According to a statement by Kehinde Bamigbetan, Special Adviser to the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, the signing took place on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.



The framework is expected to use the relationship between the Nigerian and US governments as a foundation for business-to-business transactions and investment across Nigeria's mineral value chain.

It covers cooperation in geological data and exploration, mineral development and processing, infrastructure and technical capacity.

Speaking at the ceremony, Mr Alake said the agreement represented a shift from Nigeria's traditional role as an exporter of raw minerals towards greater domestic value addition.

"Some agreements manage the present, and some agreements shape the future. The framework we sign today belongs to the second kind," Mr Alake said.

He said Nigeria and the US shared the view that supply chains for critical minerals must be secure, resilient and supported by responsible investment.

"But let me be clear about Nigeria's ambition. We are not here to remain a source of raw material for the values that others create. Our goal is to turn potential into lasting value at home through stronger local processing, new skills, quality jobs, and new opportunities for Nigerian businesses," he said.

According to the minister, the framework would enable both countries to collaborate on exploration, mineral development and processing, infrastructure and technical capacity.

He said its implementation would support the economic diversification objectives of President Bola Tinubu's administration and promote industrial growth.

Mr Alake, however, said the signing was only the beginning of the process.

"Now comes the harder and more important work: moving from agreement to implementation. A signature is a promise, results are the proof," he said.

He added that Nigeria would, in the coming months, identify viable projects, mobilise investments and establish commercial partnerships capable of delivering measurable benefits to both countries.

US pledges partnership

Mr Landau said the United States regarded Nigeria as a strategic partner, describing the country as a regional power because of its population and economic position.

He said the agreement would create opportunities for greater prosperity in both countries and reaffirmed the US commitment to supporting Nigeria's economic growth.

"The signal we are sending is that the United States and Nigeria are partners," he said.

Mr Landau said the two countries had undertaken several initiatives under Presidents Donald Trump and Bola Tinubu over the previous one and a half years, adding that Washington wanted to build on the momentum.

The US delegation included the Deputy Assistant Secretary for West African Affairs, Rich Michaels; Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Southern Africa, Foreign Assistance and Critical Minerals, Chris Kulukundis; Senior Policy Adviser to the Deputy Secretary, Wyatt Toehlkeke; and Jitu Sardar.

Sanwo-Olu, other Nigerian officials attend

Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu witnessed the signing alongside the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development, Yusuf Yabo; Director-General of the Nigerian Mining Cadastral Office, Simon Nkom; Executive Secretary of the Solid Minerals Development Fund, Fatima Shinkafi; and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Solid Minerals Company, Martin Imonitie.

Close 

Governor Sanwo-Olu later said on X that he was present at the Mission House when Nigeria and the US signed an important framework for investment in Nigeria's mining sector.

"The focus of the framework is to move beyond simply exporting raw materials by building a stronger local value chain through processing, exploration, better infrastructure and technical capacity.

"This will help us turn Nigeria's mineral wealth into lasting growth and support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's Renewed Hope Agenda to diversify our economy.

He said the initiative could help convert Nigeria's mineral resources into economic opportunities and support the federal government's economic diversification agenda.

World.title: Tanzania: Cash Still King in Public Transport Despite Four-Year Digital Push
World.content:
Dar es Salaam — CASH remains overwhelmingly king across Tanzania's public transport sector, with electronic transactions accounting for only 6.8 per cent of fares collected over the past four years, official data show.

Land Transport Regulatory Authority (LATRA) Director General Habibu Suluo said yesterday that 62.18 million passengers were recorded through online ticketing systems during the four-year period, of whom 59.27 million, equivalent to 95.3 per cent, paid their fares in cash. Only 2.91 million passengers, or 4.7 per cent, used digital payment channels, he said.

In monetary terms, cash payments accounted for 1.99tri/- of the 2.13tri/- collected, while electronic payments amounted to 144.28bn/-, representing 6.8 per cent of the total.



The figures highlight the gap between the policy drive towards digital payments and their adoption across the transport sector, despite requirements for electronic transactions in several services.

The requirements, backed by the Electronic Transactions Act (Cap. 442), cover bus rapid transit services, long distance buses, ferries and ride-hailing platforms.

Mr Suluo acknowledged the challenges of increasing digital adoption, but said operators and the government were gradually recognising the transparency benefits of electronic payment systems.

Beyond digital payments, LATRA reported significant growth in the regulated transport sector during the sixth phase government's tenure.

Commercial vehicle licences increased by 146.1 per cent, from 239,953 in 2021/22 to 590,468 in 2025/26, he said.

The number of buses connected to LATRA's Vehicle Tracking System also rose from 5,979 to 14,743 during the same period.

Turning to road safety during the rainy season, Mr Suluo urged transport stakeholders to prepare for anticipated El Niño rains and ensure vehicles were properly maintained before starting journeys.

He said vehicle owners should pay particular attention to braking systems, tyres, lights, windscreens and windscreen wipers.

"Heavy rains could cause flooding, water to overflow across roads, slippery surfaces, soil erosion, landslides and rockfalls, damage to roads, strong winds and fog, all of which could compromise road safety," he said.

Mr Suluo urged drivers to avoid flooded areas, particularly where water was flowing rapidly or its depth was unknown and to reduce speed and increase following distances during rain, fog and other periods of poor visibility.

He also advised drivers to exercise greater caution in areas affected by landslides, erosion, cracks or damaged road edges.

Passengers, he said, should check weather forecasts and road-condition updates before travelling and avoid unnecessary journeys during heavy rains.

World.title: Africa: Nigeria Demands Two Permanent UN Seats, Veto Powers for Africa
World.content:
Nigeria has demanded at least two permanent seats for Africa on the UN Security Council, with veto powers for as long as the privilege exists.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima made the demand while delivering President Bola Tinubu's national statement at the 81st UN General Assembly in New York.

He also demanded five non-permanent seats for Africa, in line with the continent's longstanding common position on reforming the Security Council.

Shettima said the Council's present configuration no longer reflected contemporary geopolitical realities and weakened the legitimacy of global decision-making.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The world of 2026 cannot remain captive to the distribution of power in 1945," he said.

He said Africa could no longer remain outside permanent membership while issues concerning the continent continued to occupy substantial attention of the Council.

According to him, Nigeria's position is consistent with the Ezulwini Consensus and Sirte Declaration, adopted as the Common African Position.

Under the position, Africa seeks at least two permanent seats with all existing privileges, alongside five non-permanent seats on the Council.

The African Union reaffirmed the demand in May, saying Africa's exclusion from permanent representation constituted a historical imbalance requiring correction.

Shettima argued that institutions claiming authority to act for humanity must adequately reflect the people on whose behalf decisions are taken.

He linked Security Council reform to efforts to restore confidence in multilateralism amid widening geopolitical divisions.

The Vice-President also reaffirmed Nigeria's commitment to the UN Charter and international cooperation.

He said Nigeria supported an international system where diplomacy takes precedence over coercion and international law guides relations among states.

Shettima recalled Nigeria's contributions to international and regional peace operations in Liberia, Sierra Leone, Darfur, Mali and The Gambia.

He said Nigeria also continues to work through ECOWAS, the African Union and Gulf of Guinea mechanisms.

According to him, these efforts cover mediation, counter-terrorism, democratic governance and maritime security.

Shettima said persistent conflicts across different regions underscored the need to return to dialogue, collective responsibility and peaceful settlement of disputes.

Close 

He identified the conflict in Sudan and other theatres as requiring urgent diplomacy because of their humanitarian, economic and geopolitical consequences.

The Vice-President also warned against a global environment where propaganda blurred distinctions between victims and aggressors and complicated accountability.

He maintained that an inclusive and effective UN remained indispensable to global peace and sustainable development.

Nigeria's demand comes amid renewed calls by African leaders for reforms to an institution whose permanent membership remains unchanged since its creation.

The Security Council has five permanent members: China, France, Russia, the UK and the US, each possessing veto power.

Africa currently has no permanent representative on the Council.

The African Union's preferred reform model provides for at least two permanent African seats, including veto privileges while existing members retain them.

The reform model also seeks five non-permanent seats for Africa.

Shettima said Nigeria remained committed to a multilateral order capable of responding more credibly to 21st-century realities.

According to him, differences among nations must not obscure their common humanity or responsibility to preserve peace for future generations. (NAN)

World.title: Liberia: 'Not Built to Silence Free Speech': Govt Defends Cybercrime Law
World.content:
River Gee County Senator Francis Saidy Dopoh II has moved to reassure Liberians, particularly journalists, activists and social-media users, that Liberia's newly enacted Cybercrime Act is not intended to suppress criticism, journalism or peaceful dissent, insisting that the law is targeted at cyber-related threats and abuse rather than legitimate expression.

"On free speech, let me be clear: this law has no intent to silence free speech," Dopoh said in a statement defending the legislation he helped champion through the Liberian Senate.

The River Gee County Senator, who chairs the Senate Committee on Posts and Telecommunications and is also the sponsor of Liberia's Data Protection Act, said the Cybercrime Act of 2025 should not be viewed as a tool for restricting the constitutional rights of Liberians to express opinions or criticize government.



Instead, he said, the legislation is intended to address conduct that poses identifiable threats to individuals, institutions and national security in Liberia's rapidly expanding digital environment.

The law was approved by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai on July 3, 2026, after more than four years of legislative consideration. The Executive Mansion subsequently published the legislation, while the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications has listed the printed Cybercrime Act among Liberia's approved Acts.

Dopoh's intervention comes amid heightened public interest in how the new law will affect online speech, particularly as Liberians increasingly use Facebook, WhatsApp, TikTok and other digital platforms for political debate, journalism, business and civic engagement.

The senator said the law is not directed at "honest opinion, criticism of government, journalism or peaceful dissent."

Rather, he identified threats of violence, harassment, incitement to violence, fraud and the exploitation of children as among the conduct the law is intended to address.

The distinction is significant because the Cybercrime Act contains provisions dealing with online communications, including cyberstalking, incitement, harmful data messages and the non-consensual distribution of intimate images.

Under the Act, cyberstalking provisions address specified communications intended to bully, threaten or harass another person where the communication places that person in fear of death, violence or bodily injury. The law also addresses certain threats involving kidnapping, injury and extortion.

The Act further criminalizes certain forms of communication intended to incite property damage or violence.

Another provision addresses the intentional distribution of harmful data messages, while a separate section criminalizes the non-consensual distribution of intimate images through a computer system.

The legislation also provides a mechanism through which a person who believes prohibited material is being distributed can seek a court order to prevent further distribution or require the removal or disabling of access to the material.

For Dopoh, however, these provisions should not be interpreted as a general restriction on speech.

He argued that the legislation is designed to protect citizens from forms of digital abuse that can cause tangible harm while maintaining the rights of individuals to participate in public debate.

The senator specifically pointed to the law's potential benefits for women, girls and children, saying it will help address online threats, blackmail and the sharing of private images without consent.

The legislation also covers a broader range of cyber offences unrelated to speech, including unauthorized access to computer systems, unlawful interception, interference with computer data and computer systems, computer-related fraud and forgery, identity theft and child sexual exploitation material.

Dopoh said these provisions are necessary as Liberia becomes increasingly dependent on digital platforms for financial transactions, communication and the delivery of essential services.

"It protects your money, including mobile money, bank accounts and online payments, from fraud and scams," he said.

He also identified banks, telecommunications companies, utilities and hospitals as institutions that require protection from cyber threats because of their importance to the functioning of the Liberian economy and public services.

But it is the law's implementation that Dopoh says will determine whether its objectives are achieved without undermining citizens' rights.

He is calling on the Executive and implementing agencies to establish the institutional structures required under the legislation, including the Liberia National Cybersecurity Center (LNCC) and the Liberia Cybersecurity Emergency Response Team (LCERT).

He wants the government to establish a 24-hour contact point for cybersecurity emergencies and issue the Presidential Order designating Liberia's Critical National Information Infrastructure.

Dopoh is also urging the government to issue clear implementation guidelines, train law-enforcement officers and other relevant officials, and publish regulations required under the Act within the prescribed timeframe.

He further called for dedicated funding and a nationwide public-awareness campaign to ensure that Liberians understand the law before it is aggressively enforced.

The demand for public education is particularly relevant to the free-speech debate because much of the law's impact will depend on how law-enforcement authorities, prosecutors and courts distinguish legitimate online expression from criminal conduct.

Liberia's Constitution guarantees freedom of expression and freedom of the press under Article 15, making the manner in which the Cybercrime Act is enforced a matter of importance to journalists and other public communicators.

Dopoh said the legislation itself provides for prosecutions to be conducted in accordance with human rights standards and said people who report cybersecurity violations in good faith should also receive protection.

His position places the emphasis on enforcement rather than merely the wording of the legislation.

For journalists, the practical question will be how provisions concerning harmful messages, threats, harassment and incitement are applied when online commentary involves public officials, political disputes or controversial issues.

For ordinary users, the law introduces a clearer legal framework around conduct that previously could be difficult to address, particularly cyber-enabled fraud, identity theft, online threats and the distribution of intimate material without consent.

Close 

Dopoh said the law should ultimately help create a safer digital environment in which Liberians can participate in online commerce and communication without becoming victims of cybercrime.

He also linked cybersecurity to economic confidence, arguing that stronger digital protections can help attract investment and support job creation.

The senator said Liberia cannot fully participate in the modern digital economy without establishing stronger protections for its information systems, financial platforms and critical infrastructure.

But he maintained that cybersecurity and civil liberties should not be treated as competing objectives.

The challenge, therefore, will be ensuring that the law is enforced against genuine cybercrime while legitimate political criticism, journalism, civic advocacy and peaceful dissent remain protected.

Dopoh urged Liberians to familiarize themselves with the new law and understand both their rights and responsibilities.

"To every citizen: learn the law, use the internet responsibly, and report abuse," he said.

He added that Liberia's goal should be a digital environment where citizens can conduct business, communicate and express themselves without fear of cyber threats.

"Let us build a Liberia where every person can go online safely, do business with confidence, and speak their mind without fear of threats," Dopoh concluded.

World.title: Uganda: Uganda Begins $121m South Sudan Power Interconnection Project
World.content:
Uganda has commenced implementation of the South Sudan-Uganda Power Interconnection Project (SUPIP) after securing UA 91.7 million, equivalent to about US$121 million, from the African Development Fund (ADF) to finance the Ugandan component of the regional electricity project.

The financing, together with counterpart funding from the Ugandan Government, will support the construction of high-voltage transmission infrastructure linking Uganda's electricity grid to South Sudan.

The project is expected to facilitate cross-border electricity trade, strengthen Uganda's transmission network in the north and provide South Sudan with access to more reliable and potentially lower-cost electricity.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The Government, through the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD), in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, Uganda Electricity Transmission Company Limited (UETCL) and the African Development Bank Group (AfDB), held the technical launch of Uganda's component of SUPIP.

The milestone follows the fulfilment of conditions required for the ADF financing to become effective and for the first disbursement to Uganda, as well as the establishment of the Project Implementation Team.

Power trade between Uganda and South Sudan

According to Baba Fataja of the African Development Bank, the bank financed studies that paved the way for the proposed interconnection, which is intended to establish an electricity trading link between the two countries.

Fataja said South Sudan continues to face challenges in accessing reliable electricity, with heavy dependence on diesel-powered generation contributing to high electricity costs.

"South Sudan is really struggling to have a reliable supply of electricity, which is very expensive because they depend on diesel," Fataja said.

He said the interconnection would provide South Sudan with an opportunity to access electricity from Uganda while creating an additional market for Uganda's available generation capacity.

"With the cooperation of the two countries, there is an opportunity for them to get a cheaper source of energy from Uganda, and at the same time Uganda can export excess energy that they produce," he said.

Fataja added that the project could eventually contribute to wider regional electricity trading as additional countries become interconnected.

299-kilometre transmission line

SUPIP is designed to integrate South Sudan into the Eastern Africa Power Pool (EAPP), supporting regional electricity trade and allowing participating countries to share available generation capacity.

The overall project involves the construction of approximately 299 kilometres of 400-kilovolt double-circuit transmission line between Olwiyo in Uganda and Juba/Gumbo in South Sudan, together with associated substations and supporting infrastructure.

Uganda's component will cover approximately 150 kilometres of 400kV transmission line.

This will include about 118 kilometres from Olwiyo Substation to Bibia and a further 32 kilometres from Bibia to the South Sudan border.

The Ugandan component will also include construction of a new 400/132/33kV Bibia Substation, upgrading of the existing Olwiyo Substation to 400/132/33kV and extension of the Karuma Substation to facilitate the evacuation of electricity from Karuma towards Olwiyo.

Daniel Okelo, Head of Grid Development and Planning at the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development, said implementation of the project is expected to run from 2026 to 2029.

The infrastructure is expected to strengthen Uganda's northern transmission network and improve the country's capacity to move electricity to regional markets.

For South Sudan, the interconnection is expected to reduce reliance on costly fossil-fuel-based electricity generation and improve access to electricity for households, businesses, industries and public institutions.

For Uganda, the project is expected to create an additional regional market for electricity generated domestically, particularly during periods when generation capacity exceeds local demand.

Increased electricity exports could also generate additional revenue while strengthening Uganda's participation in the regional electricity market.

With financing conditions now fulfilled, implementation will focus on activities required to advance the project towards construction.

These include mobilisation of the Project Supervision and Management Consultant, completion of environmental and social safeguard requirements, including the Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), finalisation of the transmission route and procurement of Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) contractors.

Close 

Uganda and South Sudan will coordinate the procurement and implementation of the cross-border infrastructure, while each government will remain responsible for its respective component.

The technical launch also brought together implementing institutions and development partners to align on financial management, procurement, environmental and social safeguards, monitoring, reporting and coordination arrangements.

Officials clarified that the technical launch should not be confused with the full ceremonial launch of the regional project, which is expected to take place at a later stage after further progress has been made on procurement and other implementation activities.

The African Development Fund financing for Uganda forms part of a broader financing arrangement involving the two governments and development partners. The South Sudan component is also receiving co-financing support involving the European Union.

Once completed, the interconnection is expected to strengthen electricity connectivity between Uganda and South Sudan and contribute to the broader development of regional power trading under the Eastern Africa Power Pool.

World.title: Reigning champion Indiana Hoosiers survive major scare from Northwestern in Big Ten opener
World.content:
The reigning National Champion Indiana Hoosiers haven't been tested much this season, and boy, did they ever get a test on Friday night.

Despite being three-touchdown favorites, the Hoosiers found themselves battling the Northwestern Wildcats to the very end, eking out a 29-23 win at home.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Coming into Friday night's game, the Hoosiers — despite getting off to a 3-0 start on the heels of a title — had dealt with one big criticism dogging them this season.

Slow starts.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Head coach Curt Cignetti had to field questions about his team's play early in games against easier opponents.

So, there was a lot of focus on whether or not that trend would continue as the Big Ten schedule got underway against the Wildcats.

Well, the answer was... kind of?

The Hoosiers opened the game with a 15-play, 67-yard drive that ate up around half of the opening quarter.

However, the slow-start bug showed up again when a drive that should’ve ended with points on the board was instead capped by a huge defensive play from Northwestern.

The Indiana defense managed to bail out the boys on the other side of the ball when Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles fumbled a snap before getting brought down in his own end zone for a safety.

The Hoosiers battled through an unusual first half with an offense that looked a little disjointed at times and more penalties than you typically see out of them.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Worse, they suffered a big blow later in the half when running back Turbo Richard was hit late after going out of bounds and went straight to the locker room.

There was no call on the play, which made a call against Indiana on a similar play moments later very unpopular with the folks at Memorial Stadium.

Indiana tacked on a touchdown and extra point to take a 12-0 lead to the locker room at the half; of course, it didn't hurt that Northwestern rushed for -5 yards through thirty minutes.

But just over halfway through the third quarter, Northwestern paid their first visit to the red zone and managed to get rid of that goose egg.

Chiles wrapped up that drive, despite suffering what sure appeared to be a dislocated finger, and led the Wildcats to the first points Indiana had allowed since their season opener.

And the Wildcats weren't done, with Chiles hitting Griffin Wilde in the back of the end zone at the start of the fourth quarter for an unbelievable touchdown.

Northwestern head coach David Braun opted to go for two and try to tie it up, but the Hoosiers thwarted them on their first and then their second attempts after a penalty.

Indiana answered back with a scoring drive of their own, with Lee Beebe Jr. — who handled most of the legwork after Richard's exit — putting the Hoosiers in the red zone with a 39-yard carry, before punching it in for a touchdown two plays later.

Penalties were a story for Indiana, who averaged just three penalties per game so far this season, but wound up with nearly triple that.

Some were costly too, including a holding penalty that set the Wildcats up on the Indiana 4-yardline, and a few plays later Chiles took matters into his own hands.

Beebe threw down another huge play to put the Hoosiers back in scoring position.

It looked like the Wildcats were on the cusp of another goal-line stand, but a costly defensive pass interference penalty gave Indiana a fresh set of downs, with QB Josh Hoover finding the end zone on a keeper that fooled just about everyone in the building.

Northwestern tacked on a field goal on the ensuing drive, but Indiana managed to recover their attempt at an onside kick.

That slow start habit is still going to be a talking point, as it let Northwestern stay in the game.

And while the injury to Richard is a big concern, Beebe's play — he finished with 203 rushing yards — was a major bright spot.

The Hoosiers will play Rutgers next weekend, followed by Nebraska, and then a big one against Ohio State on October 17.

World.title: Doctor reveals '10-year rule' for evaluating brain fog and dementia symptoms
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Losing a train of thought, struggling to recall once-familiar words, or forgetting the reason for walking into a room can leave older adults wondering if they are experiencing early signs of Alzheimer’s disease or dementia.

However, these brain blips can often be tied to hormone shifts later in life, medical experts note — and women who experience a loss of estrogen during perimenopause and menopause are particularly affected.

According to Dr. Rhonda Voskuhl, a professor of neurology at UCLA and co-founder of Cleopatra RX in Los Angeles, women experiencing memory struggles in midlife should compare their cognitive function to their own past performance before assuming something is seriously wrong.

WOMEN WHO START COMMON HORMONE THERAPY IN THEIR 50S MAY HAVE 23% LOWER DEMENTIA RISK

"I think they should listen to themselves," Voskuhl told Fox News Digital at the Livelong Women’s Health Summit in New York City on Friday. "They know. Just ask yourself."

The 10-year assessment

To help women gauge whether their memory lapses are tied to hormonal shifts, Voskuhl recommends using a quick benchmark – comparing their current mental state to where it was a decade ago.

"The first question is, are you worse than you were 10 years ago?" she said, referencing the Voskuhl Brain Fog Menopause Assessment used at UCLA's Comprehensive Menopausal Program.

KATIE COURIC COULDN'T REMEMBER THE YEAR OR THE PRESIDENT DURING FRIGHTENING BRAIN EPISODE

"Ten years is a pretty good spot. And they think, ‘What was I doing 10 years ago? What was I like? Was I having problems finding the words? Was I at the point where I couldn’t multitask anymore? Was I slow in my processing?’ And they’ll remember."

This comparison can help reveal whether a woman’s cognitive changes may be linked to menopause, while giving patients and physicians a baseline for tracking symptoms over time.

The NFL analogy

Standard memory tests don’t always catch subtle shifts in everyday cognitive function. In the medical community, this is known as subjective cognitive decline, when patients notice changes even though neurological testing remains normal.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reports that roughly one in nine adults report subjective cognitive decline, yet less than half discuss these memory concerns with a healthcare professional.

To illustrate why routine tests can miss early menopausal brain fog, Voskuhl compared it to a high-performing athlete.

"They know if they're not like they used to be."

"If somebody is an NFL football player and he says, 'I'm weaker than I used to be,' and I go and do my neurological test, I say, 'Oh no, you're still strong,'" Voskuhl said.

What the player is feeling still matters, even if a standard test shows no obvious decline, she noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Women, too, can often recognize when their cognitive abilities have changed from their own baseline and should trust those observations, according to Voskuhl.

Understanding the difference between hormonal brain fog and neurodegenerative disease comes down to how memory loss impacts daily function, experts agree.

CLICK HERE TO 

Menopausal brain fog typically involves temporary, inconsistent lapses like misplacing items or experiencing slower processing speed, but overall reasoning skills and independence remain intact, according to Mayo Clinic. Symptoms often fluctuate and can be exacerbated by stress or poor sleep.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

By contrast, early dementia causes persistent, progressive memory loss that interferes with basic daily tasks like managing finances, following familiar routes while driving or exercising sound judgment.

Amid cognitive concerns, experts advise seeking a full medical evaluation, including brain MRIs or vascular screenings, to rule out underlying issues like blood vessel disease or thyroid imbalances.
