An executive at a Nigerian insurer expects rising fuel and running costs to push drivers toward cheaper cover. Nigeria motor insurance already sits at prices that look small in dollar terms.

What was actually said

Katherine Itua is executive director for finance and investments at Consolidated Hallmark Insurance. She made the comment in September 2026.

As fuel and vehicle running costs rise, she said, more customers are likely to choose third-party cover. It is more affordable than comprehensive.

That is a forecast about customer behaviour. No data showing an actual shift has been published.

It is worth stating clearly because the distinction is easy to lose. An expectation is not a trend.

What Nigeria motor insurance costs

Third-party cover pays for damage to other people. The regulator sets a minimum premium of 15,000 naira a year, about US$11.

That minimum has applied since 1 January 2023, when it rose from 5,000 naira, about US$4. The increase was 200 percent.

Comprehensive cover also pays for the owner’s own vehicle. The regulator sets a minimum of 5 percent of the sum insured.

On a car insured for 3 million naira, about US$2,260, that is roughly 150,000 naira, about US$113. The gap between the two is the whole argument.

The costs pressing on insurers

Insurers face the same fuel bills as their customers. Offices, field operations, claims work and sales networks all run on fuel and generators.

Consolidated Hallmark budgeted petrol at about 1,500 naira a litre for 2026, roughly US$1.13. It budgeted diesel at about 2,000 naira, roughly US$1.51.

Those are planning assumptions rather than pump prices. They indicate what the company expects to pay.

Higher running costs squeeze margins on low-value policies hardest. Third-party business is the lowest-value line there is.

That cuts against the prediction rather than supporting it. A shift to cheaper policies would thin insurers’ margins further.

What the rules now require

Third-party motor cover is compulsory in Nigeria. The obligation comes from motor vehicle legislation rather than from a regulator’s statement.

The minimum third-party property damage limit for a private car is 3 million naira, about US$2,260. That figure rose with the 2023 premium change.

A larger reform has since arrived. The Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act was signed on 6 August 2025 and took effect the same day.

It sets a 60-day deadline for settling admitted claims, with interest penalties for late payment. It also creates a compensation fund for road accident victims.

Why enforcement is the real variable

The regulatory minimum and the market price are not the same thing. Some insurers and comparison sites still advertise cover from 5,000 naira, about US$4.

That gap tells you how patchy enforcement is. A minimum price that is widely undercut is a target rather than a rule.

The reform act ties valid cover to a national insurance database. In principle that makes undercutting harder to hide.

In practice, the change will show in claims data rather than in announcements. That will take a year or more.

Until then, the published minimum and the advertised price will keep diverging. Buyers should read the cover, not the headline rate.

What this means for drivers

For a driver on a tight budget, third-party cover is the legal minimum and the cheap option. It pays nothing toward your own car.

At about US$11 a year it is inexpensive by any international measure. At about US$113, so is comprehensive cover.

The real constraint is income rather than the premium. That is why the executive’s prediction is plausible even without data behind it.

Anyone comparing quotes should check the property damage limit. Below 3 million naira, about US$2,260, the policy does not meet the minimum.

What is not yet known

No figures show an actual move from comprehensive to third-party cover. Only one executive’s expectation has been reported.

Policy volume data by class has not been published for 2026. Without it the claim cannot be tested.

The current pump price of petrol was not stated alongside the comment. Only the company’s budget assumption is on record.

How the regulator will enforce the reform act’s provisions is also unclear. No enforcement actions have been announced.

FAQ

Is Nigeria motor insurance shifting to third-party cover?

One insurance executive expects it to. No published data shows an actual shift in policy purchases.

How much is third-party motor cover in Nigeria?

The regulatory minimum is 15,000 naira a year, about US$11. Some insurers still advertise cover from 5,000 naira, about US$4.

What does comprehensive cover cost?

The regulator sets a minimum of 5 percent of the sum insured. On a car insured for 3 million naira, that is about 150,000 naira, roughly US$113.

What changed in the 2025 reform act?

It set a 60-day deadline for settling admitted claims, with interest penalties for late payment. It also created a road accident victims fund and tied valid cover to a national database.

Sources: Nairametrics on the executive’s remarks and on the 2023 premium change; SHQ Legal on the 2025 reform act; Proshare on the premium rates.

World.title: Remote Osa Eco-Lodge Playa Cativo Joins Small Luxury Hotels of the World
World.content:
Playa Cativo Lodge, a secluded beachfront retreat on the Golfo Dulce in Costa Rica’s Southern Zone, has been admitted into Small Luxury Hotels of the World, the international collection of independently owned boutique properties. The addition gives the Southern Zone yet another foothold in one of the best-known names in independent luxury hospitality.

Founded in 2012, the lodge sits within a private rainforest reserve of roughly 400 hectares (1,000 acres) surrounded by Piedras Blancas National Park, a protected area that once formed part of Corcovado National Park. There is no road to the property. Guests fly into Golfito or Puerto Jiménez and finish the trip with a boat ride of about 30 minutes or arrive by helicopter. The crossing often brings sightings of dolphins and, in season, whales. On land, visitors share the grounds with toucans, scarlet macaws, monkeys and sloths.

The lodge has 18 rooms, ranging from ocean-view guest rooms to casitas with private plunge pools and a family villa. The rooms are designed to stay open to the surrounding forest, and most rely on breezes off the gulf rather than air conditioning, though some room types now offer it.

The property also offers wellness activities and a kitchen built around local ingredients, part of which come from the lodge’s own organic farm. Management says more than 95% of the land is devoted to conservation and that the reserve strengthens the protection of neighboring Piedras Blancas. The operation also relies on renewable energy, organic agriculture, recycling and the elimination of single-use plastics.

The Golfo Dulce itself became Latin America’s first Whale Heritage Site in 2023, a World Cetacean Alliance designation for places where communities protect whales and dolphins. Humpback whales from both hemispheres use the gulf to give birth and nurse their calves.

General manager Kenneth Hidalgo said joining the collection recognizes a style of hospitality rooted in independence, privacy, authenticity and a deep sense of place. He added that conservation stands as one of the lodge’s central pillars, treated as part of the luxury itself and as something guests are invited to take part in.

Hidalgo also said the membership is a chance for international travelers to discover Osa and the Golfo Dulce as one of the world’s great nature and luxury destinations. The lodge describes the surrounding wilderness not as a backdrop but as the reason the property exists. Small Luxury Hotels of the World, known as SLH, has spent more than 35 years building a portfolio of independent boutique hotels and now counts more than 700 properties in over 100 countries.

Its members average around 50 rooms, and the company says it personally visits and vets every hotel before admission and inspects members annually. The company is owned and led by siblings Daniel Shamoon and Jennica Shamoon Arazi. It has been expanding quickly, adding 29 hotels in the first three months of 2026 alone.

Membership carries real commercial weight. Through a partnership with Hilton, more than 550 participating SLH hotels can be booked through Hilton’s own channels, putting small independent properties in front of the chain’s loyalty members. SLH also runs its own complimentary guest loyalty program, The Club by SLH.

Playa Cativo joins a Costa Rican roster that includes Tabacón Thermal Resort and Spa in La Fortuna, Rio Perdido in Bagaces, Hotel Nantipa in Santa Teresa, Los Altos Resort in Manuel Antonio, Alta Las Palomas in San José and Hotel Three Sixty in Ojochal de Osa. It is the only member of the collection on the shores of the Golfo Dulce.

The news caps a strong run for the lodge. It earned a place in Tripadvisor’s 2025 Travelers’ Choice Best of the Best awards, ranking fourth among luxury hotels in both Costa Rica and Central America, and says it was honored again in the 2026 edition. For the Southern Zone, which remains far less developed than Guanacaste or the Central Pacific, the recognition adds to a growing reputation among travelers willing to go the extra distance for remote, nature-based luxury.

World.title: Human Trafficking Cases Reach 16-Year High in Costa Rica
World.content:
Costa Rica recorded 83 human trafficking victims in 2025, the highest number reported in any single year since at least 2010, according to figures released by the country’s National Coalition Against the Illegal Trafficking of Migrants and Human Trafficking (CONATT). The new figures show the problem affects Costa Ricans as well as foreigners and continues to fall heavily on women and young people.

Between 2010 and 2025, authorities officially recognized 611 people as trafficking victims in Costa Rica. Women accounted for 72% of those cases, while 234 victims, or 38%, were children or teenagers. The remaining 377 were adults. More than half of the victims were Costa Rican. Of the 611 cases recorded over the 16-year period, 330 involved Costa Rican nationals and 281 involved foreigners.

The numbers are a reminder that human trafficking does not only involve people being brought illegally across an international border. Costa Ricans can also become victims inside their own country or after being recruited for supposed opportunities elsewhere. Trafficking generally involves someone being recruited, moved, housed or controlled through deception, threats, pressure or abuse so that another person can exploit them. That exploitation can include forced labor, sexual exploitation, servitude or forced begging.

One of the biggest challenges for authorities is that traffickers do not always approach victims in ways that immediately look suspicious. Melissa Bermúdez Otárola, who represents the Costa Rican Social Security Fund (CCSS), before CONATT, said recruitment methods can include fake job offers, relationships built on trust and emotional manipulation. Those tactics can make cases particularly difficult to spot when the person behind the exploitation is someone the victim initially knows or trusts.

Women, teenage girls and children can face especially high risks in cases involving sexual exploitation. Economic problems, dependence on another person, discrimination and abusive relationships can all make it easier for traffickers to target someone in a vulnerable position. The figures were released as Costa Rica marked the International Day Against Sexual Exploitation and Human Trafficking this week.

The CCSS said its hospitals and clinics have a nationwide protocol for dealing with suspected trafficking cases. Victims can receive medical and psychological care regardless of whether they are Costa Rican, foreign residents or migrants without regular immigration status. Health workers are also trained to recognize warning signs and coordinate with the agencies responsible for protecting victims.

Authorities are asking people who suspect someone may be a trafficking victim to report it rather than trying to intervene themselves. Suspected cases can be reported through Costa Rica’s 9-1-1 emergency system. The Professional Migration Police can also be contacted at 2106-4005. The Judicial Investigation Police, or OIJ, receives trafficking reports through its specialized unit at 2256-5702 and 2256-5703, as well as through the confidential line 800-8000-645.

The 83 victims recorded in 2025 do not necessarily represent the full scale of trafficking in Costa Rica. Trafficking can remain hidden for long periods because victims may be afraid to report what is happening, may depend financially on the person exploiting them or may not initially recognize themselves as victims.

What the latest figures do show is that Costa Rica officially recognized more trafficking victims in 2025 than in any other year during the 2010-2025 period tracked by CONATT.

World.title: Costa Rica Blows 3-0 Halftime Lead in 4-3 Home Loss to Curaçao
World.content:
Costa Rica’s national team threw away a three-goal halftime lead and lost 4-3 to Curaçao last night, a huge collapse that left home fans booing, chanting for coach Fernando Batista’s exit and mocking their own team with olé chants before many of them streamed out of the stadium.

The Concacaf Nations League opener at Estadio Ricardo Saprissa was Batista’s first competitive match in charge since Costa Rica missed the 2026 World Cup. For 45 minutes, it looked like the fresh start the program had been waiting for. Orlando Sinclair opened the scoring in the third minute with a hard, angled shot inside the box, his first goal for the national team.

Carlos Mora added a second midway through the first half and struck again from the edge of the area just before the break to make it 3-0. Curaçao, which qualified for the 2026 World Cup for the first time in its history, turned the game after coach Dick Advocaat sent on Kenji Gorré, Tahith Chong and Jordi Paulina in the 57th minute. Those three substitutes produced all four of the visitors’ goals in a span of about 20 minutes.

Gorré pulled one back in the 62nd minute, and Chong beat goalkeeper Abraham Madriz with a shot from outside the area four minutes later. Gorré leveled the score at 3-3 in the 78th minute, tapping in after a teammate’s shot hit the post, and Paulina volleyed in a cross from Juninho Bacuna with less than 10 minutes left to complete the comeback.

Batista accepted responsibility afterward. He said the team had the match under control and played well in the first half, but that his decision to reorganize the defense when Gerald Taylor came on cost Costa Rica control of the midfield, and that two quick goals shook the side. He said the second half was his responsibility and that he understood the fans’ anger.

The players shouldered the blame as well. Midfielder Orlando Galo said the team came out of halftime without the courage Costa Rica represents, lost its shape and failed to show character, adding that the players alone were responsible. Mora said it was not the first time the team had let a lead slip and that a match under control cannot get away like that.

Captain Francisco Calvo called the defeat a very hard blow and described the second half as a slump. He said the team still has three group matches left and must recover the points in Jamaica. The frustration carried past the final whistle. Reports from the stadium said Galo and Calvo were involved in a confrontation with several Curaçao players in the area beneath the stands, with shoving and insults but no punches, before security staff separated the two groups and sent them to their locker rooms.

Inside the stadium, a section of the crowd began chanting “Fuera Bocha,” calling for Batista’s dismissal, after Curaçao’s third goal, and security near the Costa Rica bench was reinforced for the final minutes. Many fans left after the fourth goal, while the Curaçao players celebrated with the small group of visiting supporters. Attendance was sparse and Costa Rica played at Saprissa because the National Stadium was booked for other events during at this time.

Costa Rica sits in Group A of League A alongside Haiti, Trinidad and Tobago, Curaçao, Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic, and only the top two teams advance to the quarterfinals. In the group’s other opening matches, the Dominican Republic beat Nicaragua 3-2 and Haiti defeated Trinidad and Tobago.

There is little time to regroup since Costa Rica faces Haiti on Sunday at Sabina Park in Kingston, Jamaica, then travels to Managua to play Nicaragua before hosting Haiti at Saprissa on Oct. 4. The defeat adds to a difficult stretch for a program still rebuilding after its World Cup elimination, one that also included a 3-0 friendly loss to England in June.

World.title: Ashema Chang charged after allegedly burning down Eugene Thompson’s house and leaving him homeless; Court orders psychiatric evaluation
World.content:
Ashema Chang charged after allegedly burning down Eugene Thompson’s house and leaving him homeless; Court orders psychiatric evaluation

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Eugene Thompson says he lost his home, belongings and virtually everything he owned when fire destroyed his Belama Phase 5 residence just one day after he was ordered to leave the property amid a domestic dispute with Ashema Chang. Now, Chang has appeared before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court in connection with the dispute, but her arraignment was halted after the Chief Magistrate determined that she was not in a condition to enter a plea and ordered that she undergo a psychiatric evaluation.

Chang, 25, was brought before Court #1 on Tuesday, September 22, on a charge stemming from the case. During the hearing, however, she reportedly identified herself as “Erica,” appeared uncertain about where she was living and gave responses that caused the Chief Magistrate to question whether she understood the proceedings.

The court therefore did not take a plea and ordered that Chang be evaluated before the matter proceeds.

The case is linked to the September 15 fire that completely destroyed Thompson’s home at #5217 Belama Phase 5. Thompson, 43, told police he had lived at the property for about five years and estimated the house alone at approximately $45,000, excluding appliances, tools and other belongings lost in the blaze. The house was not insured.

Thompson had been served with a protection order the previous day and said he complied with the court’s direction to leave the residence while Chang remained there. He later told police that, days before the fire, Chang had allegedly sent him a threatening voice message referring to the house being burned.

Police subsequently sought Chang for questioning and later detained her. According to the information provided in the court matter, she was charged with threat to damage property.

At Tuesday’s hearing, the Chief Magistrate questioned Chang about whether she had previously visited a clinic or taken medication. A sister who was present told the court that Chang had recently seen a doctor and had previously been prescribed medication, although she could not provide details.

The Chief Magistrate ordered Chang’s family to have her undergo a psychiatric evaluation and obtain information on her medical history before the case continues.

Rather than remanding her to prison, the court granted Chang bail of $300 plus one surety of the same amount. She met bail and is scheduled to return to court on November 13, 2026.

The cause of the September 15 fire has not been publicly established, and the allegations against Chang remain before the court.

World.title: ‘The Devil This Time Used Meh’: Security guard fined $800 after caught on camera stealing $2,000 motorcycle
World.content:
‘The Devil This Time Used Meh’: Security guard fined $800 after caught on camera stealing $2,000 motorcycle

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City security guard who admitted stealing a $2,000 motorcycle told a Magistrate that “the devil this time used me” as he pleaded for leniency in court on Friday.

Twenty-six-year-old Jaimie Adrian Fuller, a security guard employed with Fort Point Security Company, appeared unrepresented in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court, where he pleaded guilty to a single charge of theft.

Fuller was accused of stealing a green Lifan motorcycle valued at $2,000 from Patrick Martinez on September 16, 2026.

According to the prosecution’s case, Martinez had left the damaged motorcycle near a laundromat on Freetown Road. When he later checked for it, the motorcycle was gone.

Police investigating the theft reviewed surveillance footage which reportedly showed a shirtless man pushing the motorcycle away from Freetown Road and through nearby streets, including Douglas Jones Street and Yorke Street.

An officer who reviewed the footage reportedly recognized the man as Fuller. Police said the individual captured on camera also appeared to walk with a limp.

Fuller pleaded guilty but offered an explanation to the court, saying he had done wrong and was willing to pay for any damage caused to the motorcycle.

“I did the wrong thing, but at the moment I never realized what I was doing. I returned the cycle and I am willing to pay for damages caused to it if I must,” Fuller told the court.

He also explained that he helps care for his mother and sister and expressed remorse for his actions.

“The devil this time used me,” Fuller told the Magistrate.

Taking his guilty plea and mitigation into consideration, the Magistrate imposed a non-custodial sentence, fining Fuller $800 plus $5 cost of court.

He has until November 30, 2026, to pay the fine or face three months imprisonment.

World.title: UDP demands full investigation into reported Guatemalan military aircraft incursion
World.content:
UDP demands full investigation into reported Guatemalan military aircraft incursion

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The United Democratic Party is demanding a full investigation into reports that a Guatemalan military aircraft may have entered Belizean airspace near Lighthouse Reef Atoll and Caye Caulker.

In a statement issued Thursday, September 25, the UDP said Belizeans deserve clear answers about the aircraft’s route, purpose and exact position during the reported September 24 flight.

The Opposition referred to comments attributed to Ministry of National Defence and Border Security CEO Francis Usher indicating that Belize had not authorized the flight.

The UDP also pointed to Guatemala’s subsequent response, saying the Guatemalan Ministry of National Defence stated that its military operations comply with national and international law, but did not directly answer whether the aircraft entered Belizean airspace.

The party is now calling on the Government to establish the aircraft’s route using available radar, air traffic and flight records and to make its findings public.

It also wants the Government to seek a direct explanation from Guatemala regarding the purpose of the flight and the aircraft’s location near Lighthouse Reef and Caye Caulker.

The UDP said that if evidence confirms the aircraft entered Belizean airspace without authorization, Belize should lodge a formal diplomatic protest and raise the incident with appropriate regional and international partners.

The reported incident comes amid the longstanding Belize Guatemala territorial dispute. Belize has described the peaceful resolution of that dispute as a major foreign policy priority, with the matter currently before the International Court of Justice. Ministry of Foreign Affairs

The UDP said it would support lawful and peaceful measures to protect Belize’s sovereignty.

World.title: UDP says “Guatemala must provide a direct answer”
World.content:
UDP says “Guatemala must provide a direct answer”

By Zoila Palma: The United Democratic Party (UDP) is calling on the Government of Belize to provide answers following reports that a Guatemalan military aircraft flew near Lighthouse Reef Atoll and Caye Caulker on September 24.

In a statement, the UDP said Chief Executive Officer in the Ministry of National Defence and Border Security Francis Usher confirmed that Belize did not authorize the flight.

Guatemala’s Ministry of National Defense has maintained that its military operations comply with national and international law, without directly addressing the aircraft’s location, the UDP said.

The UDP is urging the Government to establish the aircraft’s route using radar, air traffic and flight records and to make the findings public.

“Belize needs a specific account of the flight, not a general assurance,” the party said.

It is also calling for a direct explanation from Guatemala regarding the purpose of the flight and the aircraft’s position near Lighthouse Reef and Caye Caulker.

The UDP further stated that if evidence confirms the aircraft entered Belizean airspace without authorization, “the absence of authorization makes a formal diplomatic protest necessary.”

The call comes as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs says it is working with the Ministry of National Defence and Border Security to officially confirm the details of the reported incident, while stating that any incursion by a foreign military aircraft would constitute a violation of Belize’s sovereignty.

The UDP also linked the incident to Belize’s recent protest over the reported obstruction of Belizean nationals near Sarstoon Island.

“Belizeans deserve the facts, and Guatemala must provide a direct answer,” the UDP said.

World.title: Man says he paid car dealer more than $13,000 for Pathfinder but never got it then found same vehicle being advertised on Facebook Marketplace
World.content:
Man says he paid car dealer more than $13,000 for Pathfinder but never got it then found same vehicle being advertised on Facebook Marketplace

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a complaint of obtaining property by deception after a Belize City man reported paying more than BZ$13,000 for an imported SUV that was never delivered — only to later allegedly find the same vehicle being advertised for sale on Facebook Marketplace.

A 31-year-old man told police that in March he contacted a car dealer to purchase a 2014 Nissan Pathfinder through an online bidding site.

The complainant said they agreed on a price of BZ$13,000, with BZ$10,000 to be paid as a deposit and the remaining BZ$3,000 when the vehicle arrived in Belize.

According to the report, the man met the dealer at the Novelo’s Bus Terminal on March 20 and handed him BZ$10,000 cash. He said he later received an electronic receipt.

On June 24, the car dealer allegedly informed the complainant that the Pathfinder had reached Belize’s northern border and requested the outstanding balance plus a BZ$150 broker’s fee.

Smith told police that he subsequently transferred BZ$3,150 to an account provided.

The vehicle was reportedly supposed to be delivered on June 29, but the complainant alleged that the car dealer later told him he was unable to retrieve it from the border.

Nearly three months later, on September 17, Smith said he was scrolling through Facebook Marketplace when he saw a 2014 Nissan Pathfinder advertised by an account bearing the same dealer’s name.

Smith told police he recognized the SUV because the  allegedly used the same photographs as the original online listing for the vehicle he had paid to purchase.

Police are investigating the complaint as obtaining property by deception. No criminal charge is indicated in the situation report.

World.title: Belize to protest after Guatemalan Military plane spends 70 minutes in Airspace, turns off transponder
World.content:
Belize to protest after Guatemalan Military plane spends 70 minutes in Airspace, turns off transponder

By Zoila Palma: Belize is preparing to issue a formal protest note to Guatemala after a Guatemalan Army aircraft entered Belizean airspace, circled near Lighthouse Reef and remained inside the country’s airspace for approximately one hour and 10 minutes before exiting through the Sarstoon River. The incident occurred on September 24, 2026.

Francis Usher, Chief Executive Officer in the Ministry of National Defence said the aircraft, identified as FAG706, entered Belizean airspace from the east at approximately 7:29 p.m. and began circling in the vicinity of Lighthouse Reef.

“FAG706 did enter our airspace at 7:29 pm local time on 24 September and it entered from the East and began circling in the vicinity of Lighthouse Reef,” Usher stated. He added that “they began circling as if though they were looking for something.”

According to Usher, the aircraft disappeared from Belize’s secondary radar at approximately 8:07 p.m., indicating that its transponder had been turned off.

However, he said Belizean authorities continued tracking the aircraft through primary radar. “But even if you fall off the secondary radar, we can still track you using the primary radar. So, we were able to pick them up. They were still in Belizean airspace,” he explained.

Usher said FAG706 eventually left Belizean airspace at approximately 8:40 p.m., departing through the south pass of the Sarstoon River. The aircraft therefore remained in Belizean airspace for approximately one hour and 10 minutes after entering from the east.

Meanwhile, CEO in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Oscar Arnold said Belize will deliver a protest note to Guatemala’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, including information on the aircraft’s location and movements. “And we will demand from them an explanation as to why this is taking place. We find it very troubling that the leadership would not have this information available to them at the time when they made the social media post stating that they operate within the scope of professionalism and respect of sovereignty,” Arnold said.

World.title: Guatemalan military plane enters Belize airspace, circles Lighthouse Reef and exits through Sarstoon
World.content:
Guatemalan military plane enters Belize airspace, circles Lighthouse Reef and exits through Sarstoon

By Zoila Palma: A Guatemalan Army aircraft, FAG706, spent approximately one hour and 10 minutes inside Belize’s airspace on September 24, 2026, before exiting through the southern part of the country, according to Francis Usher, Chief Executive Officer in the Ministry of National Defence.

Usher provided details of the incident today.

Usher said the aircraft entered Belizean airspace from the east at 7:29 p.m. and began circling near Lighthouse Reef. “FAG706 did enter our airspace at 7:29 pm local time on 24 September and it entered from the East and began circling in the vicinity of Lighthouse Reef,” Usher stated.

He explained that the aircraft appeared to be circling between Lighthouse Reef and other aviation reference points, adding that “they began circling as if though they were looking for something.”

According to Usher, the aircraft disappeared from the secondary radar at approximately 8:07 p.m., indicating that its transponder had been turned off.

However, he said Belizean authorities continued tracking the aircraft using primary radar. “But even if you fall off the secondary radar, we can still track you using the primary radar. So, we were able to pick them up. They were still in Belizean airspace,” he explained.

Usher said the aircraft eventually departed Belizean airspace at approximately 8:40 p.m., around one hour and 10 minutes after entering the country. “At approximately 8:40pm, 1 hour and 10 minutes after, they initially entered Belize, they departed Belize through the south pass, the Sarstoon River,” he stated.

CEO in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Oscar Arnold has indicated that Belize will deliver a protest note to Guatemala’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs along with coordination and location.

“And we will demand from them an explanation as to why this is taking place. We find it very troubling that the leadership would not have this information available to them at the time when they made the social media post stating that they operate within the scope of professionalism and respect of sovereignty,” Arnold said.

World.title: Burglars steal cash, cigarettes, lottery tickets and 50 live 9mm rounds from Racecourse Street shop
World.content:
Burglars steal cash, cigarettes, lottery tickets and 50 live 9mm rounds from Racecourse Street shop

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a burglary at J&C Shop on Racecourse Street in Belize City where thieves reportedly stole more than BZ$7,600 worth of property — including 50 live rounds of 9mm ammunition.

Police responded to the business early Monday morning, September 21, after the businessman was alerted that locks securing the shop had been damaged.

Investigators say entry was gained by cutting a padlock on the burglar-bar door and opening a shutter.

The shop owner later provided police with a detailed list of stolen property including cigarettes, cigars, scratch lottery tickets, beer, noodles, a network video recording device and UPS, and BZ$3,104 in cash.

Also reported stolen were 50 live 9mm rounds valued at BZ$75.

Police estimated the total loss at BZ$7,622.

Investigators processed the scene and reportedly lifted fingerprints. Police also recovered a pair of bolt cutters and took a DNA swab from a beer can which surveillance footage allegedly showed the perpetrators drinking from during the burglary.

Police have also reviewed surveillance footage from the shop as the investigation continues.

World.title: Cephas’ injury-time strike gives Boyz dramatic 3-2 win over Guatemala in Nations League
World.content:
Jamaica's Kasey Palmer battles Guatemalan Óscar Santis for the ball. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — A stoppage-time goal from substitute Renaldo Cephas gave Jamaica’s Reggae Boyz a dramatic come-from-behind 3-2 win over Guatemala in their Concacaf Nations League Group B League A opener at the National Stadium on Friday.

Jamaica avenged last year’s loss to the Central Americans at the Gold Cup despite a double from Oscar Santis, the first coming in the second minute.

The Reggae Boyz, rallied from a goal down to lead 2-1, Guatemala levelled before Cephas’ late strike settled the points.

Santis, who scored in Guatemala’s 1-0 win at the Gold Cup, gave them an early lead when he fired low under goalkeeper Andre Blake to finish off a counter-attack.

They could have been 2-0 up in the 18th minute, but Darwin Lom guided a cross from Santis just wide of the far left post with the Jamaican goal at his mercy.

Kasey Palmer, who had a good outing, pulled Jamaica level in the 39th minute when he capitalised on an error by Jorge Aparicio and fired low under goalkeeper Kenderson Navarro for his third goal for Jamaica.

Palmer was also involved as Jamaica took the lead in the 53rd minute, making the pass to Ruman Burell, who scored, beating Navarro to his right into the far corner.

A mistake in the Jamaican defence left the door open for Santis in the 67th minute, and he made no mistake, dribbling around Blake, who came off his line, and scored in an open goal.

Both teams came close to scoring. Cephas shot just wide in the 79th minute, and Olger Escobar hit the inside of the Jamaican left upright in the 90th minute.

Four minutes into added time, Cephas made up for his earlier miss when he beat Navarro with his fourth goal in national colours.

Meanwhile, head coach Rudolph Speid had named seven members of the team that had lost in the final game of the failed World Cup 2026 attempt in the starting X1—goalkeeper and team captain Blake, Joel Latibeaudiere, Richard King, Isaac Hayden, Palmer, Ronaldo Webster and Tyreece Campbell.

Jamaica’s bid for a spot in the expanded FIFA World Cup to be hosted by Concacaf failed after a 1-0 loss to the Democratic Republic of Congo in their FIFA intercontinental play-offs in Mexico in March.

Starting team: Andre Blake, Joel Latibeaudiere, Damion Lowe, Richard King, Isaac Hayden, Karoy Anderson, Kasey Palmer, Ronaldo Webster, Tyreece Campbell, Rumarn Burrell, Javon East.

— Paul A Reid

World.title: Bartlett welcomes Sandals, Royal Caribbean partnership
World.content:
Minister of Tourism Edmund Bartlett

Tourism Minister Edmund Bartlett has welcomed the signing of a partnership agreement between Sandals Resorts and Royal Caribbean Group, highlighting its potential to expand Jamaica’s international reach, support tourism investment and create opportunities for workers and local businesses.

“Sandals is a Jamaican success story, built on the vision of Gordon ‘Butch’ Stewart and the contribution of generations of Caribbean hospitality professionals. His son, Adam Stewart, has carried that legacy forward as executive chairman, guiding the brand into a new chapter of growth and global partnership. This announcement represents a significant moment in that journey. We recognise the importance of that legacy and the possibilities that greater global reach could bring to its next chapter,” a release from the tourism ministry quotes Bartlett.

He noted that combining Sandals’ resort expertise with Royal Caribbean Group’s international customer base and distribution networks could introduce Jamaica to wider audiences.

Over time, this could support demand for resort stays, encourage further investment and create additional opportunities across the tourism economy, including procurement from Jamaican farmers and manufacturers, opportunities for attractions and creative enterprises, and training and career development for tourism workers.

These possibilities, he said, align with Jamaica’s Tourism 3.0 growth agenda, which places greater emphasis on retaining tourism value locally, developing human capital and ensuring that communities share in the sector’s progress.

World.title: FIFA president Infantino at National Stadium for Reggae Boyz clash
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — FIFA president Gianni Infantino is at the National Stadium in Kingston for Jamaica’s Concacaf Nations League game against Guatemala.

Infantino arrived around 7:00 pm amid an ongoing re-election campaign for the top job in football.

The FIFA president’s campaign has been marred by controversy surrounding a proposal to take aspects of the World Cup to private investors, which prompted swift and widespread backlash from football associations worldwide.

Attendance at the match just an hour before kickoff was scant, with barely any seats filled at the sporting ground.

This is the first official match at the stadium since a record number of Jamaicans packed the venue to witness the possibility of the country booking a ticket for the 2026 World Cup in their Concacaf final round finale against Curacao.

That match ended nil-nil, and the resulting draw left the Reggae Boyz in second place in their group, sending Curacao through to the World Cup. They were forced into the inter-confederation play-offs and eliminated after falling to DR Congo.

Five members of the Reggae Boyz team who lost in the final game of the failed World Cup 2026 attempt were named in the starting team to face Guatemala in their Concacaf Nations League Group B game.
