World.title: Lula or Bolsonaro as president? Brazil gears up to vote
World.content:
Brazilians go to the polls on October 4. The front-runners are multilateralist incumbent Lula da Silva and former President Jair Bolsonaro's son, Flavio, who wants to bring Brazil closer to the US and away from China.

Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva spoke in no uncertain terms at the opening of the UN General Assembly on Tuesday in New York: "Brazil does not belong in anyone's backyard," the Brazilian president said. His comment was directed at his US counterpart Donald Trump, despite Trump not being in attendance.

The US president has repeatedly interfered with Brazilian domestic politics, siding with former President Jair Messias Bolsonaro and the far-right opposition. In July, Trump imposed sanctions on a judge who found Bolsonaro guilty of attempting a coup and sentenced him to 27 years in jail. Washington only lifted the sanctions after negotiating with Lula.

Bolsonaro's eldest son Flavio is Lula's biggest challenger in the upcoming presidential election on October 4, and polls currently show the two of them to be neck and neck in a potential runoff.

The election in the world's fifth largest country is drawing a great deal of international attention. Brazil is an agricultural giant and very rich in natural resources — boasting rare earth elements, vast water resources and enormous crude oil reserves.

Brazil one of South America's last bastions of the left

Lula is the "last man standing" of the South American left, while Flavio Bolsonaro is part of an increasingly strong far-right camp. Argentina, Bolivia, Peru, Chile, Ecuador and Colombia all have governments that are sympathetic to Trump. And since January, Venezuela has been what some describe as a US protectorate.

Lula advocates for multilateralist diplomacy and good international relations with all countries Image: Silvia Izquierdo/AP Photo/picture alliance

Foreign policy hasn't played a big role in the campaign, but this election will nonetheless decide whether Brazil moves closer to Trump's US. Washington is seeking economic and military dominance in South America through the Shield of the Americas initiative, focused on combating violent cartels. After his military intervention in Venezuela, Trump is now exerting economic pressure on Mexico and Cuba. At the same time, he is trying to counter Chinese influence in the region.

For his part, Lula is an advocate of multilateralist diplomacy, wanting Brazil to engage in dialogue and trade with everybody. China has long been Brazil's most important trading partner.

Flavio Bolsonaro favors a conservative alliance with the US and other right-wing states. But for Leonardo Paz from the Brazilian Fundacao Getulio Vargas think tank, a Bolsonaro victory would not necessarily automatically mean better relations with the US. He told DW that Lula had established a largely normal relationship with Trump — both are 80 years old — despite some initial friction. The two leaders got along well, said Paz, even if Lula has not succumbed to Trump's pressure.

Who is Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Paz did admit that if Bolsonaro won, the 45-year-old would be more likely to accommodate Trump, pointing out that his father Jair had made far-reaching concessions to the US when he was president. During Jair Bolsonaro's time in office from 2019 to 2023, Brazil agreed to forgo its "developing country status" in World Trade Organization negotiations in exchange for a mere promise that the US would back its bid to become a member of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD). Trump also said he was considering giving Brazil NATO "privileges." Neither promise came to anything.

"While relations with the US would continue as they are with Lula, it is completely unclear what a Flavio Bolsonaro presidency would mean," Rubens Ricupero, a former Brazilian diplomat and minister, told DW. "Lula has prestige in foreign policy, while Bolsonaro is completely inexperienced."

Would Brazil pull out of BRICS?

A victory for Bolsonaro would likely jeopardize Brazil's role in BRICS, the alliance that comprises Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and five other states. Bolsonaro has said that one of his first acts would be to review whether Brazil should stay in the alliance, arguing that BRICS only serves to provoke the US. He has also spoken out against China's efforts to reduce the global dominance of the US dollar.

It's hard to tell how serious such intentions are, considering the importance of economic ties between China and Brazil. Javier Milei, Argentina's current president, also engaged in harsh rhetoric against China before he came to power, but quickly adopted a more conciliatory tone once in office to not jeopardize Chinese loans.

"Political relations with China would likely cool, but I wouldn't expect any substantial changes in economic and commercial relations," predicted Ricupero in case of a Bolsonaro victory.

Paz agreed that Flavio Bolsonaro was unlikely to take an extremely aggressive stance toward China in case of victory. He explained that, like Milei, Jair Bolsonaro had engaged in some sharp rhetoric against Beijing at the beginning of his term but had quickly softened his tone, given the fact that Brazil's agricultural sector in particular is so dependent on China.

Paz pointed out that the Bolsonaro family enjoyed most support in Brazil's rural regions, which made good money with China. "The unknown factor with Flavio Bolsonaro is how much pressure the US would exert so that Brazil distanced itself from China and to what extent he would yield to the pressure," said Paz.

If he wins, Flavio Bolsonaro is expected to dismantle policies that protect the environment Image: Bruna Prado/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

Brazil not likely to become major world player

Paz said that despite possessing enormous natural resources that are important to the global economy, Brazil would likely remain a minor player on the world stage as it had neither the economic strength to provide financial aid to other countries nor the military strength to help resolve conflicts. "This severely limits Brazil's ability to act," he said.

But Brazil could continue to be a major protagonist in the Global South, he said, as it is under Lula. "This is particularly evident in the international debate on global governance, in which Brazil raises issues such as new trading conditions, climate policy and development," he said.

Bolsonaro supporters, seen here with a Trump inflatable at a rally on September 7, favor a Brazil that is close to Trump's US Image: Alexandre Meneghini/REUTERS

Ricupero said Lula carried particular weight in foreign policy, especially regarding the environment and climate change. "His commitment to addressing ecological challenges was clear from his choice of [leading environmentalist] Marina Silva as environment minister," he said.

The former diplomat said he feared Flavio Bolsonaro would repeat the mistakes of his father, and this was one of the reasons the election was drawing such attention from around the world. He pointed out that Brazil had become more isolated after Jair Bolsonaro dismantled major environmental policies, adding that relations with the European Union had particularly suffered and negotiations on a trade agreement between Mercosur and the bloc had been put on hold. The deal was finally signed early this year.

This article was originally written in German.

Skip next section German FM Wadephul visits Canada as it prepares to become EU associate member

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul took a one-day break from the UN General Assembly in New York to visit Canada.

In light of the discussion about Canada’s possible associate membership in the European Union, he has called for people not to focus on words.

“In my view, this is less about terminology and more about ensuring that we truly deepen our cooperation in key areas,” Wadephul said during a meeting with his Canadian counterpart, Anita Anand, in the capital, Ottawa.

Wadephul said that both Canada and the EU have shown "great interest" in further deepening cooperation. The German government welcomes this and will hold further discussions on the matter, he added.

Wadephul and Anand signed a confidentiality agreement to facilitate the exchange of classified documents. This agreement was expected to bring significant benefits, particularly with regard to enhanced military and defense cooperation.

World.title: Iranian President Pezeshkian brought a diplomatic tone to New York for UNGA. What did his remarks signal?
World.content:
Iran's president used his trip to New York this week for the UN General Assembly to signal openness to talks over the nuclear dispute. However, the chances of a major breakthrough on the war remain low.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who traveled to New York to attend the UN General Assembly this week, specifically made time to meet with American journalists and media representatives.

In an interview with the conservative US broadcaster Fox News, he signaled a willingness to make concessions in the nuclear dispute with the United States.

Washington has made clear that Iran must never be allowed to possess nuclear weapons. Asked whether Iran was prepared to hand over its highly enriched uranium, Pezeshkian said his country would comply with its obligations under international law and the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

In its most recent assessment, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) estimated that Iran had more than 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to up to 60%.

Since the US-Israeli attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities in 2025, Iran has suspended its cooperation with the IAEA. The agency has continued to demand access to Iranian facilities and updated information on its nuclear stockpile and the whereabouts of its nuclear material.

Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran if no deal is reached To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Asked point-blank "Do you want a nuclear bomb or not?" during the exclusive interview on Fox News' "Special Report," Pezeshkian firmly rejected the premise.

"Not at all. Not at all. Our martyred, esteemed supreme leader had announced several times that, from a religious decree, it is unholy. It is illegal," he told host Bret Baier, referencing religious edicts issued against weapons of mass destruction.

Despite Pezeshkian's claims, the IAEA has assessed that Iran's fissile material is being enriched far beyond what is needed for civilian use.

Diplomacy: A first step?

A major breakthrough in the conflict between Iran and the United States is not expected anytime soon, Iran expert Arman Mahmoudian, a lecturer in Middle East Studies at the University of South Florida, told DW.

"Pezeshkian does not have the authority to initiate comprehensive de-escalation with the United States. In particular, hard-liners and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps appear to continue to wield considerable influence over Iran's decision-making process," he added.

Nevertheless, Mahmoudian thinks Pezeshkian's visit could help establish a more direct channel of communication between Tehran and Washington.

He also sees the possibility of creating a framework for future negotiations in New York, adding that the two sides could develop a road map that would pave the way for more substantive talks and, in the longer term, potentially contribute to de-escalation.

There are already signs of this, including meetings between Iranian and US delegations earlier this week. The White House, meanwhile, has confirmed that "positive and constructive" talks were continuing through intermediaries.

Hormuz — and Houthis — as leverage

The future of the Strait of Hormuz is also at the center of the discussions. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reportedly said that Tehran had presented Washington with a proposal to resume negotiations.

Under the proposal, the strategically important waterway could be reopened within seven days if certain conditions were met. It remains unclear what those conditions are.

In the past, Iran has demanded the release of frozen Iranian assets, an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports and vessels, and a commitment by Washington not to interfere in Iran's internal affairs.

Strike on Iran school: Did US commit a war crime? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The Strait of Hormuz, through which around 20 million barrels of oil normally pass every day — roughly 20% of global oil consumption — has become one of Iran's most important sources of leverage.

The United States has failed to eliminate all of Iran's capabilities to threaten shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, Kelly Grieco, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center, told DW in July.

This is despite the US attacks having caused significant damage to Iran's navy and defense industry.

"At a certain point, it becomes really hard to find some of these targets," said Grieco. "They're mobile. They're distributed."

Without a long-term strategy, Grieco warned, the United States could therefore become trapped in a recurring cycle: Iran rebuilds its military capabilities, Washington launches another round of attacks and the cycle repeats itself.

Nearly seven months after the start of the Iran war, the conflict has also spread to a second strategically important shipping route.

The Iran-backed Houthi movement has expanded its control over Yemen's Red Sea coast and the strategically important area around the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This gives Iran another important lever along major international shipping routes.

Balancing pressure and negotiations

Middle East expert Mahmoudian expects Iran to continue pursuing a dual strategy of military pressure and diplomacy, saying that Tehran is likely to continue using the Strait of Hormuz as leverage and to prevent a full return to normal shipping traffic.

Red Sea strains rattle energy markets To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"At the same time, Iran will most likely continue rebuilding its military and strategic infrastructure inside the country," he said. "Reports suggest that Iranian authorities are already moving quickly to reconstruct some damaged facilities."

On the diplomatic front, he added that Iran is likely to continue negotiations with the US, either directly or through intermediaries.

Tehran is aware that the current situation, with the continuing threat of military attacks, sanctions and economic pressure, is not sustainable in the long term, Mahmoudian said, adding that Iran will therefore continue to have an interest in reaching a political agreement with Washington.

A deal with Iran will require time and difficult negotiations, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in New York on September 23, playing down expectations of a quick agreement. At the same time, he stressed that President Donald Trump has military options at his disposal alongside the diplomatic route.

This article was originally written in German.

World.content:
Skip next section Albania's Rama tells of 'Flamingo Revolution,' warning not of a rogue AI, but one following rogue orders

Edi Rama's government was an early adopter of AI, but also had an early experience of its disruptive capabilities Image: Leonardo Munoz/AFP

Prime Minister Edi Rama told the chamber that while Albania was not a developer of "frontier models" in AI, "we are a nation that has already lived the future others are still debating," given how outside actors had tried out the technology's darker capabilites on its citizens.

Rama said he felt he owed the chamber a "simple message," if not necessarily the one most commonly discussed during the week.

"The greatest immediate danger is not that artificial intelligence will stop obeying humanity. The greatest danger is that it will obey the wrong human beings perfectly," he said.

"The public debate imagines machines that awaken, acquire ambitions and turn against their creators," Rama said. "But the systems confronting us today do not wake up with hatred in their hearts, they multiply ours. They have no ambition of their own, they serve the ambition of others. They carry no flag, but they can be deployed by a state. They tell no lie for their own benefit, but they can tell a billion lies on others' behalf."

Rama mentioned how Albania had become the first government to launch an AI minister. He said this showed his government's belief that "inside an accountable state," the technology could be used to "reduced the distance between citizens and public services."

But he said Albania had also learned how "artificial intelligence outside accountability can be used to eliminate the distance between a lie and the human mind."

He relayed the story of the so-called "Flamingo Revolution," a "fabricated narrative of an Israeli invasion of the Albanian coast."

This entirely fictional invasion "was manufactured, was personalized and delivered through voices, pages and channels citizens already trusted." Rama explained how the details of the overarching story were personalized to maximize their impact with the individuals reading them.

"Different fabriactions entered different emotional worlds, all serving the same strategic lie," he said. "The consequences were real. Citizens had their own reasons to protest — don't take me wrong. But suddenly, they started to protest also against a phantom enemy. Antisemitic tropes entered our public discourse for the first time ever."

Rama said that amid the AI disinformation drive, "fear became anger, anger became mobilization and fabrication became political reality."

"And this was not a laboratory experiment. I'm not talking to you about a science fiction movie. It was a Tuesday, in Tirana, our capital city."

Rama said it wasn't an algorithm that invented the objective, but rather a human actor. The algorithm didn't develop hatred, but "it discovered how to activate ours."

He called this particular use case "systematic fraud as a service," and warned its potential for use in scenarios like elections were just as real as in trying to amplify animosity to war in the Middle East.

World.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
World.content:
Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

"I personally don't feel safe as a citizen in my country and as a person who has worked for independent media for a long time," Georgian media expert and advocate for press freedom Nino Robakidze told DW. Her activism with international civil society groups has made her a target in her home country.

Similarly, Georgian journalists are currently facing "physical threats, digital threats, psychological threats. And there is also financial and legal pressure around their media organizations," she reported.

Robakidze was one of the participants at DW's panel discussion "Democracy under pressure? The situation for cultural and media professionals in Georgia," held on Thursday in Berlin's James-Simon-Galerie.

Host Jochen Rosenkranz, director of DW's Culture and Sports department, pointed out in his introduction that it had been difficult to find Georgians willing to participate in the panel. Many had refused, saying they feared the repercussions not only for themselves, but also for their friends and family.

"We're all afraid of the intimidation," Georgian-born musician, filmmaker, journalist and cultural organizer Marika Lapauri-Burk explained. She nevertheless agreed to take part in the discussion, alongside Nino Robakidze and journalist Juri Rescheto, head of DW's Riga bureau.

Jochen Rosenkranz, Marika Lapauri-Burk, Nino Robakidze and Juri Rescheto at the DW discussion panel 'Democracy under pressure? The situation for cultural and media professionals in Georgia' Image: Stephanie Englert/DW Images

Lapauri-Burk added that the government had become increasingly creative in its arbitrary reasons to detain those with critical voices.

Local civil society groups and human rights organizations estimate that from 90 to over 100 political dissidents and protesters are currently imprisoned or in pre-trial detention.

Russian influence impacting democratization efforts

Once thought of as a leading democracy of the Caucasus region, Georgia is undergoing a rapid transition toward authoritarianism under the Georgian Dream (GD) party, in power now since 2012.

The party originally declared itself pro-European, but in recent years has sought more overtly to align with Russia. The party gained an increased majority in a contested October 2024 parliamentary election.

A month later, the GD announced the suspension of EU accession negotiations until 2028, despite a substantial majority of Georgians strongly favoring European integration. Halting the talks ignited demonstrations across the country as the government increasingly aligned its policies with Moscow.

Demonstrators try to storm Georgia's presidential palace To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

But the transformation could be felt years before the election: "The real pressure on independent media and professional journalists escalated after Russia's unprovoked invasion in Ukraine," says Robakidze. An important anti-Western campaign followed the invasion, which "had a huge impact on Georgian media environment at large," she added.

The country was also rocked by anti-government protests in 2023-2024 as pro-EU protesters took to the streets. They were pushing back against new, Russian-style "foreign agents" legislation, which required all organizations that received foreign funding to register with the state and comply with extensive reporting requirements.

That came into force in June 2025, and a stricter version has introduced criminal liability and prison sentences of up to five years for individuals and groups who fail to register their activities as being "under foreign influence."

Nino Robakidze speaking at the panel 'Democracy under pressure? The situation for cultural and media professionals in Georgia' Image: Stephanie Englert/DW Images

Culture directly affected by the law

Many independent cultural institutions, festivals, arts organizations and heritage projects are heavily reliant on funding from the European Union, European foundations and international cultural programs.

Critics say the law stigmatizes institutions for their vaguely defined "foreign influence."

The same laws that target activists and journalists threaten the grants, partnerships and institutions that have connected Georgian artists to Europe for decades.

The state agency responsible for enforcing the "foreign agents" law, known as the Anti-Corruption Bureau, uses the law to persecute prominent civil society groups, launching inspections and freezing their bank accounts.

Another law also operates in tandem with the controversial "foreign agent" legislation.

Georgia's anti-LGBTQ law, officially a legislative package entitled "On Family Values and the Protection of Minors," explicitly bans the "popularization" or "propaganda" of same-sex relationships and non-binary gender identities in public spaces, media, education and the arts.

Freedom of expression under threat

Cultural producers are forced to risk choosing between self-censorship, shutting down entirely or facing severe state retaliation.

"The situation is becoming increasingly difficult for critical thinkers — especially artists," explained Juri Rescheto, who notes that many critical thinkers can be found within artistic circles. They are affected "not only in their art but also in their private lives," he added.

Rescheto cited the example of a small gallery he visited in the city of Gori, where protesters' slogans were projected onto a wall as part of an exhibition. It all felt "harmless, really — or so we would say here in the West," the journalist said. Yet the gallery is now facing closure because the city refuses to renew their lease since the action, he added.

A protest performance by the 'Vaso Abashidze State New Theater' in 2025 Image: Jerome Gilles/NurPhoto/picture alliance

Artists have generally been playing a powerful role in the protests: "There were many actions that were very artistically conceived," Lapauri-Burk noted.

"Ode to Joy" from Ludwig van Beethoven's 9th Symphony — the official anthem of the European Union — has often been played as a pro-European symbol of democratic resistance at anti-government protests in Tbilisi, Georgia, Rescheto added.

DW's new Georgian-language service

This year, Georgia is the focus of the Beethovenfest's Campus Project; a cultural exchange project developed in cooperation with DW.

"Music transcends borders and language barriers and brings people together," DW's director general Barbara Massing noted at the opening of the panel discussion, which also celebrated the recent launch of DW's new Georgian-language service on Instagram . Georgian has now become Deutsche Welle's 33rd language.

DW's director general Barbara Massing at the James-Simon-Galerie in Berlin Image: Stephanie Englert/DW Images

"With the new Georgian-language service in cooperation with France Medias Monde and TVP World, we are strengthening the European commitment to free media and trustworthy information in a region that is specifically targeted by disinformation campaigns and faces unique political and social challenges," said Massing.

Robakidze welcomes such an initiation supporting Georgians who still hope for a democratic future. Severe fatigue, state crackdowns and a sense of despair among participants is seeing protest dwindling. Even so, "We still need to remain ready to take action," she said. To that end, "We need all the media support we can get."

Edited by: Hans Kellett

World.title: La estafa del falso empleado de banca
World.content:
Recibir un SMS que alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en nuestra cuenta bancaria puede evitar que seamos víctima de un robo, excepto si no ha sido el banco quien realmente lo ha emitido

En la estafa del falso empleado de banca el delincuente primero envía un mensaje con una alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en la cuenta y facilita un enlace o un número de teléfono al que llamar. Ya en la conversación, intenta convencer a la víctima de que su dinero está en peligro para que autorice operaciones que resultarán fraudulentas

En 2025, Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) registró 25.133 casos de phishing. Durante los dos últimos años, tanto la Policía Nacional como la Guardia Civil y el Banco de España han emitido alertas sobre el aumento de las llamadas de falsos empleados bancarios.

TÉCNICAS DE MANIPULACIÓN

Autoridad Suplantan a profesionales pertenecientes a bancos a los que la víctima concede poder y confianza Urgencia Crean la sensación de que hay poco tiempo para actuar, lo que evita que la víctima reflexione o consulte con alguien Sobrecarga de información técnica Emplean jerga bancaria para intimidar y hacer creer que dominan una situación compleja Aumento gradual de las peticiones Incluye a la víctima en grupos de aplicaciones de mensajería para hacerle creer que mucha gente ya está ganando dinero

CIBEREXPERTO NOMBRE Jordi Sánchez CARGO Experto en fraude de CaixaBank “Durante la llamada, el estafador te hace creer que te está guiando para solucionar tu problema, pero en realidad, está intentando que tu hagas exactamente lo que necesita, emitir operaciones bancarias, descargar aplicaciones o facilitar información, como códigos o datos de tarjetas” Play / Pause CÓMO EVITAR LA ESTAFA DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA 1 Sospechar de mensajes inesperados. No clicar en ningún enlace que aparezca en el mensaje ni llamar al número que ofrecen. Ante la duda, siempre se debe llamar a los números oficiales del banco 2 Desconfiar de la urgencia y de las amenazas.Mensajes como “Su cuenta será bloqueada” buscan que se actúe sin pensar 3 No compartir claves ni códigos de verificación. El banco nunca solicitará contraseñas u otros códigos de seguridad 4 No descargar archivos ni instalar aplicaciones. Los estafadores pueden pedir que se descarguen programas que en realidad les están dando acceso al teléfono de la víctima

Una estafa que ha evolucionado. Este fraude comenzó como un SMS y una llamada, pero hoy se dan variantes como la que busca robar información de las tarjetas bancarias mediante el uso de la tecnología NFC del teléfono móvil. Este sistema de comunicación inalámbrica permite compartir información entre otros, tarjetas y móviles, y realizar pagos sin contacto. Los estafadores solicitan a la víctima que se descargue una aplicación maliciosa y que acerque la tarjeta al smartphone. Así, sus datos son enviados a otro teléfono de los atacantes, donde crearán una tarjeta de forma virtual con la que intentar sacar dinero o comprar en comercios.

El teléfono puede parecer auténtico. Los estafadores pueden hacer que en la pantalla del móvil de la víctima figure el mismo número que utiliza el banco para atender a sus clientes o que el SMS aparezca en el mismo hilo que las comunicaciones legítimas mediante una técnica que se conoce como spoofing (que significa suplantación).

Conocen datos personales de su víctima. En muchos casos, disponen de información de su objetivo, como el banco del que es cliente, parte del DNI o la dirección de correo electrónico.

Si ya se ha caído en la estafa. Se debe poner en conocimiento del banco de inmediato para que se puedan adoptar las medidas operativas oportunas. También es muy importante guardar las evidencias, como capturas de pantalla, SMS, correos y registro de llamadas. Presentar una denuncia ante la Policía Nacional o la Guardia Civil.

OTROS CASOS DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA

World.title: El curioso caso de los barrios con nombres inventados por las inmobiliarias en México
World.content:
Mientras las torres de lujo avanzan sobre zonas tradicionales y las familias enfrentan una presión creciente para vender sus casas y marcharse, las inmobiliarias rebautizan las colonias populares

Una imponente escultura metálica circular recibe a los visitantes del Cuadrante Polanco, un conjunto residencial de imponentes torres de departamentos en una zona de rápida transformación de Ciudad de México. En la acera de enfrente se construyen dos edificios más. Las torres del otro costado también aparecieron en los últimos cinco años. La grama (césped) está bien cuidada, los locales comerciales son prístinos y los guaruras (personal de seguridad privada) hacen sus rondas. Lo único que parece fuera de lugar es que, en realidad, no estamos en Polanco: las inmobiliarias que han levantado este nuevo barrio ostentoso han tomado prestado el nombre de la colonia de lujo por excelencia de la ciudad, con la que colindan.

La megalópolis de Ciudad de México, dividida en sus variopintas colonias —o urbanizaciones—, atraviesa una transformación acelerada y nada discreta. New Polanco, como se le dice con sorna, se asienta sobre manzanas que hasta hace pocas décadas constituían un parque industrial. En las inmediaciones conviven sedes de multinacionales, museos y concesionarios de Ferrari con fábricas de harina, estaciones eléctricas y hasta una planta cervecera que llena el aire con olor a cebada. El barrio, como otros similares en la ciudad, también es una expresión de los factores que están cambiando la cara a las zonas tradicionales y desplazando a las comunidades en las principales ciudades del país.

Un hombre camina en la cerrada Andrómaco, en Ciudad de México. Rodrigo Oropeza

Los expertos lo han definido como una doble crisis en el mercado: de oferta y de asequibilidad, traducida en el alza sostenida de los precios de compra y renta y en la inclinación del portafolio hacia unidades de mayor valor. La gentrificación se come los barrios populares y obliga a los habitantes que han convivido durante generaciones a buscar nuevos rumbos, muchas veces en las periferias. También produce barrios que no existen en los mapas o demarcaciones oficiales: “Condesa Sur”, “Roma Oriente” y “Reforma Norte” se apropian de los nombres de las urbanizaciones de mayor plusvalía con las que limitan, en un intento por justificar los altos precios.

“Pero esto no es Polanco. Lo quieren hacer para atraer más gente para vender sus departamentos”, corrige Alfredo Sánchez, funcionario público retirado que ha vivido toda su vida, 68 años, en la “Cerrada de Andrómaco”, un pasillo angosto que recorre la distancia de una cuadra y alberga coloridas casas de dos o tres pisos a ambos lados. El contraste es tangible. El vecindario popular, un vestigio de lo que fue la zona, se ha quedado atrapado entre un centro comercial y un parque infantil que, detrás de altas murallas, forma parte de las áreas comunes de un conjunto de torres residenciales.

Algunos habitantes de las casi 60 familias que viven ahí dicen que sienten la presión de las inmobiliarias para vender sus casas y ceder el espacio a nuevos complejos. Y aunque pueda parecer una oferta tentadora, aceptarla no les permitiría seguir viviendo en su zona: las propuestas rondan los 2 millones de pesos (unos 115.000 dólares), mientras que un departamento en el área cuesta más del doble, cerca de 350.000 dólares.

Vista aérea de la cerrada Andrómaco, en Ciudad de México. Emiliano Molina

En las principales ciudades —Ciudad de México, Guadalajara y Monterrey—, cerca del 78% del inventario digital de vivienda corresponde a propiedades de alto valor, según una radiografía del sector elaborada por Propiedades.com, un sitio web inmobiliario. “Esta configuración refleja una brecha importante entre la oferta digitalizada y las necesidades de vivienda asequible para una gran parte de la población”, agrega el estudio del segundo semestre del 2025.

La empresa, que rastrea aumentos de hasta 180% en las rentas en zonas de la capital, detalla que el encarecimiento ha desplazado a residentes hacia áreas aledañas con precios más accesibles, aunque estas “zonas de contención” comienzan a registrar un aumento en la demanda e indicios de revalorización. La Condesa y la Roma, donde palpita el corazón de la gentrificación de la capital, han empezado a desbordarse hacia otras comunidades, donde las fachadas art déco, que florecieron desde 1925, dan paso a edificios con gimnasio, terrazas y áreas infantiles.

En agosto de 2026, el precio promedio por metro cuadrado de vivienda en Ciudad de México se elevó un 4,4% y alcanzó cerca de 3.500 dólares, consolidándola como el precio más alto del país, de acuerdo con el seguimiento del banco Banorte. Según estudios académicos, es también la segunda ciudad más costosa de Latinoamérica, solo por detrás de Montevideo, en Uruguay, según el Relevamiento Inmobiliario de América Latina (RIAL) de la Universidad Torcuato Di Tella, en Argentina.

Fachada de la cerrada Andrómaco, en Polanco, el 10 de septiembre. Rodrigo Oropeza

La Administración de la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum ha reconocido el problema estructural, que también golpea el desempeño de la economía, y anunció el año pasado la meta de edificar y financiar 1,8 millones de viviendas populares, para beneficio de 12 millones de familias. En paralelo, el partido gobernante Morena promueve iniciativas legislativas en Ciudad de México para evitar que las desarrolladoras se asimilen a colonias de mayor plusvalía, en un intento que han denominado de publicidad engañosa y voracidad inmobiliaria. “Cuando cambia el nombre de un barrio, cambia quién puede vivir en ese barrio”, ha dicho la diputada local de Morena Cecilia Vadillo, quien promueve la propuesta.

Sin embargo, en la Cerrada de Andrómaco, que se ha hecho viral en redes sociales como reflejo de la disparidad, se quejan del abandono mientras temen por lo que pasará en los próximos años, mientras los servicios de electricidad y agua se han encarecido y han empezado a presentar fallas, dicen, ante el alto consumo de los vecinos. “Los políticos vienen, toman nota y se van. Nos preocupa que llegue un presidente al que se le bote la canica y nos diga que nos vamos porque nos vamos, con una indemnización que no nos alcance para vivir en la ciudad”, se queja José Mendoza, de 63 años. Su familia ha vivido en este pequeño vecindario durante tres generaciones. “Los de allá”, dice señalando los edificios en la otra acera, “quisieran que desapareciéramos”.

World.title: Odemira, una ruta por el concejo del Alentejo más salvaje
World.content:
Cerca de 50 kilómetros de costa, pueblos blancos y arenales vírgenes desfilan por el concejo más extenso de Portugal, una tierra marcada por la fuerza creativa y donde el interior rural choca con el océano

Es muy común encontrar al escalabardo por el Alentejo, irrumpiendo de pronto en los caminos o cruzando temerario la carretera. El escalabardo, conocido también como meloncillo, es un mamífero pequeño y alargado, de pelaje pardo y cabeza afilada, similar a un hurón o una comadreja. Un icónico animalito que, por su conexión con esta tierra portuguesa, también da nombre a una interesante iniciativa ambiental, social y comunitaria desarrollada en la localidad de São Luís. “Damos un nuevo uso a la ropa que se deshecha para que, en lugar de acabar en la basura, pueda reutilizarse de manera creativa”, explica Ana Baleia desde su sede en esta freguesia de la región de Odemira, trazada con casas blancas y calles empedradas.

La creatividad es, de hecho, la enseña que enarbola este concejo, el más extenso de Portugal, erigido en un importante foco de inspiración al que acuden numerosos artistas y creadores para desarrollar su talento. Odemira, parte del parque natural del Suroeste Alentejano y Costa Vicentina, está considerado uno de los rincones más salvajes del litoral portugués. Aquí, donde el interior rural se da de bruces con el océano, se concentra la naturaleza más pura. “Puede que sea la diversidad (el mar, el río, la llanura, la sierra) pero lo cierto es que todo en esta zona estimula la creación artística”, apunta Baleia, a propósito de tradiciones tan arraigadas como la cerámica, el mimbre o el trabajo en telares, que conviven con otras disciplinas más contemporáneas.

Más información Recorriendo Esposende, un museo moderno al aire libre único en Portugal

Los secretos del océano

A juicio de los artesanos, es la belleza del entorno la que mantiene vivas las costumbres en un rincón marcado por la presencia del agua. Considerado uno de los ríos más limpios de Europa, el Mira atraviesa la región del Alentejo con la peculiaridad de fluir de sur a norte y el privilegio de dejar a su paso todo un despliegue de paisajes vírgenes. Recorrer Odemira es descubrir llanuras doradas por el sol, colinas ondulantes y campos alfombrados de viñedos hasta donde alcanza la vista. Estampas que chocan de pronto con una costa escarpada que da lugar a acantilados, dunas y calas solitarias.

Cigüeñas blancas anidan en los salientes de los acantilados marinos, en cabo Sardão. Cristina Candel

Nada como aventurarse por este litoral embravecido para dar con playas tan espectaculares como Almograve, encajada entre oscuras formaciones rocosas, o Carvalhal, donde el oleaje favorece la práctica de surf, o la pequeña y recogida Nossa Senhora, a la que se accede por pasarelas de madera. Pero es cerca de la playa de Cavaleiro, concretamente en el cabo Sardão, donde acontece un fenómeno sin igual: este lugar es el único punto conocido en el planeta en el que las cigüeñas blancas anidan en los salientes de los acantilados marinos, en vez de hacerlo en los árboles o los tejados. Un comportamiento especial que se puede observar muy de cerca, sobre los farallones y con el Atlántico de fondo, especialmente durante la primavera.

Villas de ambiente marinero

Más allá de la naturaleza, esta región atesora toda la magia de los pueblos alentejanos, con su peculiar arquitectura de fachadas encaladas que contrastan con los zócalos pintados en azul. Pueblos que, fuera de la temporada alta, hacen gala de un ritmo pausado y de un ambiente acogedor en el que se respira una estrecha conexión con el mar. Empezando por el propio Odemira, que da nombre al concejo, allí donde el río comienza a ser navegable hasta toparse con el océano. Esta es una población encaramada sobre una colina, cuya actividad cultural se concentra en el Café-Librería Mirabolante, que a menudo organiza tertulias, recitales y exposiciones de arte.

Vila Nova de Milfontes, en la desembocadura del Mira, con la fortaleza de São Clemente integrada entre las playas fluviales y las casas blancas del casco antiguo. Cristina Candel

Situada en la desembocadura del Mira, a Vila Nova de Milfontes se la distingue por la majestuosa silueta de la fortaleza de São Clemente, integrada entre las playas fluviales y las casas blancas del casco antiguo. Un castillo que fue levantado para contener el ataque de los piratas que asolaron este tramo de costa, ya por entonces ribeteado de playas dunares y recoletas calas salvajes. Hoy, para descubrirlas a pie, a caballo o en bicicleta, existe toda una red de senderos que atraviesan esta localidad que, al no ser ni villa, ni nueva, ni disponer de mil fuentes, comparte con la cántabra Santillana del Mar el sambenito de “las tres mentiras”.

Vecinos de la pequeña villa marinera de Zambujeira do Mar. Cristina Candel

Estos mismos caminos discurren por Zambujeira do Mar, una pequeña villa marinera que se posa sobre un acantilado para asomarse a uno de los arenales más impactantes del sur de Portugal. En su entramado, apenas compuesto por unas cuantas callejuelas que siempre acaban en el océano, no falta alguna fachada señorial, pequeñas muestras de arte urbano y la Capela de Nossa Senhora do Mar, la cual, por su posición sobre un promontorio con vistas a la playa y el pueblo, resulta una localización excelente para contemplar la puesta de sol.

Unas notas de ‘saudade’

Fue la calma de esta región la que logró cautivar a la reina portuguesa del fado. Cuentan que Amália Rodrigues, quien eligió como refugio vacacional al discreto pueblo de Brejão (entre Odemira y Zambujeira) para huir del bullicio de Lisboa, alumbró muchas de sus canciones mirando a ese Atlántico que irrumpía de pronto tras sortear un camino de juncos. En su honor, este mismo paraje fue rebautizado como la Praia da Amália, en el punto donde la artista acudía para guarecerse del mundo.

Mural con la imagen de Amália Rodrigues firmado por el artista urbano Ivo Santos, en Brejão. Cristina Candel

Pero también su memoria ha quedado impresa en las paredes de Brejão a través de los murales pintados por el artista urbano Ivo Santos en el verano de 2018. Cuatro retratos gigantescos de quien conjugó su voz única con hermosos versos de poetas antiguos para hacer de este género musical un desgarrado canto a la nostalgia. Con su recuerdo permanece viva la saudade de esta tierra impregnada de océano: “Ven a saber si el mar tendrá razón / Ven acá a ver bailar mi corazón”.

World.title: 10 experiencias en el Matarraña para sacarle todo el jugo a la comarca aragonesa en septiembre
World.content:
Pedalear por la vía verde de la Val de Zafán, caminar por el Solo Sculpture Trail, dormir en un antiguo molino de papel y más pistas en esta zona de la provincia de Teruel que es tierra de cañones y, sobre todo, de buitres

Wikipedia dice, todo el mundo repite —incluida la IA—, y será verdad mientras no se demuestre lo contrario, que el río mediterráneo mejor conservado del planeta es el Matarraña. Este afluente del Ebro, de casi 100 kilómetros de longitud, ha dado nombre a la comarca en la que Teruel se funde y confunde con Tarragona y Castellón, y ha labrado las rocas calizas de los Puertos de Beceite, donde nace, como si en vez de agua pura llevara carburo de silicio verde, abrasivo y cortante a más no poder. Aparte de fabulosos cañones y de pozas que piden a gritos bañarse hasta bien entrado el otoño, este rincón del noreste de la provincia de Teruel tiene muchas otras cosas que sorprenden al viajero.

La primera es que aquí no hablan como los demás turolenses, sino chapurriau, una variedad aragonesa del catalán cantarina y cadenciosa que, a los forasteros, salvo que sean de las provincias de al lado, les suena a valenciano. Matarraña —o Matarranya, como lo escriben también— es un no parar de sorpresas. Tomen nota de estas 10.

Más información 24 horas en Ayamonte, la ciudad de Huelva donde vivir uno de los mejores atardeceres de Europa

Penetrar en la comarca siguiendo a un tren loco

Por Matarraña pasó un tren hoy difícil de explicar, que iba de La Puebla de Híjar a Tortosa, del norte de Teruel al Bajo Ebro, y que pretendía llegar algún día hasta la orilla del mar. Un loco sueño ferroviario que duró 30 años (de 1941 a 1971) y que dejó este abrupto y solitario rincón del mapa aragonés lleno de puentes inútiles y de estaciones en mitad de ninguna parte.

Se esfumó el tren, pero su itinerario y su espíritu insensatos permanecen en la vía verde de la Val de Zafán. Una buena manera de hincarle el diente a la comarca es echarse a pedalear desde la que fue la estación de Valjunquera con las bicis y los guías de Senda. Salvo en un par de túneles, que no se ve nada, se va descubriendo un paisaje cada vez más ordenado de olivos y almendros y una luz cada vez más mediterránea. Hay una parada obligada en el alto viaducto que hay a 9,5 kilómetros del inicio, para saludar al río Matarraña. Al otro lado, en otra antigua estación, se halla el muy recomendable hotel La Parada del Compte.

Comer lo que comió Picasso

Pedaleando por una vía verde llana no es que se haga mucho ejercicio, pero hambre sí que se hace. Para calmarla, no hay mejor opción en toda la comarca que Fonda Alcalá. Ubicado en Calaceite, miembro de la Asociación Los Pueblos Más Bonitos de España, por esta casa de comidas algo más que centenaria —data de 1922— han pasado García Márquez, Álvaro Cunqueiro, Francesc Català Roca, Paco de Lucía, Serrat… No en este orden, lógicamente. El que no pasó, pero sí comió lo que aquí se hace, fue Picasso. Les perdius de Picasso, las perdices que le guisaron en esta casa y le llevaron enlatadas a Francia en 1967, y las judías blancas de Beceite con sardinas de cubo son dos platos legendarios, fundamentales. Pero el chef Ignacio Alcalá se inventa todos los días otros más excitantes y divertidos, que es lo que aprendió a hacer en las cocinas de Neichel y Can Roca.

Hacer senderismo en una galería de arte

He aquí sin duda lo más flipante de la comarca, naturaleza aparte: Solo Houses, una hermosa finca campestre de 200 hectáreas en el municipio de Cretas, donde llevan 13 años materializándose como naves alienígenas casas alucinantes de arquitectos de vanguardia que se pueden alquilar desde 850 euros por noche y donde pronto lo hará un hotel de habitaciones circulares exentas, con vistas al bosque diseñado por Smiljan Radić, Premio Pritzker 2026. Obviamente, alojarse aquí es solo para amantes de la arquitectura y gente con pasta.

Una mujer pasea entre esculturas del Solo Sculpture Trail, en la localidad de Cretas. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

El resto debe contentarse con ver los ovnis de lejos, paseando entre las vides de la bodega Venta D’Aubert y las esculturas del Solo Sculpture Trail, un circuito creado por los propietarios de todo esto, los galeristas Christian Bourdais y Eva Albarrán, para exponer al aire libre y vender obras que tampoco parecen de este mundo. Se tarda hora y media en ver las 20 esculturas y solo cuesta cinco euros. También se puede visitar la bodega y catar cinco de sus vinos por 25.

La bodega Venta D’Aubert. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Asomarse a la vecina Tarragona por un desfiladero

Si pasear por un sendero de pago entre esculturas carísimas parece algo pijo y rebuscado, en el pueblo de al lado, en Arnes, podemos hacerlo en un lugar verdaderamente salvaje, el desfiladero de Els Estrets, y bañarnos en las aguas inmaculadas del río que lo atraviesa —un afluente del río Algás, que a su vez lo es del Matarraña—, sin pagar un euro. Al llegar al aparcamiento donde arranca la senda, descubriremos estupefactos Les Gronses, unas formidables moles anaranjadas donde pululan escaladores, cabras monteses y buitres leonados.

El desfiladero de Els Estrets, en la vecina Terra Alta de Tarragona. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Y nada más echarnos a andar, un cartel que dice: “Parc Natural dels Ports”. Estamos en Cataluña, concretamente en la Terra Alta de Tarragona. Otro cartel advierte que el baño solo está permitido en el Toll Blau (el charco azul). Allí veremos dos o tres humanos y, más adelante, si es que se dejan ver, alguna nutria y la libélula Macromia splendens, en peligro de extinción. Mucho más fácil de observar, libando en las lavandas, es la mariposa Cleopatra. El desfiladero se recorre, yendo y volviendo por camino evidente, en un par de horas.

Dormir en un antiguo molino de papel

Vistas desde el hotel La Fábrica de Solfa, en Beceite. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Beceite, además de un bonito pueblo, con muchas de sus casas colgadas sobre el encañonado río Matarraña, es el campo base ideal para explorar la comarca, porque está cerca de su paraje más deseado —el Parrizal, donde nace aquél— y porque hay un hotelito familiar que es un hotelazo. La Fábrica de Solfa, que así se llama, fue un molino de papel: con la fuerza del río se trituraba ropa vieja y se obtenía la pasta necesaria. Ahora es una fábrica de actividades: todas las que se cuentan en este reportaje y algunas más. De amorosos cuidados que prodigan Javier y Alberto Moragrega a los que llegan exhaustos después de hacerlas. Y de ricos platos: el recapte de fesols de Beceite, el ternasco de Aragón, las texturas de té de roca y todo lo que se sirve en el restaurante Marca al Agua. Tampoco se desayuna mal, viendo a las nutrias jugar en el río saltarín. Lo único malo es que aparecen al rayar el sol, así que hay que madrugar.

Darse un baño de multitudes y otro en un ‘fish spa’ natural

A solo tres kilómetros de Beceite se encuentra el Parrizal (o Parrissal), el desfiladero que nadie que visita esta comarca deja de admirar y recorrer, a tal punto que hay que reservar online para evitar mayores aglomeraciones de las que ya se forman sobre las tablas de dos palmos de ancho que hay instaladas en las paredes verticales del cañón, a buena altura sobre las aguas impolutas del recién nacido Matarraña. Avanzar nadando por el propio río, que sería lo deseable para librarse del sudor propio y de los atascos, está prohibido.

Pasarelas en la senda del Parrizal. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Donde sí está permitido mojarse y remojarse es en La Pesquera, en las pozas que forma el río Ulldemó, afluente del Matarraña, a tres kilómetros también de Beceite. Comparadas con las de otros ríos de montaña, estas aguas de hipnótico color verde jade son hasta cálidas. Y mucho más relajantes: metes los pies y acuden docenas de diminutos barbos y madrillas a limpiar tus células muertas. Esto es ictioterapia y La Pesquera, un fish spa natural, sin kimonos ni musiquillas new age.

Remar con el último sol en el pantano de Pena

Kayak al atardecer en el pantano de Pena. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

A la misma distancia de Beceite que el Parrizal y La Pesquera, está el pantano de Pena, uno de los más antiguos de Teruel (de 1930) y el único de la cuenca del Matarraña. Si hubiera muchos pantanos, no sería el río mediterráneo mejor conservado del mundo. Ir allí a navegar en kayak al atardecer es una de las actividades que recomienda y organiza La Fábrica de Solfa. Desde el hotel se llega con una bici eléctrica en un cuarto de hora y, después de rodear el embalse en media más, se embarca y se rema hasta el centro para admirar cómo el penúltimo sol se duplica en la cabecera y el agua se vuelve de oro. Girando luego el kayak en redondo y apuntando con la proa hacia el noreste, se ve cómo los últimos rayos iluminan la Caixa, una cumbre que a los matarrañeses les parece que tiene forma de caja de caudales y por eso la llaman así. Si remando y girando se vuelca accidentalmente, o adrede para refrescarse, no pasa nada: aquí está permitido el baño.

Asistir al banquete de 500 aves carroñeras

José Ramón Moragrega entre buitres en el Observatorio de Aves Mas de Bunyol. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

En la sierra de Arca, donde está la Caixa, anidan multitud de buitres leonados. No es solo que allí hay cortados rocosos idóneos para ellos. Es que al pie de la montaña, en una masía de Valderrobres, vive José Ramón Moragrega, que lleva más de 30 años alimentándolos. Todos los días, Buitreman —así le llaman— sale a las 9.15 con una carretilla llena de pulmones de cerdo y la vuelca ante una muchedumbre expectante de estas enormes carroñeras. Hasta 500 de ellas se reúnen para compartir de muy malos modos este desayuno, formando una monumental tremolina de polvo, chillidos e iracundos aleteos. Todo puede verse y fotografiarse en el Observatorio de Aves Mas de Bunyol, una masía que es también un formidable hide, con grandes ventanales orientados a los cuatro vientos para no perderse nada, desde el momento en que Buitreman vuelca la carretilla y se aparta a toda velocidad de sus pequeños de picos afilados como cuchillos —por eso va con casco, porque más de una vez ha salido descalabrado—, hasta cuando aparecen los alimoches para disputarse las migajas de la tragantona.

Al despedirse de los visitantes, Moragrega les confía casi entre lágrimas su delicado estado de salud y que sus niños pueden quedarse pronto sin desayuno si alguna entidad pública o privada no asume la gestión del observatorio, que es también alojamiento rural. Es un negocio rentable, asegura.

Vuelta a las rocas huesudas del Masmut

Muchos buitres leonados que desayunan en Mas de Bunyol pasan el resto del día haciendo la digestión en las Rocas del Masmut, en Peñarroya de Tastavins, donde hay una importante colonia de ellos. El PR TE-157, uno de los Senderos Turísticos de Aragón, bien mantenido y señalizado, invita a rodear este manojo de peñas anaranjadas de más de 100 metros de altura, similares a los Mallos de Riglos, cuyo nombre se cree que viene de los masmuda, una tribu bereber que quizá estuviera asentada aquí cuando España era musulmana.

Es una ruta circular de poco más de tres horas, cuatro si el senderista se desvía a los tres kilómetros para subir al mirador del Masmut. Situado a 500 metros de las rocas y a similar altura, es un buen lugar para verlas como las ven los buitres, asomando como las falanges de un gigante muerto y enterrado bajo la costra caliza del Matarraña.

Un pícnic regenerativo para despedirse del Matarraña

La última sorpresa de esta ruta llena de ellas la puede dar Tel·lúric, una masía centenaria del municipio de Ráfels cuyos nuevos propietarios no es que respeten la tradición agrícola de los masos, de estas catedrales civiles del campo matarrañés, es que van un paso más allá. O un paso más acá, porque trabajan la tierra con tal cuidado que no solo no se agota, sino que se regenera. Los olivos, los almendros y las viñas que atiende Sorin Dragoman no son soldados invasores de ejércitos cuadriculados, sino pacíficos hermanos de los pinos, las carrascas, el tomillo, el romero, el té de roca y el poleo.

Con todo lo que aquí se produce (vinos, aceite y almendras con certificación ecológica y de agricultura regenerativa) dispuesto sobre un mantel a cuadros, y también con las carnes a la brasa que salen sin parar de la cocina, se organizan unos pícnics delante de la masía que son una manera estupenda de despedirse del Matarraña. El águila culebrera sobrevuela los cultivos de Tel·lúric sin sospechar que son cosa de humanos.

World.title: New group home for psychiatric patients tried in Rotterdam
World.content:
Rotterdam is to set up a new type of supervised accommodation for homeless people with serious psychiatric problems and addiction issues.

Forty people will be brought together under one roof in Poortugaal, a village near Rotterdam that is also home to a forensic psychiatric clinic, in a supervised environment where they can receive more structured support.

The residents will be allowed to stay in the facility for up to eight years, receiving long-term and structured support that is often lacking in temporary accommodation.

Around 1,500 people in the Netherlands are classed as posing a high risk to public safety. They often have learning difficulties, suffer from psychiatric illness and struggle with addiction, which can lead to aggressive, disruptive or deranged behaviour in public.

Many of the patients have spent their lives alternating between living on the streets and being incarcerated in clinics or prisons, posing a danger to themselves and others.

Pillar to post

“They get passed from pillar to post when what they really need is intensive support for several years,” Laura van Goor, of Artes, the organisation running the facility, told Nieuwsuur. “But we don’t have that right now in the Netherlands.”

Psychiatric clinics are intended for short stays of around three months, but patients often end up staying longer to prevent them ending up back on the streets.

But the treatment is short-term and keeping patients in care for longer adds to waiting lists.

Van Goor said the patients would have more freedom to move around on the campus than in smaller-scale facilities, while also benefiting from a more structured regime. They will not be allowed out unsupervised.

Drink and drugs will be formally banned, unlike in temporary housing where usage is usually tolerated. “But it’s not a case of ‘if you use, you’re out,’ Van Good said. “That’s not possible: 95% of them have drug problems.”

World.content:

Almost half of Dutch people say that have experience social nuisance in their neighborhood, from noisy neighbors to the drug trade, according to new figures from the Dutch statistics office.

The CBS released its biennial Safety Monitor on Friday, which found that 42% of adults say they dealt with some type of anti-social behaviour near their homes during 2025.

The report looks at crime and safety issues across the country.

The largest number of complaints stem from loitering youth, which make up 26% of the reported problems. Issues with neighbors account for 20% of the concerns.

Overall problems with nuisance have risen in the past few years. Some 14% of people say they have experienced significant social nuisance in their neighborhood, up from 12% in 2021.

Those living in urban areas have the most problems. City residents report nearly four times the number of issues than non-urban dwellers.

World.title: Cabinet wants private companies to pay more towards gas storage
World.content:
The Dutch government wants to make private companies responsible for storing gas for the winter to cut its liabilities as prices on the markets soar.

At the moment the cost of filling the four gas storage facilities in Norg, Grijpskerk, Bergermeer and Alkmaar is met by the government-funded operator Energie Beheer Nederland, but soaring gas prices mean they are facing a €1 billion loss.

Private companies have no commercial incentive to stock up on gas for the winter because prices are currently forecast to drop after the autumn.

Demand has been stoked by the need for European governments to meet EU-set targets to fill their gas reserves by the start of November. The Netherlands last week reduced its target figure from 74% to 64%. The current storage level is 57.5%.

Under EU rules the Dutch government is also not allowed to keep the stored gas it buys for itself, but must export it to other member states who need it, as well as the UK, which has limited gas storage facilities.

The Netherlands’ facilities date from the time when it exported gas from the Slochteren field in Groningen, but since it was forced to end production two years ago because of earthquakes in the northern province it has filled the chambers with imported gas.

LNG imports

The high cost of importing liquefied national gas from the United States, which is the main supplier, have added to the government’s costs.

It wants to pass on the cost to commercial companies such as Essent, Eneco and Vattenfall by making it mandatory for them to build up their own reserves. A similar obligation is in force in Austria.

“At the moment there is virtually no market in the Netherlands for storing gas in the seasonal storage facilities, even though seasonal storage is an essential element of supply guarantee in the portfolio of suppliers’ prospectuses,” the letter, sent from the ministry of economic affairs, said.

“The question is whether the bill should continue to be met by the Dutch taxpayer, or whether supply guarantee can be be ensured through a different mix of measures for a lower cost.”

World.title: Xavi satisfied as Gakpo earns Oranje late draw against Germany
World.content:
New Dutch national football coach Xavi Hernandez declared himself satisfied with his team’s performance following the 1-1 draw with Germany in Amsterdam.

Cody Gakpo converted a magnificent skewered pass by debutant Ruben van Bommel with a crashing volley in stoppage time to earn Oranje the point their second-half dominance deserved.

“We were a little nervous in the first half, but the second half is the way we want to play,” the Spaniard said after the opening game in the Nations League, his first match since being appointed last month.

Germany took the lead in the 32nd minute when Felix Nmecha pounced on a loose ball in the penalty, but the Dutch were aggrieved that their opponents had played on after Brian Brobbey went down injured in the centre circle.

Captain Virgil van Dijk said: “We thought the ball should have gone out, but it didn’t go out, and it was unfortunate that it fell right in front of them after a good block by Jan Paul van Hecke.”

Van Dijk had the ball in the net after 15 minutes, but his header was disallowed after the referee decided Brobbey had impeded goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen.

Zierkzee recall

Brobbey was replaced by AZ striker Mexx Meerdink, who missed a glorious chance to equalise on his debut after Crysencio Summerville made space in the penalty area with a smart turn.

On Friday Xavi called up Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee, who last played for the national team two years ago, as a replacement for Brobbey ahead of the next Nations League match against Serbia in Belgrade on Sunday.

Van Bommel, who became the third generation of his family to play for Oranje after and his father, Mark, his grandfather, Bert van Marwijk, came on in the second half and capped his debut with the assist that set up Gakpo’s goal.

“I ran forward and I saw Cody free at the far post, and I thought, I have to get it to him somehow. It wasn’t an easy finish, but the pass wasn’t bad either,” the PSV winger said.

Another second-half substitute was Borussia Dortmund midfielder Joey Veerman, who made his first appearance in an orange shirt for two years after being frozen out of the international set-up by Xavi’s predecessor Ronald Koeman. Veerman came on for Marseille’s Quinten Timber, who was selected to take the place of the injured Frenkie de Jong.

World.title: Dutch PM Jetten warns “hands off the ICC” in debut UN speech
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten gave a fiery address to the United Nations on Thursday, defending the International Criminal Court and the rule of law.

“Hands off the ICC and all those other institutions that protect the international legal order,” he said in his first address at the UN’s annual meeting in New York.

Although Jetten did not call out American president Donald Trump specifically, the speech came after reporting earlier this week that the United States is planning to escalate its fight with the ICC and sanction the institution as a whole as part of its campaign to dismantle the court “brick by brick”.

The White House has already sanctioned 13 staff members, including court president, Japanese Judge Tomoko Akane, over the investigation into alleged Israeli war crimes in Gaza.

“Take, for example, the attempts to undermine the International Criminal Court – a court based in my country, in my city. This undermines the international legal order as a whole. And that affects us all,” Jetten said.

As the court’s host state, the Netherlands is obliged to provide assistance such as cooperation with security, facilitating visas and transporting defendants and witnesses.

He also called for Russia to be held accountable for the war in Ukraine. “In this conflict, Ukraine has no choice but to defend itself,” said Jetten. “But Russia chooses to wage war day after day,” he said.

World.title: Van Weel survives no-confidence debate over crime stats row
World.content:
Justice minister David van Weel has survived a motion of no confidence after he apologised to MPs who accused him of misleading them over police crime figures.

MPs called an emergency debate on Thursday over the minister’s response to reports that police had not responded to some 10,000 criminal complaints because they lacked the capacity to do so.

Van Weel told parliament in June that more than half the cases were reports of crimes rather than official complaints, which police are required to investigate.

But he was corrected by the government’s audit office, the Algemene Rekenkamer, which said in its annual report to parliament that only 10% of the cited cases were verbal reports.

“The consequence is that victims of crimes such as sexual offences and serious theft had not had justice and these serious cases have not had any significant attention,” the auditors wrote.

Van Weel initially tried to shrug off the reprimand as a “difference of insight”, but after MPs called a debate and tabled a motion of no confidence he attempted to apologise for his choice of words.

Measures of crime

The minister blamed the confusion on the different criteria used to measure the seriousness of the complaint. Police prioritise crimes based on how much evidence is available to start an investigation, such as witness statements and camera footage, while auditors use the “Crime Harm Index”, which looks at the severity of sentences imposed by courts.

Van Weel acknowledged that he had “given the impression” that he “had trivialised the seriousness of the Court of Audit’s report”, but insisted: “That doesn’t make it wrong information.

Opposition MPs said the minister’s explanation did not go far enough and threatened to back a motion of no confidence tabled by the far-right PVV, which would have forced Van Weel to resign.

Different attitude

“The minister has had several chances to say he gave parliament the wrong impression, but hasn’t taken them,” said Caroline van der Plas of the farmers’ party BBB.

Van Weel made a second, stronger apology that stopped short of admitting he had misled MPs, which was enough to persuade all parties not to vote for the motion, with the exception of the PVV and Forum voor Democratie.

“I realise now, after your contributions, that I intentionally or unintentionally gave you the wrong impression and that you felt misled,” he said. “That was never my intention, but it shouldn’t have happened.”

“At the last minute we saw a different attitude,” Ingrid Coenradie of right-wing opposition party JA21 commented. “We would have liked to have seen that at the start.”

The Polish government has granted same-sex couples who married abroad and have had their wedding certificates transcribed into the Polish registry the same tax rights as other married couples. The decision follows a ruling by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) requiring Poland – whose domestic law does not allow same-sex couples to form any type of legal union – to recognise same-sex marriages contracted in other EU member states. Podpisałem dziś interpretację ogólną, która zapewnia, że osoby, które uzyskały transkrypcję aktu małżeństwa będą miały w polskich urzędach skarbowych takie same prawa i obowiązki podatkowe jak wszyscy małżonkowie. — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) September 24, 2026 “Today, I signed a general interpretation ensuring that persons who have obtained a transcription of their marriage certificate will have the same tax rights and obligations in Polish tax offices as all other married couples,” announced finance minister Andrzej Domański in a social media post. A general interpretation is an official position taken by the finance ministry aiming to clarify the application of tax law in a specific area. Among the benefits that couples with a transcribed foreign marriage certificate can now receive include preferential treatment under inheritance and gift tax rules and the ability to file joint personal income tax returns. Couples may also pay tax on behalf of a spouse and refuse to testify as a witness in proceedings involving their spouse. “This is about basic equality, justice and fairness,” Domański told broadcaster TVN. “We want these rights to be enforceable in an effective way.” The finance minister said that the decision would have a “negligible” impact on the state budget. He also noted that such couples would be subject to the obligations that apply to other married couples in Poland, which include liability for their spouse’s tax obligations. Osoby, które uzyskały tak zwaną transkrypcję aktu małżeństwa, będą miały przed polskimi urzędami skarbowymi dokładnie takie same prawa i obowiązki jak pozostali małżonkowie – powiedział minister finansów Andrzej Domański w rozmowie z Grzegorzem Kajdanowiczem w @faktypofaktach w… pic.twitter.com/uVwDaD3ZDk — tvn24 (@tvn24) September 24, 2026 The finance minister’s decision has drawn criticism from right-wing politicians, who argue that recognition of same-sex marriage violates the constitution, which states that “marriage, being a union of a man and a woman, shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland”. Paweł Szefernaker, chief of staff to President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, said Domański’s actions were “inconsistent with the constitution” and had been carried out “without legislation, without debate, without honestly telling Poles what is really happening”. “Everyone has the right to a private life,” he added. “However, the state has a duty to protect the legal order and provide tax support for marriage.” Patryk Jaki, a deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s largest opposition party, said that the finance minister’s actions “clearly violate Polish law and will have legal implications in the future” for Domański, who is “writing additional points in the indictment against himself”. Sławomir Mentzen, one of the leaders of the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) group, said the tax interpretation “will be revoked on the very first day” if his party comes to power. To jest niezgodna z Konstytucją próba faktycznego zrównania małżeństwa ze związkami jednopłciowymi. Bez zmiany Konstytucji, bez ustawy, bez debaty, bez uczciwego powiedzenia Polakom, co naprawdę się dzieje. Każdy ma prawo do prywatnego życia według własnych wyborów. Ale państwo… https://t.co/0CQ9Lnfl02 — Paweł Szefernaker 🇵🇱 (@szefernaker) September 24, 2026 The changes follow a ruling issued by the CJEU in November 2025 ordering Poland to recognise same-sex marriages contracted in other EU states. The court found that failing to do so infringes the freedom to move and reside within the EU as well as the right to respect for private and family life. In light of that ruling, in March this year, Poland’s own Supreme Administrative Court (NSA) ordered Warsaw’s registry office to recognise a marriage conducted by two Polish men in Germany by transcribing it into the Polish civil registry. In May, the Polish government issued a regulation allowing such transcriptions of foreign same-sex marriages to take place nationwide. It went into force in August. However, even before then, some cities had begun transcribing marriage certificates, beginning with Warsaw and Wrocław in May. At the end of August, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski reported that 84 same-sex couples had already transcribed their foreign marriages under the government’s new regulation. Poland has begun paying benefits to same-sex couples who married abroad then entered their marriage into the Polish registry. The EU court ordered Poland to recognise such marriages, even though domestic law does not allow for any form of same-sex union https://t.co/svnRjyBO8Q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 22, 2026 While foreign same-sex marriages can now be entered into Poland’s civil registry, questions have remained as to what that will mean in practice for such couples, especially as domestic law does not recognise same-sex relationships. In another development, labour minister Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk announced last week that the Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) has begun paying care allowances to qualifying same-sex couples who married abroad and have had their wedding certificates transcribed into the Polish registry.
