World.title: Here’s How the New Zagreb Pedestrian Zone Will Look
World.content:
September the 25th, 2026 – The brand new Zagreb pedestrian zone has been presented as part of European Mobility Week.

Zagreb’s city administration has emphasised that the presented solution retains hospitality terraces as an important part of the social life of the Lower Town, but provides for their uniform design and better integration into the public space. Poslovni reports that three years after the temporary arrangement of the pedestrian zone in Masarykova Street, the City of Zagreb has presented the project for its permanent and comprehensive arrangement that covers Masarykova and Teslina streets as well as parts of Preradovićeva and Gajeva up to Berislavićeva Street.

The project envisages uniform paving of the entire space, divided into a pedestrian zone and a calmed traffic zone between Republic of Croatia Square and Gundulićeva Street, as well as the formation of new public focal points at key intersections and points within the zone. Special emphasis has been placed on the greening of the space. The planting of around 50 new trees connected into a continuous tree line between the two arms of the Green Horseshoe is planned, along with additional green surfaces, urban furniture, drinking water fountains and spaces for rest. The project also includes new bicycle parking, zones for short-term stopping and delivery, as well as a series of measures that improve accessibility for persons with disabilities and the safety of all users of the space.

a unique and well connected pedestrian zone in the heart of zagreb

The conceptual design was prepared by the Institute for Spatial Planning of the City of Zagreb, and an extensive participatory process included citizens, residents, business users and experts of various profiles, it was announced on Thursday from the Office of Zagreb Mayor Tomislav Tomašević.

Zagreb Deputy Mayor Luka Korlaet said that by arranging the pedestrian zone they are creating a complete public space intended for safer and higher-quality pedestrian movement, staying, socialising and public events. It is especially important, he says, that they are connecting the existing pedestrian spaces and expanding the pedestrian zone on the northern arms of the Green Horseshoe, from Republic of Croatia Square to Zrinjevac. In this way they are creating a unique, connected and passable pedestrian whole in the very centre of Zagreb, Korlaet emphasised.

Director of the Institute for Spatial Planning Nikša Božić said that an interdisciplinary team of the Institute worked on the project, which brought together architects, landscape architects, traffic experts and other collaborators.

“It is particularly important to us that through the preparation of the conceptual design we built on the tradition of arranging public spaces that the Institute developed in previous decades, participating in projects such as the arrangement of Jurišićeva and Draškovićeva streets, the Stock Exchange Square and other important city locations,” Božić said.

what are the top priorities?

He noted that in preparing the solution the Institute took into account the collected views, proposals and needs of citizens as well as the results of expert analyses of the space and its development potentials.

The results of a survey fully completed by around 3,400 citizens showed that 88.4 percent of participants support the comprehensive arrangement of the space. The temporary arrangement was rated as positive or extremely positive by 76 percent of respondents, while 72 percent of them supported the expansion of the pedestrian zone to Teslina and Gajeva streets. As the most important priorities citizens highlighted more greenery, benches and spaces for staying, as well as better organisation of traffic and delivery.

World.title: Zagreb City Break, Remote-Worker Style – Why 90 Days Could Be All You Need
World.content:
September the 25th, 2026 – Zagreb is an up and coming city break, but it could be more than that thanks to the remote worker boom. Many talk about Croatia’s famed “digital nomad visa”, but 90 days and zero admin could be all you need.

Not every remote worker wants (or needs) a full digital nomad visa. For many professionals, the classic Croatian “temporary stay of digital nomads” route – with its income thresholds, documentation piles and multi-month planning – is overkill. If your passport already allows visa-free entry to the Schengen area, you can simply turn up and stay for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. That window is long enough to settle into a real routine, yet short enough to feel like an extended city break rather than a bureaucratic relocation. Zagreb is perfectly suited to this lighter approach.

the 90 day limit could be all you need

Unlike the coastline and the islands, which swing between peak-season summer intensity and winter quiet, Zagreb functions as a proper European capital all year. Trams run, cafes stay open, co-working spaces keep their regular hours, and the cultural calendar never really stops. You get the infrastructure of a serious city without the summer price spikes that hit Split or Dubrovnik.

Reliable high-speed internet is the baseline, not a luxury. The co-working scene is mature and varied – from community-focused hubs to quieter central spots – so you can choose between focused workdays and networking as the mood takes you. Plenty of remote workers simply rotate between a well-chosen apartment and a handful of cafes with strong Wi-Fi and power sockets; the cafe culture here is built for lingering.

a big-little city with plenty to offer

Outside working hours, the city rewards curiosity. Upper Town’s cobbled streets and the instantly recognisable St Mark’s Church, the Museum of Broken Relationships, Maksimir Park, Lake Jarun (Zagreb’s unofficial “sea”), and the open-air Dolac Market are all within very easy reach. In the evenings, the bar and restaurant scene is lively without being overwhelming. Weekends open the door to day trips – Plitvice Lakes, the hills around Samobor, or a quick train to Ljubljana – without the stress of long-haul logistics.

Cost of living remains noticeably lower than in most Western European capitals, so a three-month stay feels financially sustainable rather than extravagant.

you don’t need to be a digital nomad to… be a digital nomad

Croatia’s official digital nomad temporary stay is designed for longer periods (up to 18 months) and requires proof of remote work for a non-Croatian entity, health insurance, a clean criminal record, and a minimum income currently set at 2.5 times the average net salary – currently over €3,600 per month, or the equivalent in savings. Processing takes time and the paperwork is real.

The 90-day Schengen short stay, by contrast, asks far less of you if your nationality qualifies for visa-free entry. You arrive, register your accommodation as required, work remotely for your existing foreign employer or clients, and leave before the 90 days are up (or before you hit the 183-day tax-residency threshold if that matters to you). No special permit, no income threshold tied to Croatian averages, no multi-week application process. It is simply a long, productive city break with a laptop. Of course the usual rules apply: you cannot take local employment, and the days count toward your overall Schengen allowance. But for many remote professionals testing life in Croatia, or simply wanting a change of scenery without administrative drama and a baptism of fire from the Croatian bureaucratic machine, that is precisely the point.

who could this work best for?

This approach suits a whole cohort of people; those who already work remotely for a company or clients outside Croatia and hold a passport that allows 90 days visa-free in the Schengen zone, those who want a proper base rather than a series of hotel stays and those prefer a walkable, cafe-packed European city with four seasons and good transport links, and those who are curious about Croatia but not yet ready to commit to the full digital nomad process. It also works well as a trial run. Spend 60–90 days in Zagreb, get a feel for the rhythm, the food, the community and the climate, then decide whether a longer digital nomad stay or a return trip next year makes sense for you.

no visas, no paperwork, and full freedom

Book a furnished apartment or serviced flat with reliable internet rather than a short-term tourist rental if you can. Join a coworking space for at least a few days a week to meet people. Use the city’s excellent public transport and the green spaces to keep the work–life balance healthy. And treat the weekends as genuine exploration time – Zagreb rewards slow discovery more than checklist tourism.

In short, you do not need a special visa to work remotely from Croatia for three months. You just need a laptop, a passport that opens the Schengen door, and a city that actually works for everyday life. Zagreb quietly delivers on all three. For practical information on accommodation, events and getting around, the Zagreb Tourist Board is a good starting point. The rest is simply showing up and getting to work – and leisure.

World.title: Končar Showcases Croatian Manufacturing to the World in Berlin
World.content:
September the 25th, 2026 – Končar has showcased Croatian manufacturing to the world in Berlin, taking the most prominent positions at this year’s InnoTrans.

Končar’s striking visuals were visible in the most prominent positions right at the entrance to the space of the prestigious fair, and the scene at the very entrance to the exhibition area was spectacular, where Končar’s train, a top product of Croatian industry, was positioned in a more prominent place than giants such as Alstom and Stadler. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that after it was put into regular service on the Zagreb – Split route a week earlier in cooperation with the customer HŽ Passenger Transport, the second train from this series has now also been presented to the international public. With the global premiere of its latest solution for more modern, more comfortable and more sustainable passenger transport, Končar has once again confirmed that the knowledge, competences and technological solutions developed in Croatia compete on equal terms with the biggest names in the European railway industry.

croatia impresses visitors from around the world

The InnoTrans fair in Berlin once again brought together the world’s leading manufacturers, carriers, operators and experts from the fields of transport technology, railways, public transport and sustainable mobility. Among the most visited parts of the fair was the outdoor exhibition area with 3,500 metres of track, on which 130 exhibitors from 17 countries of the world exhibited a total of 113 vehicles, including the latest generations of trains, locomotives and vehicles with alternative propulsion systems. Precisely in such an international environment Končar is presenting technological solutions developed and produced in Croatia for the jubilee 10th time, confirming its position among the relevant European manufacturers of modern rail vehicles and advanced solutions for sustainable urban mobility.

berlin breaks records

All 42 exhibition halls in the Berlin Messe complex, with a total exhibition area of around 200 thousand square metres, are completely full. After two years ago it was the only one at InnoTrans to present a battery train, which then also became the first such product in commercial use in Europe and one of the first such products in the whole world, Končar has also displayed its new bimodal electro-diesel train at one of the most attractive positions on the outdoor exhibition area of the fair – on 75-metre-long tracks.

At the same time, the latest solutions for railway infrastructure, electrification, urban mobility and traffic digitalisation were presented on the spacious indoor area, further emphasising the ability of the domestic company to independently develop and deliver integrated technological solutions for the transport systems of the future.

“The presentation of our latest bimodal train at InnoTrans is confirmation that Končar today stands side by side with the leading European manufacturers of railway vehicles. It is a product of a new generation that confirms the strength of domestic knowledge, innovation and industrial competences and Končar’s ability to respond to the requirements of modern and sustainable railway transport. We believe that precisely with such projects we contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of the Croatian economy and positioning Croatia among the countries that actively participate in shaping the future of sustainable mobility in Europe,” emphasised Končar Management Board President Gordan Kolak.

One train, two sources of propulsion and no compromises – precisely this idea guided the development of the new Končar bimodal electro-diesel train that combines the advantages of electric and diesel traction and enables uninterrupted traffic on electrified and non-electrified sections of the railway network. Additional operational adaptability is provided by the possibility of controlling up to three coupled units from one driver’s cab, whereby the capacity of the train can be adapted to the actual transport needs. Accordingly, it is an innovation that represents a direct response to the need for more sustainable and more efficient railway transport on long routes that encompass both types of infrastructure, and is the result of many years of experience and independent development at Končar – Electric Vehicles.

With its presentation Končar rounds off a unique development portfolio of trains and, after electric, diesel-electric and battery trains, is introducing the fourth propulsion platform developed and produced in Croatia to the market. The new train is also one of the best references of the long and successful application of Croatian products in domestic railway transport. Namely, the model from the new generation that was put into service last week represents a total of the 70th train that Končar has delivered to HŽ Passenger Transport, which further confirms the joint orientation towards the modernisation of the domestic railway system.

a new era

“The new train for long-distance transport combines the development, design and production competences of the Končar Group. Thanks to the bimodal propulsion system it ensures a high level of reliability and quality of service on the entire network, while bringing passengers a higher standard of comfort through first class, a catering zone and full accessibility for persons with reduced mobility. It is a technologically advanced and operationally flexible solution that meets the requirements of modern railway transport and the long-term needs of sustainable mobility,” emphasised Josip Ninić, President of the Management Board of Končar – Electric Vehicles.

By developing advanced rail vehicles, digital platforms and integrated solutions for critical infrastructure, including railway and transport systems, Končar is increasingly entering a new era of electroenergetics and urban mobility and occupying the position of a serious European partner for the implementation of complex projects. In this way it not only confirms the technological strength of Croatian industry, but also actively contributes to positioning Croatia as a relevant participant in the European green and digital transition and one of the centres of development of the technologically most complex solutions in this part of Europe.

This year InnoTrans is celebrating its 30th anniversary – and, quite fittingly, the fair is recording new record figures. For the first time more than 3,170 exhibitors will participate, which is around 200 more than in 2024, which was also a record year. All 42 exhibition halls in the Berlin Messe complex, with a total exhibition area of around 200 thousand square metres, are completely full. The same applies to the outdoor exhibition area of InnoTrans of 20 thousand square metres, where this year 113 vehicles from 17 countries will be exhibited.

Of the approximately 130 exhibitors presenting themselves on the outdoor area, around 30 of them are participating in that segment for the first time. Therefore the event has great prospects of surpassing the record attendance of around 170 thousand visitors from 2024. That is a huge advance compared to the modest beginnings of what is today the world’s leading railway transport fair.

World.title: Exotic Indian Bananas Successfully Being Grown in Međimurje
World.content:
September the 25th, 2026 – Exotic Indian bananas are successfully being grown in Međimurje, seeing seeds turn into three thousand seedlings.

In the municipality of Štrigova, an area in the north of Međimurje known primarily for its vineyards, one of the largest plantations of Indian bananas in this part of Europe was planted a few years ago. Index reports that behind the project is the family of Ivan Žižek, who decided to grow this unusual fruit after learning that it tolerates low temperatures well and is not attacked by diseases, HRT reports.

3,000 seedlings

The Žižek family planted a plantation of Indian banana, also known as pawpaw (asimina), in the village of Banfi three years ago. Since the seedlings are expensive and they needed more than three thousand of them, they opted for a cheaper but slower route. “We obtained a larger quantity of fruit from Italy, manually extracted the seeds, processed them and put them to germinate. Luckily, everything germinated excellently so we grew the first rootstocks of asimina that way. After that I personally started grafting them,” Ivan explains.

The trees are not yet in full yield so for now the family is selling only fresh fruit. In a year or two they plan to start production of food and cosmetic products from that fruit. “A tree in full yield can give around 20 kilograms. We plan to place 20 to 30 percent on the market through retail chains, and the rest would go into the food industry – for craft breweries, jams, liqueurs and aromatic wines,” says Roman Mraz.

hail reduced the yield

This year’s plantation was also quite damaged by strong hail that hit the area in June. “Still, with some earlier varieties we noticed that the first fruit we tasted was of good quality and tasty inside,” Ivan emphasises.

The Indian banana plantation is not the only example of growing exotic crops in that area. Namely, next to the edge of the plantation of fruit that originates from North America, the Žižek family is also growing 16 pistachio trees, whose original homeland is the Middle East, and 65 feijoa bushes, a fruit species from South America.

World.title: Iraq targets first Gulf Cup win against Kuwait
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq will take on Kuwait on Saturday, looking for their first victory in the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup, after drawing 1-1 with Oman in Jeddah.

The Group A match will take place at Prince Abdullah Al Faisal Stadium in Baghdad at 6:55 p.m. local time, with Iraq starting the second round with one point and Kuwait aiming to rebound from a 1-0 loss to Saudi Arabia.

Iraq started quickly against Oman on Wednesday, with Mohammed Qasim scoring in the sixth minute with a strong left-footed finish.

Oman answered in the second half with Nasser Al-Rawahi, who equalized in the 67th minute to give both sides a draw.

News from Iraq’s Coach Graham Arnold said that preparations for the first match had been restricted, with his group having little time together before playing an Oman team that had been in camp for many days.

Arnold mentioned that Iraq’s players are physically, tactically, and emotionally ready for Kuwait. Arnold may make changes to his team for the match against Kuwait due to exhaustion and the hot weather in Saudi Arabia.

Half of Iraq’s Gulf Cup roster had competed in the 2026 World Cup, with the remaining being younger players given a chance with the national team.

Arnold said that Mustafa Saadoun and Mohammed Qasim are available for the match, while defender Akam Hashim’s fitness is being examined.

Saturday’s encounter is crucial after Iraq’s two-point loss to Oman. Saudi Arabia leads Group A with three points, Iraq and Oman have one apiece, while Kuwait has no points after the first round.

The top two teams advanced to the semifinals.

Iraq’s last group encounter is against Saudi Arabia on September 29, making it crucial to win against Kuwait before facing the current group leaders.

World.title: Iraqi PM calls on US firms to seize investment opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on US companies on Wednesday to seize investment opportunities available in Iraq, particularly in the petrochemicals, glass, and phosphate industries, as well as the gas and clean energy sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting in New York with a delegation from the US Chamber of Commerce, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister stated that Iraq has considerable natural resources, human resources, and a key geographical position, all of which serve as necessary foundations for successful partnerships. He explained that the government is seeking to use these resources to promote economic development and increase investment possibilities.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the government’s commitment to providing support for businesses and investors, such as granting ownership of land for investment projects in accordance with Iraqi laws, as well as access to tax and customs exemptions for up to ten years.

Iraq is working on infrastructure and transportation projects, notably the strategic project of the Development Road, which will improve Iraq’s position as a corridor connecting the East and West, according to al-Zaidi.

The prime minister affirmed that the government looks forward to establishing factories and setting up projects to diversify the economy and create job opportunities.

Al-Zaidi also asked members of the US Chamber of Commerce and specialized firms to attend the Baghdad Energy Conference and capitalize on the prospects offered in the country. He added that Iraq aspires to establish economic partnerships based on collaboration, mutual interest, and long-term investment.

World.title: Iraqi PM, US president discuss partnerships, regional stability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in New York on Tuesday on the sideline of his participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The two leaders discussed bilateral relations and approaches to strengthen cooperation and partnership between the two countries across political, economic, and investment sectors, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two sides also reviewed the latest developments in the region, as well as the joint efforts undertaken by Iraq and the United States to enhance regional and international security and stability.

The discussion takes place ahead of a crucial September 30 milestone, which marks a shift in Washington-Baghdad ties toward long-term economic collaboration as the US prepares to end its coalition military mission in Iraq.

Amid continuing negotiations between Iraq and US officials, including a recent meeting between al-Zaidi and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Washington pressured Baghdad on its obligations to place weapons possessed by armed factions under state supervision.

In addition to their exclusive bilateral discussion, al-Zaidi attended President Trump’s larger gathering that included leaders from important regional powers, including Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, Egypt, and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nations.

The larger gathering addressed strategies to coordinate post-war arrangements, protect global commerce supply lines, and develop diplomatic frameworks for Middle Eastern stability.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Iranian president in New York
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Wednesday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New York on the sidelines of their participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the meeting addressed developments in the region and the necessity of working together to handle difficulties in ways that promote security and stability.

The two leaders also addressed approaches to keep the region from spiraling into a cycle of escalation, tensions, and crises.

During a meeting on Wednesday with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein emphasized the importance of defusing regional tensions through dialogue.

The meeting addressed bilateral relations and regional developments, as well as the importance of continued coordination between the two countries to respond to current challenges and support diplomatic efforts aimed at enhancing regional stability.

Hussein also stressed the significance of continued diplomatic efforts among the parties involved to defuse tension and prevent escalation.

Araghchi outlined the discussions that began between Iran and the United States, sponsored by an intermediary, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meetings in New York. These discussions attempt to de-escalate the situation and find approaches to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for navigation.

The two ministers also discussed the outcomes of the meeting involving the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, and Turkey—attended by US President Donald Trump—as well as how regional and international relationships might help efforts for de-escalation.

World.title: Iraq’s Gulf Cup 27 match against Oman ends in 1-1 draw
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi and Omani national teams drew 1-1 on Wednesday in the opening match of the 27th Gulf Cup held at Prince Abdullah Al-Faisal Sports City Stadium in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Iraq launched a strong attack, causing Oman to make a defensive mistake. Zaid Ismail took advantage of the rebound and set it up for Mohammed Qasim, who fired a rocket shot with his left foot into the near corner, giving the “Lions of Mesopotamia” an early lead in the sixth minute.

The Omani team’s performance improved, and their level rose during the second half. After a decisive and skillful pass from Ahmed al-Kaabi, Nasser al-Rawahi scored the equalizer brilliantly from a close range, winning the “Man of the Match” award in recognition of his outstanding performance.

In a candid evaluation, Australian coach Graham Arnold, who manages the Iraqi national team, acknowledged that the team’s performance fell short of expectations. He pointed out that the rushed preparations had hindered the implementation of their tactical plan.

The Iraqi team only had one training session before the tournament compared to six for the Omani team.

“We were not the better side, and we must work harder in the coming matches to secure the win,” Arnold said.

The manager of the Oman team, Tarik Sektioui, expressed his great pride in his team, describing the squad as “fighters” for their ability to recover from an early setback and snatch a vital opening point against the defending champions.

World.title: Turkey to hand over military base to enhance Iraqi sovereignty
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced on Wednesday that Turkish forces will gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zelikan base to the Iraqi government.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the handover process will take place in accordance with an agreed-upon mechanism and timeline amid the progress Iraq has achieved through security measures.

During their meeting on the sideline of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, the two leaders agreed to deepen security cooperation in negotiations in which Iraqi and Turkish authorities discussed strategic relations.

Additionally, al-Zaidi and Erdogan agreed to completely expand the Iraqi state’s authority in Sinjar and to eliminate the presence of banned foreign armed groups.

Turkey established a military base in Bashiqa, near Mosul, in December 2015, initially deploying around 600 soldiers to train local forces to combat ISIS terrorist groups.

The deployment of Turkish soldiers without formal consent from Iraq has been a longstanding point of contention, often regarded as a violation of Iraq’s sovereignty and a strain on the relationship between Ankara and Baghdad.

As part of the agreement, Iraq agreed to restore state authority in Sinjar and remove or disarm foreign armed groups and militias that Turkey sees as security risks.

World.title: Iraq to raise gas production at Nahr Bin Umar to 300 million cubic feet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil revealed on Monday that it is planning to increase associated gas recovery at the Nahr Bin Umar field to 300 million cubic feet per day.

Deputy Minister for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber chaired a meeting to review associated gas recovery plans and projects at the Nahr Bin Umar field in the southern province of Basra.

The meeting was attended by representatives from the South Gas Company (SGC) and the project operator, Halfaya Gas Company, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The meeting focused on the development plan to enhance associated gas recovery, aiming for a target of 300 million standard cubic feet per day.

The plan will be implemented in two phases, each with a capacity of 150 million standard cubic feet per day.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil said earlier that the Bin Umar gas project will produce between 500 and 600 tons of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Saber mentioned earlier that the project, which will minimize gas flaring and support the country’s electricity grid, is planned to be operational by the end of April.

Saber confirmed the news while inspecting the project’s final connection point in mid-April.

The project will produce 70 million standard cubic feet per day of raw gas, between 500 and 600 tons of LPG for home consumption, around 80 million standard cubic feet per day of dry gas for power plants, and more than 1,800 barrels per day of condensates.

The initiative is an important step toward increasing gas utilization, preventing gas flaring, and strengthening the country’s electricity grid.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 3 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Tuesday that oil exports for August reached approximately 70 million barrels, with daily shipments exceeding three million barrels.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the deals the ministry reached to transport oil through the Turkish port of Ceyhan raised the volumes to 600,000 barrels per day, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Iraq’s oil exports fluctuated during September 2026, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions related to the Middle East war and Baghdad’s efforts to diversify its export routes.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that exports started at three million barrels per day at the beginning of September but have since gradually declined to about 2.4 million barrels per day at present.

Despite a decline in Iraqi oil exports during September, the figures still surpassed the average daily exports in August, which were approximately 2.35 million barrels per day. This increase was bolstered by enhanced shipping traffic and a decrease in shipping disruptions in the Gulf over the past few weeks.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

The prime minister indicated that it is important to improve infrastructure and export capacity to meet the expected rise in output.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Al-Zaidi directed an increase in output from oil fields in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the expansion of exploration activities to achieve the plan’s objectives and reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

NEW DELHI: EC, which is reeling under allegations of faultlines among its members, is now being questioned over a software update recently made in the application used by booth level officers, with its description on the Apple app store reading "mark VIP elector-related changes".EC sources told TOI Friday the instruction to BLOs on "flagging of marked electors" was a standard instruction, which was part of all three special intensive revision orders approved by the commission.The instruction to field officers to "mark" prominent electors in their jurisdictional areas has figured in EC's instructions for all special summary revisions, well before SIR was conceived, they said. For instance, Para 20 of the SSR exercise ordered by EC on May 29, 2023, with Jan 1, 2024, as the qualifying date, directed the "flagging of marked electors, viz MP/MLA/MLC, holders of declared offices and personalities from fields of arts, culture, journalism, sports, members of judiciary and public services, etc". Para 21 said the electoral registration officers were to ensure that the names were in the proposed draft roll.The same instruction was reiterated in the SIR order for Bihar dated June 24, 2025, and the orders for SIR Phase 2 and 3.Nowhere in the SIR or SSR instructions has the terminology 'VIP' been used. "It somehow made it to the app description," an officer said. EC officials said the BLO app software update was meant to help such prominent persons "marked" in the electoral database by flagging any notices served and enabling the proof furnished by them to be uploaded on the app without delay.Meanwhile, EC sources said the postponement of the electoral literacy club conferences in UP had nothing to do with the row and the decision was made on Sept 21.On reports alleging annual confidential reports were held up due to differences between commission members, EC officials said such delays were not unusual. TOI has further learnt there have been few full commission meetings in the past few months.

World.title: Lawyers move SC, AG for action on poll panel chief
World.content:
As questions are being raised against CEC Gyanesh Kumar for allegedly unilaterally taking many decisions pertaining to the SIR drive, a

lawyer has filed a petition in court seeking his criminal prosecution, and another has approached the attorney general, seeking his permission, as required under the law, to file a contempt petition against him.

The petition filed in SC said action needed to be taken against the chief election commissioner for his "unilateral, unauthorised, and illegal decisions" taken in the name of EC. It referred to Section 18 of Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, and the law laid down by a constitution bench in the TN Seshan case in 1995 to say EC's decisions mandatorily had to be taken by the majority.

EC has maintained that all the decisions regarding special intensive revision of electoral rolls were taken unanimously by Kumar and his two colleagues, election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

The petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, echoing claims made in a news report, sought quashing of unauthorised modifications made to Form 6 on ECINet/ERONet portals requiring ancestry/last-SIR declarations, and also sought immediate restoration of the statutory Form 6 as prescribed under Registration of Electors Rules to permit all eligible adults to register as voters on the basis of original statutory requirements.





Mentioning the alleged illegal acts of CEC, the petition said, "Introducing a mandatory ancestral condition (last SIR linkage) for first-time young voters without legislative authority or amendment of Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, was explicitly branded as unauthorised and illegal by a majority of the commission."

The petition said depriving decentralised electoral registration officers of their statutory authority under sections 13B, 22 and 23 of Representation of the People Act, 1950, and centralising electoral roll management under the director general of IT in Delhi was another wrong.

"Tampering with the electoral roll constitutes a cognisable offence under Section 32 of RP Act, 1950, as well as provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita concerning falsification of records and public servants disobeying directions of law. In such a scenario, divested of any statutory or constitutional immunity, CEC remains directly accountable under the law - subject to police investigation, evidence gathering, and regular trial proceedings as an ordinary accused," the petition said, adding CEC could not claim immunity for illegal acts.

It said CEC's act of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bore no "reasonable nexus" or legal connection to his official duties and fell squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constituted distinct, personal criminal liability.

Another apex court advocate, Shiv Kumar Tripathi, wrote to the attorney general, bringing to his notice the "constitutional misconduct and contempt of court" by CEC and sought his approval to file a contempt case against him.

"SC has repeatedly emphasised EC's independence, impartiality and institutional integrity. CEC's office is one of constitutional primacy, but it is not intended to function as an authority overriding the equal constitutional status of other election commissioners in collective decision-making. Any departure from this constitutional framework may undermine public confidence in free and fair election," Tripathi said in his letter.

World.title: Blend social reforms with political work: PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister

Friday asked

members to draw inspiration from

to blend social reforms with their political work instead of focusing on vote bank politics.

"When we look at Mahatma Gandhi's life, we see he fought against the British and led the freedom movement.

But he was also a great social reformer. He always worked against social evils.

We as political workers too should not merely focus on vote-bank politics and allow things to continue as they are. We must continue working for social reforms," he said.

He was interacting virtually with participants of "Seva Yatra", a motorcyle rally from Varanasi to Vadnagar organised by BJP to mark his 76th birthday and his continuous stint of 25 years as head of govt.

Modi drew from his own experience as a frequent traveller across the length and breadth of India and said it has deeply enriched his life and values. "The message of service should be spread not merely by our words but action," he said, highlighting the felicitation of sanitation workers and other service-oriented programmes to make his point. Serving people is serving the country, he said, adding that BJP ideologue Deen Dayal Upadhyay, whose birth anniversary fell on Friday, put serving people at the core of his ideology.

He praised those who carried out the cleanliness work in Prayagraj, noting that their efforts made the 'Kumbh Mela' famous worldwide for sanitation and elevated India's honour.

"So, I felt compelled to wash the feet of those who have enhanced India's honour so much, to seek their blessings," he said.

Modi also said over the past 12 years, the gap between cities and villages in India has significantly narrowed and infrastructure in villages has improved to a great extent. He said self-reliance among women has also increased in the country.

World.title: Amazon, Flipkart & JioMart fined for illegal herbicide sale
World.content:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product.Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed for preventing and eliminating weeds.CCPA directed the e-commerce marketplaces to discontinue false s and conduct self-audits to identify products that violate the law or pose a risk to life and safety.Proceedings began after the department of agriculture and farmers' welfare forwarded a complaint from Crop Care Federation of India. The department said insecticides and pesticides are regulated under Insecticides Act, 1968, and Insecticides Rules. It said no chemical named Cyclosinone was listed in the Act's Schedule, and the product did not disclose its composition.CCPA rejected the companies' argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers.

World.title: Kochi is changing the way it dates, talks about sex and relationships
World.content:
There is something amusing about the fact that a city famous for Chinese fishing nets, churches, synagogues and the occasional wholesome family lunch is also becoming a surprisingly interesting place to talk about sex.

In Kochi, the conversation is increasingly moving beyond the old binary of sex as either something that happens after marriage or something that happens in whispers. Dating apps have given young Malayalis a new vocabulary for meeting people; words such as “breadcrumbing”, “ghosting” and “situationship” have entered the local lexicon, while platforms built specifically around Malayali identity are offering an alternative to the generic swipe.

World.title: Jaishankar meets Iranian, Russian Foreign Ministers on UNGA margins
World.content:
India held discussions with Russia and Iran on the margins of the high-level UN General Assembly session, days after U.S. President Donald Trump signed a new law on sanctions on countries purchasing oil and gas from Moscow and Tehran.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met his counterparts from Iran and Russia, with discussions ranging from bilateral issues, cooperation in the BRICS grouping and the Gulf conflict.

Mr. Jaishankar met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and discussed bilateral issues as well as cooperation in the BRICS grouping.

“A good meeting with FM Sergey Lavrov of Russia today #UNGA81. Exchanged views on a number of ongoing issues. Also took stock of our bilateral and BRICS cooperation,” Jaishankar said, referring to the grouping of Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates.

India had earlier this month hosted the BRICS Leaders’ Summit that was attended by Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

A readout of the one-on-one meeting between Mr. Jaishankar and Mr. Lavrov provided by the Russian Foreign Affairs Ministry said that the two leaders discussed "key issues of Russian-Indian cooperation, the schedule of upcoming bilateral contacts, and current regional and global issues, including the Ukraine crisis and the situation in the Middle East”.

They expressed their intention to continue efforts to strengthen the “special and privileged strategic partnership” and to maintain close coordination at the UN, in the G20, BRICS, and other international groupings.

Mr. Jaishankar also met Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on the margins of the high-level UNGA session in New York Friday.

“Appreciate the conversation with FM @araghchi of Iran at the @UN #UNGA81. We discussed the latest developments with regard to the Gulf conflict. Will continue to be in touch,” he said.

Last week, Mr. Trump signed the ‘Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026’, which authorises and expands statutory sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran.

India has said it remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people, and it will continue to do so through diversified sourcing, in response to the US’ Russia sanctions legislation.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act authorises Mr. Trump to impose sanctions on Russia and steep tariffs on its trading partners such as India and China in the oil and gas sector.

Continuing another busy day of engagements at the UN, Mr. Jaishankar co-chaired the India-Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Troika Ministerial Meeting in New York on the margins of the UNGA.

He reviewed the progress of the India-GCC Joint Action Plan 2024–28 and discussed ways to further advance the partnership.

India welcomed the launch of India-GCC free trade agreement negotiations. “Look forward to strengthening ties in the areas of trade, investment, energy, food security, health, new technologies, culture and people-to-people exchanges. Thanked GCC leaderships for the support extended to the Indian community.”

India also reiterated its strong commitment to freedom of navigation and safety of seafarers and commercial shipping.

Mr. Jaishankar co-chaired an event ‘AI in the Context of International Peace & Security, with an Emphasis on Maritime Security’, alongside Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis.

In a post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said he emphasised the need to harness the possibilities offered by AI, anticipate its consequences and mitigate its risks.

“This calls for an approach that enables innovation while remaining conscious of its security implications,” he said. He shared that the New Delhi Declaration emphasises democratic access to AI resources, building secure and trustworthy systems, investing in human capabilities and harnessing AI for economic growth and social good.

In the maritime domain, AI can enhance maritime domain awareness, search and rescue, disaster response, identification of suspicious activity and resilience of ports and critical infrastructure, he said.

At the same time, it can enable sophisticated reconnaissance, vulnerability mapping and cyber operations targeting vessels, communication networks and undersea infrastructure, he added.

Mr. Jaishankar underlined that increasing autonomy in maritime systems raises questions of attribution, accountability and escalation, while also compressing decision-making time.

He pointed out that in the maritime domain, the UN Charter and international law, including the law of the sea, remain essential frameworks governing State conduct.

“Greater transparency, confidence-building, capacity development, technical cooperation and exchange of best practices are essential to ensure that AI is developed and used consistent with these principles,” he said.

World.title: Chhattisgarh government declares school holiday amid heavy rain, flood-like situation
World.content:
The Chhattisgarh government has declared a holiday for schools across the State on Saturday (September 26, 2026), as heavy rain battered parts of the State, inundating several areas and cutting off villages.

Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai, in a post on X on Friday (September 25, 2026), announced the closure of all government, private and aided schools, saying the safety of students was the top priority.

छत्तीसगढ़ में हो रही भारी बारिश को देखते हुए छात्रों की सुरक्षा सर्वोपरि रखते हुए कल (26 सितंबर) को सभी शासकीय, अशासकीय एवं अनुदान प्राप्त स्कूलों में अवकाश घोषित किया गया है।



अभिभावक बच्चों को घर पर ही रखें। सभी से अनुरोध है कि सतर्क रहें और अनावश्यक यात्रा से बचें। — Vishnu Deo Sai (@vishnudsai) September 25, 2026

Mr. Sai said heavy rainfall could lead to waterlogging, rising water levels in rivers and streams, and transportation difficulties in several areas, and that the decision was taken to ensure children faced no risk.

He also instructed District Collectors to conduct relief and rescue operations with full vigilance in view of flooding and waterlogging caused by continuous rainfall, including in the Bastar division, which comprises seven districts, another statement said.

"There should be no delay in providing assistance to people in need in affected areas. Keeping the safety of citizens as the highest priority, the administration should remain prepared to deal with every situation," the release quoted Mr. Sai as saying.

He directed officials to monitor the situation, with special attention to villages and settlements in low-lying areas and those near rivers and streams.

Incessant heavy rain battered several parts of the State on Friday (September 25, 2026), inundating low-lying areas, swelling rivers and cutting off remote settlements in the Bastar region.

Mr. Sai asked relief and rescue teams to remain ready with the necessary resources, and directed district administrations, the police, urban local bodies, panchayats and other departments to work in coordination so that immediate assistance is provided in any emergency.

He also directed officials to ensure safe shelters, food, drinking water, medicines and other essential facilities as required, and asked people not to venture unnecessarily into waterlogged areas or swollen rivers and streams, and to follow the district administration's advisories.

A rain-related death was reported in Kondagaon district, where a farmer, 40, drowned on Friday (September 25, 2026) after falling into a flooded drain while trying to catch fish in a partially submerged paddy field, officials said.

Between June 1, 2026, and September 25, 2026, the State recorded an average of 1,082.4 mm of rainfall, which is 100.1% of its 10-year seasonal benchmark of 1,081.5 mm. Over the past 24 hours alone, the State received an average of 52.8 mm of rain.

Balrampur recorded the highest rainfall relative to its seasonal average, at 169.4% (1,527.7 mm), while Narayanpur recorded the highest cumulative rainfall, at 1,600.4 mm.

Some districts, however, received below-normal rainfall: Surguja recorded 606.6 mm (75.5%), Jashpur 828.7 mm (79.7%), Kabirdham 672 mm (82.2%), Bemetara 597.1 mm (74.5%) and Kanker 1,110.7 mm (75.9%). Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki recorded 74.7% and Bijapur 78.7% of normal rainfall. Rainfall in Bastar, Dantewada, Bijapur, Sukma, Korba, Janjgir-Champa, Durg and Rajnandgaon was close to normal.

World.title: U.S. looking to become huge source of India’s energy needs: Senior State Department official
World.content:
India, with massive energy needs, has for a long time been exploring ways to diversify its energy sources, and the U.S. is looking to meet those demands, a senior State Department official has said.

Last week, U.S. President Donald Trump signed into law the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026', which authorises him to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil and gas, including China and India.

The law is named after late Senator Lindsey Graham, who had proposed a sanctions bill imposing 500% tariffs on countries for buying Russian oil.

Responding to a question on the bill and India’s response about “potential implications" for the bilateral relationship, the official said that the U.S. Congress took a pretty hard approach, especially publicly.

“India has been looking for a long time to diversify its energy sources. They're a country that has massive energy needs,” the official said.

“You had members of Congress calling out India in particular, so of course India has to respond. We understand that. They have a domestic constituency, as do we. Like, there is no sort of hard feelings on any of that kind of activity.”

In response to a question by PTI on the bill and India’s concerns over it, the official said the U.S. Congress passed a bill that gave President Trump a new tool in his toolbox.

“That doesn't necessarily mean he deploys it tomorrow, but he has the opportunity to. His focus is on ending this war. It's been something he campaigned on and something he's been dedicated to from the beginning,” he said.

“We're looking for our friends, especially like India, to help support that effort. But I think you'll have to stay tuned on how the bill gets implemented. But there is a broad national security waiver, so you can imagine there's a scenario, and the President uses that as well,” he added.

Noting that “unfortunately” for a long time, Venezuelan and Iranian sources were cut off, “the options were very limited", he said.

"Now, with President Trump's incredibly successful operation in Venezuela, we are moving into a better position that countries like India are going to be able to get access to that market,” he added.

Pointing out that the “Indians are very interested”, the official said the country used to have refineries in Venezuela but it is very complicated to get those back up and running, given the damage the Nicolás Maduro regime did to the industry.

"We are looking to also become a huge source of India's energy needs. We're increasing our hydrocarbon exports,” the official said adding that the U.S. is now the largest exporter of LPG, and second for LNG.

“The demands are great, and the needs for oil are there. We are looking for alternatives,” the official said, adding that these are conversations that happen frequently, including between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Secretary Marco Rubio, and they will continue.

“But I would say even before the war, India had been looking to diversify when it came to energy for a long time. It's not a new concept. We just need to expedite it faster,” the senior State Department official said.

World.title: Dhiraj sets Asian Games record, tops recurve qualification; India finish second in team events
World.content:
Fresh from his World Cup Final triumph, Dhiraj Bommadevara made a strong start to his Asian Games campaign, smashing the men's recurve qualification record with 698 points to top the standings Okazaki City on Saturday (September 26, 2026).

Asian Games 2026 LIVE

Dhiraj, currently ranked fourth in the world, produced a superb second half to move clear at the top. He shot 348 in his first 36 arrows and then dropped just 10 points in the final 36, adding 350 to finish on 698 out of a possible 720.

His score bettered the previous Asian Games qualification record of 690 by Korean Lee Woo Seok, who slipped to fourth position with 687 points.

Korea's rising star Kim Je Deok, a member of the Paris Olympics gold-medal winning team, finished second with 693, while Chinese Taipei's Chin-Hun Tang was third with 692.

The top finish earned Dhiraj a bye into the second round of the 64-archer individual elimination draw.

Seok, the Paris Olympics bronze medallist, could be a potential semifinal opponent if both archers progress that far.

Dhiraj holds a 2-1 head-to-head record against the Korean, who is ranked 19th in the world.

The 25-year-old Army archer will be looking to go all the way after his quarterfinal exit at the Hangzhou Asian Games.

India have never won an Asian Games gold in the men's recurve individual event, with Tarundeep Rai's silver in 2010 remaining the country's best finish.

There was a major surprise in the Korean camp as legendary archer Kim Woojin failed to make the individual elimination round.

Woojin, who was eyeing a third Asian Games gold, finished third among the Korean archers and missed the cut as only the top two from each country qualify for the 64-player elimination draw.

India's other two recurve archers, Neeraj Chauhan and Yashdeep Bhoge, finished 18th and 25th respectively with scores of 676 and 665 as the latter missed out on the knockout.

India finished second in the men's team qualification behind Korea.

As the second seed in the 32-team draw, India received a bye into the pre-quarterfinals, where they will face the Philippines. The team will need three wins to secure a medal.

India had won a men's team silver in Hangzhou.

In the women's compound section, 21-year-old Chikitha Taniparthi gave India a major boost by topping the individual qualification with 705 points from a maximum 720.

Chikitha's performance comes as India look to continue their dominance in the compound events, having swept all five gold medals at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023, besides winning one silver and one bronze.

Iran's Bita Asheghzadeh Oskouei finished a close second with 704 points, while Korea's Park Jungyoon and Kang Yeonseo took the third and fourth spots.

Triple Asian Games gold medallist Jyothi Surekha Vennam was the second-best Indian, finishing 13th in the qualification standings to make the cut for elimination.

Teenager Prithika Pradeep, who bagged a maiden World Cup bronze in Madrid this year, however missed out on an individual berth.

She scored 695 to finish third among the Indian archers, with only the top two from each country advancing.

India nevertheless secured the second seed in the women's compound team event behind China.

They will begin their campaign against Mongolia in the 16-team draw.

The women's recurve and men's compound qualifications will get underway in the second half.

World.title: Congress accuses CEC of law violation over Form 6 changes, urges Supreme Court to hold him accountable
World.content:
The Congress on Saturday (September 26, 2026) accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of knowingly breaking the law and Constitutional practices by "unilaterally" changing Form 6 and called on the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance and hold him accountable.

In a post on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Mr. Kumar's continued tenure is an affront to the people of India and that he must resign, as suggested by Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi.

Mr. Ramesh stated that late at night on Friday (September 25, 2026), a "panicked" Election Commission directed officers to organise special enrolment camps for young voters and give them "wide publicity" through social media.

"But the CEC himself had earlier made it virtually impossible to add young voters through a blatantly illegal and unconstitutional change to Form 6. A new mandatory section was added that asks if your parents/grandparents were in the previous SIR, creating a barrier for first-time Gen Z voters.

"The change is completely illegal. -- Violation 1: In early July 2026, the online form was stealthily changed with no official notification," the Congress leader said.

Pointing out the second violation, he said the ECI does not have the power to amend Form 6. "This power is only held by the Union Government as per the Representation Of The People Act, 1950. This is clearly a huge overreach by the Election Commission," Mr. Ramesh said.

"Violation 3: The form was changed without any amendment to the Rules that govern it under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. That can only be done by the Union Government with proper intimation to Parliament. A statutory form, defined by the law, was unilaterally changed by the CEC Gyanesh at the instance of the rattled PM-HM duo," he added.

Mr. Ramesh claimed that, incidentally, the two election commissioners had called for this "illegal and unauthorised" change to be reversed "so young and first-time voters can register without any harassment".

"The CEC has broken not just Constitutional conventions and practices but has also knowingly broken the law as passed by Parliament. His continuation in office is an affront to the people of India.

"A confirmed law-breaker in charge of implementing laws -- what has Indian democracy degenerated into. The Supreme Court must immediately take suo motu cognisance and hold him accountable," the Congress general secretary said.

He asserted that Mr. Kumar can still redeem himself by resigning and turning approver, a suggestion by Rahul Gandhi, adding that the youth will approve this move.

Amid a row over the Election Commission adding a declaration to the form for new voters seeking to enrol in the electoral rolls and making the registration process difficult, poll panel officials said on Friday (September 25, 2026) that as many as 2.37 crore electors in the 18- 28-year age bracket were added since the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise was rolled out in Bihar last June.

After the change in the online form, it's not only the existing voters who must show details of their parents in the SIR to remain on the electoral rolls; those seeking inclusion in the voter list also have to cite details of the exercise.

By issuing instructions, the Election Commission has made it mandatory to attach SIR details of parents for new voters filling Form 6 for inclusion in the electoral rolls.

A poll panel functionary underlined that the declaration was added through instructions and that Form 6 has not been amended.

If a person fills out Form 6 online, he or she cannot proceed further till the declaration is filled.

World.title: ‘What steps are you taking?’: HC questions DU over hostel shortage, flags ‘vague’ reply
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday criticised Delhi University over its response on the issue of adding additional hostel facilities for students as “absolutely vague” while hearing various petitions on the September 6 Satya Niketan multi-storey building collapse in which seven persons, including five students, lost their lives.

The court made stern remarks on the question of building new hostels for students.

A counsel for one of the petitioners pointed out that DU’s affidavit showed that only 5,698 students were being provided hostel accommodation, even as nearly 1.3 lakh students regularly attend classes. The Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia then stated: “You (DU) are only giving figures, as against the students’ strength of more than a lakh, you are giving hostel facilities to a few thousand. And then you say that you are taking steps. What are those steps?”

“From which corner are you not getting cooperation? Tell us,” it added.

The DU counsel said the university would file a “better affidavit”.

During the proceedings, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the civic agency and the Delhi police, shared details of the action taken by the MCD and the police following the collapse.

Multiple inquiries

He said the Delhi government had commissioned a magisterial inquiry to look into the incident, as well as issues such as the validity of permissions, compliance with building by-laws and the role of the concerned officials.

The Delhi government had also constituted a high-powered committee on student accommodation and safety to examine issues relating to student accommodation and safety in Delhi and to recommend appropriate, time-bound measures, Mr. Mehta added.

On the Satya Niketan tragedy, the MCD said the exact cause of the collapse could not be ascertained. It, however, said that the downpour before September 6 “could have weakened” the old structure. The civic agency added that it had carried out a detailed inspection of about 300 properties in the students’ hub and found 101 housing PGs.

PGs vacated

“Of these, three properties were declared dangerous, and the PGs in them were vacated. Ten properties were identified as vulnerable and requiring major repairs, while 14 were found to require minor repairs,” the MCD told the court, which listed the matter for hearing on October 14.
